```pascal
begin
    max:=[A], i:=0,j:=0;
    while [B] do
        begin
        if A[i,j]>max then max:=A[i,j]
        if [C] then j:=j+1
        else begin
            j:=0;
            i:=[D]
        end
    end
end.
```
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Start max at A[0,0]; loop while rows remain (i<n); advance j until the last column (j<n-1), then reset j to 0 and move to row i+1.

questions.text: Consider a singly linked list having n nodes. The data items $d_1,d_2,\dots d_n$ are stored in these n nodes. Let X be a pointer to the j-th node $(1\le j\le n)$ in which $d_j$ is stored. A new data item d stored in node with address Y is t be inserted. Give an algorithm to insert d into the list to obtain a list having items $d_1,d_2,\dots,d_{j-1},d_j,\dots,d_n$ in the order without using the header.
questions.subject: pds
questions.answer: Y->next = X->next; X->next = Y; swap(X->data, Y->data)
questions.solution: Without a pointer to the predecessor, link Y after X and then exchange the data of X and Y so that d ends up before $d_j$ in position j.
questions.reviewNote: Printed target list omits d; the intended order is $d_1,\dots,d_{j-1},d,d_j,\dots,d_n$.

questions.text: An ISAM (indexed sequential) file consists of records of size 64 bytes each, including key field of size 14 bytes. An address of a disk block takes 2 bytes. If the disk block size is 512 bytes and there are 16 K records, compute the size of the data and index areas in terms of number of blocks. How many levels of tree do you have for the index?
questions.subject: db
questions.answer: Data area 2048 blocks; index 64 + 2 + 1 = 67 blocks; 3 levels
questions.solution: 8 records/block gives 16384/8 = 2048 data blocks; index entry = 14+2 = 16 B, 32 per block: 2048/32 = 64 first-level, 64/32 = 2 second-level, 1 root block.

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Each call executes the if-statement n-1 times then recurses on n-1, so $a_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}k=n(n-1)/2$.
questions.reviewNote: The code has no explicit base case; $a_1=0$ assumed.

questions.text: Prove by the principal of mathematical induction that for any binary tree, in which every non-leaf node has 2 descendants, the number of leaves in the tree is one more than the number of non-leaf nodes.
questions.subject: pds
questions.answer: Proof by induction on internal nodes: L = I + 1
questions.solution: Base: a single node has L=1, I=0. Step: replacing a leaf by an internal node with two leaf children increases I by 1 and L by 1, preserving L = I+1.

questions.text: Out of a group of 21 persons, 9 eat vegetables, 10 eat fish and 7 eat eggs : 5 persons eat all three. How many persons eat at least two out the three dishes?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: With x = number eating exactly two dishes and y = exactly one: y + 2x + 3(5) = 9+10+7 = 26, so y + 2x = 11 and the answer x+5 lies between 5 and 10; if all 21 ate something, y + x = 16 would force x = -5, so the data is inconsistent/underdetermined.
questions.reviewNote: Data as printed does not determine a unique answer (and is inconsistent if every person eats at least one dish); left unanswered.

questions.text:
Show that proposition C is a logical consequence of the formula

$$A\wedge(A\to(B\vee C))\wedge(B\to\sim A)$$

Using truth tables.
questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: Formula true only for A=1, B=0, C=1, where C is true
questions.solution: A=1 forces B=0 via $B\to\neg A$, and then $A\to(B\vee C)$ forces C=1; the only satisfying row has C true.

questions.text: A control algorithm is implemented by the NAND - gate circuitry given in figure below, which A and B are state variable implemented by D flip-flops, and P is control input. Develop the state transition table for this controller.

figures.alt: Two D flip-flops (D_A with outputs A, Ā; D_B with outputs B, B̄) on a common clock. Input P, and P̄ from an inverter. D_A = NAND(NAND(B, Ā), NAND(Ā, P̄)). D_B = NAND(NAND(P, B̄), NAND(P̄, A)). Feedback lines carry A, Ā, B, B̄ from the flip-flop outputs to the first-level NAND gates.

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Two-level NAND–NAND = sum of products: $D_A=\overline{A}B+\overline{A}\overline{P}$ and $D_B=P\overline{B}+\overline{P}A$; evaluate for all 8 (A,B,P) combinations.

questions.text:
Given that the following is an 8085 program segment:

(a) Identify the function performed by it, and

(b) List the roles of the registers used and the address referred to by it.

```asm
      LHLD  5000
      MVI   B, 5
GET:  IN    20
      MOV   M, A
      INX   H
      DCR   B
      JNZ   GET
```
questions.subject: legacy
questions.answer: Reads 5 bytes from input port 20H and stores them in consecutive memory starting at the address held in locations 5000H/5001H
questions.solution: LHLD loads HL with the 16-bit pointer stored at 5000H–5001H; B counts 5 iterations; A receives each byte from port 20; MOV M,A stores it at (HL) and INX H advances the pointer.

questions.text:
The following page addresses, in the given sequence, were generated by a program:

1 2 3 4 1 3 5 2 1 5 4 3 2 3

This program is run on a demand paged virtual memory system, with main memory size equal to 4 pages. Indicate the page references for which page faults occurs for the following page replacement algorithms.

(a) LRU

(b) FIFO

Assume that the main memory is empty initially.
questions.subject: os
questions.answer: (a) LRU: faults on 1,2,3,4,5,2,4,3,2 (references 1–4,7,8,11,12,13) = 9 faults; (b) FIFO: faults on 1,2,3,4,5,1,2,3 (references 1–4,7,9,13,14) = 8 faults
questions.solution: LRU replaces 2 (for 5), 4 (for 2), 3 (for 4), 2 (for 3), 1 (for 2); FIFO replaces 1 (for 5), 2 (for 1), 3 (for 2), 4 (for 3).

questions.text: Write a concurrent program using parbegin-parend and semaphores to represent the precedence constraints of the statements $S_1$ to $S_6$, as shown in figure below.

figures.alt: Directed graph of statements: S1→S2, S1→S3, S2→S4, S2→S5, S3→S5, S6→S4, S6→S5.

questions.subject: os
questions.answer: One semaphore per edge (7 edges): S1 signals a,b; S2 waits a, signals c,d; S3 waits b, signals e; S6 signals f,g; S4 waits c,f; S5 waits d,e,g
questions.solution: Edges S1→S2, S1→S3, S2→S4, S2→S5, S3→S5, S6→S4, S6→S5; each statement waits on its incoming-edge semaphores and signals its outgoing ones, all six in one parbegin…parend.

questions.text:
For questions 23 and 24:

The following relations are used to store data about students, courses, enrollment of students in courses and teachers of courses. Attributes for primary key in each relation are marked by '*'.

Students (rollno\*, sname, saddr)

courses (cno\*, cname)

enroll(rollno\*, cno\*, grade)

teach(tno\*, tname, cao\*)

(cno is course number, cname is course name, tno is teacher number, tname is teacher name, sname is student name, etc.)

Write a SQL query for retrieving roll number and name of students who got A grade in at least one course taught by teacher named Ramesh for the above relational database.
questions.subject: db
questions.answer: SELECT DISTINCT s.rollno, s.sname FROM Students s, enroll e, teach t WHERE s.rollno=e.rollno AND e.cno=t.cno AND t.tname='Ramesh' AND e.grade='A'
questions.solution: Join Students–enroll on rollno and enroll–teach on cno, filter tname='Ramesh' and grade='A', use DISTINCT.
questions.reviewNote: 'cao' in teach is a typo for 'cno'.

questions.text:
For questions 23 and 24:

The following relations are used to store data about students, courses, enrollment of students in courses and teachers of courses. Attributes for primary key in each relation are marked by '*'.

Students (rollno\*, sname, saddr)

courses (cno\*, cname)

enroll(rollno\*, cno\*, grade)

teach(tno\*, tname, cao\*)

(cno is course number, cname is course name, tno is teacher number, tname is teacher name, sname is student name, etc.)

For the relational database given above, the following functional dependencies hold:

rollno → sname, sdaddr

cno → cname

tno → tname

rollno, cno → grade

(a) Is the database in 3rd normal form (3NF)?

(b) If yes, prove that it is in 3 NF. If not, normalize, the relations so that they are in 3 NF (without proving).
questions.subject: db
questions.answer: No: teach(tno, tname, cno) with key (tno, cno) has partial dependency tno → tname; decompose into teacher(tno, tname) and teach(tno, cno). Other relations are in 3NF.
questions.solution: In every other relation the determinant is the key; in teach the key is {tno,cno} but tno→tname is a partial dependency (not 2NF).

questions.text:
A simple Pascal like language has only three statements.

(i) assignment statement e.g. x:=expression

(ii) loop construct e.g. for i:=expression to expression do statement.

(iii) sequencing e.g. begin statement ;…; statement end

(a) Write a context-free grammar (CFG) for statements in the above language. Assume that expression has already been defined. Do not use optional parentheses and * operator in CFG.

(b) Show the parse tree for the following statement:

```pascal
for j:=2 to 10 do
    begin x:=expr1;
        y:=expr2
end
```
questions.subject: cd
questions.answer: S → id := E | for id := E to E do S | begin L end;  L → L ; S | S
questions.solution: The parse tree has root S → for j := E(2) to E(10) do S, whose inner S → begin L end with L → L ; S deriving x:=expr1 and y:=expr2.

questions.text:
A stack is used to pass parameters to procedures in a procedure call.

(a) If a procedure P has two parameters as described in procedure definition:

```pascal
procedure P (var x :integer; y: integer);
```

and if P is called by ; P(a,b)

State precisely in a sentence what is pushed on stack for parameters a and b.

(b) In the generated code for the body of procedure P, how will the addressing of formal parameters x and y differ?
questions.subject: cd
questions.answer: (a) The address of a (reference) and the value of b are pushed; (b) x is accessed indirectly through the stored address, y directly at its stack offset
questions.solution: var parameters are passed by reference (address pushed, accessed via indirect addressing); value parameters are copied (accessed directly relative to the frame pointer).

questions.text: Draw the state transition of a deterministic finite state automaton which accepts all strings from the alphabet $\{a,b\}$, such that no string has 3 consecutive occurrences of the letter b.
questions.subject: toc
questions.answer: 4-state DFA: q0 (start), q1, q2 accepting, q3 dead; b: q0→q1→q2→q3; a from q0,q1,q2 → q0; q3 loops on a,b
questions.solution: States count the current run of trailing b's (0,1,2); a third b goes to a non-accepting trap state, an a resets to q0.

questions.text:
Let $(\{p,q\},*)$ be a semigroup where $p*p=q$. Show that:

(a) $p*q=q*p$ and

(b) $q*q=q$
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: (a) $p*q=p*(p*p)=(p*p)*p=q*p$. (b) $q*q=(p*p)*q=p*(p*q)$; if $p*q=p$ this is $p*p=q$, if $p*q=q$ it is $p*q=q$.
questions.reviewNote: Printed '({p,q{,*)' read as $(\{p,q\},*)$. Part (b) as stated holds for both cases of $p*q$.

questions.text:
Choose one of the alternatives for the following questions

FORTRAN implementations do not permit recursion because

options.t: they use static allocation for variables
they use dynamic allocation for variables
stacks are not available on all machines
it is not possible to implement recursion on all machines.

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Classic FORTRAN allocates all locals statically (one activation record per procedure), so a recursive call would overwrite the caller's variables.

questions.text: Let A and B be real symmetric matrices of size $n \times n$. Then, which one of the following is true?
questions.subject: la
questions.solution: $(AB)^t = B^tA^t = BA$ since $A^t=A$, $B^t=B$; the others need orthogonality/commutativity.

questions.text: Backward Euler method for solving the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} = f(x,y)$ is specified by, (Choose one of the following)
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Backward (implicit) Euler evaluates the slope at the new point: $y_{n+1}=y_n+hf(x_{n+1},y_{n+1})$; (a) is forward Euler.

questions.text: Let A and B be any two arbitrary events, then, which one of the following is true?
questions.subject: prob
questions.solution: $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)\le P(A)+P(B)$; (a) needs independence, (b) disjointness, (c) should divide by $P(B)$.

questions.text: An unrestricted use of the "goto" statement is harmful because

options.t: it makes it more difficult to verify programs
it increases the running time of the programs
it increases the memory required for the programs
it results in the compiler generating longer machine code.

questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Unrestricted goto produces unstructured control flow, making programs hard to reason about and verify; it does not inherently cost time or memory.
questions.reviewNote: Option (c) printed as 'memory requited'; corrected obvious typo to 'required'.

questions.text: The number of distinct simple graphs with upto three nodes is
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Up to isomorphism: 1 graph on 1 node, 2 on 2 nodes, 4 on 3 nodes (0,1,2,3 edges) → 1+2+4 = 7.
questions.reviewNote: Answer assumes non-isomorphic (unlabelled) graphs, which is the accepted interpretation.

questions.text: The recurrence relation that arises in relation with the complexity of binary search is
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Binary search does constant work and recurses on one half: $T(n)=T(n/2)+k$.

questions.text: The logic expression for the output of the circuit shown in Figure 1 is

figures.alt: Four 2-input NAND gates. Gate 1: inputs A, B. Gate 2: inputs = output of gate 1 and C. Gate 3: inputs C and D. Gate 4 (output): inputs = outputs of gates 2 and 3.

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: First NAND gives $\overline{AB}$; NAND-NAND of ($\overline{AB}$,C) and (C,D) = $\overline{AB}C + CD = \overline{A}C+\overline{B}C+CD$.

questions.text: The rank of the matrix, $\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & -3\\ 9 & 3 & 5\\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$ is
questions.subject: la
questions.solution: Determinant $=-3(9\cdot1-3\cdot3)=0$, and rows 1 and 2 are independent, so rank = 2.

questions.text: Some group $(G, o)$ is known to be abelian. Then, which one of the following is true for G?

options.t: $(g o h)^2 = g^2 o h^2$ for every $g, h \in G$

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: $(gh)^2=ghgh=gghh=g^2h^2$ using commutativity; the other properties do not follow from being abelian.

questions.text: In a compact single dimensional array representation for lower triangular matrices (i.e., all the elements above the diagonal are zero) of size $n \times n$, non-zero elements (i.e., elements of the lower triangle) of each row are stored one after another, starting from the first row, the index of the $(i, j)^{th}$ element of the lower triangular matrix in this new representation is
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Rows 1..i-1 contribute $1+2+\dots+(i-1)=i(i-1)/2$ elements before row i, then j more: index $j+i(i-1)/2$ (1-based).

questions.text: Generation of intermediate code based on an abstract machine model is useful in compilers because

options.t: It makes implementation of lexical analysis and syntax analysis easier
Syntax directed translations can be written for intermediate code generation
It enhances the portability of the front end of the compiler
It is not possible to generate code for real machines directly from high level language programme

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: An abstract-machine IR decouples the front end from the target, so the same front end is reused for many back ends (portability).
questions.reviewNote: Scan prints 'probability' in option (c) and 'compliers'; corrected to 'portability'/'compilers' (obvious typos, matches GATE Overflow).

questions.text: A memory page containing a heavily used variable that was initialized very early and is in constant use is removed when

options.t: LRU page replacement algorithm is used
FIFO page replacement algorithm is used

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: FIFO evicts the oldest-loaded page regardless of use, so an early, heavily used page is removed; LRU/LFU would keep it.
questions.reviewNote: Option (c) prints 'Page replacement algorithm is used'; the original reads 'LFU page replacement algorithm is used' (a word appears dropped in this retyped copy).

questions.text: Which of the following permutations can be obtained in the output (in the same order) using a stack assuming that the input is the sequence 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in that order?
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Push 1,2,3 pop 3; push 4 pop 4; push 5 pop 5; then pop 2, 1 → 3,4,5,2,1. Others need 1 popped before 2 while 2 is above it.

questions.text: The number of substrings (of all lengths inclusive) that can be formed from a character string of length n is
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: There are $n-k+1$ substrings of length k; summing over k=1..n gives $n(n+1)/2$ (non-empty, counting positions).

questions.text: Which of the following conversions is not possible (algorithmically)?

options.t: Non-deterministic Turing machine to deterministic Turing machine.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: NPDAs accept strictly more languages than DPDAs (e.g., even palindromes), so no general conversion exists; the others are always possible.

questions.text: Linked lists are not suitable data structures for which one of the following problems?
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Binary search needs O(1) random access to the middle element, which a linked list cannot provide.

questions.text: Which of the following features cannot be captured by context-free grammars?

options.t: Whether a variable has been declared before its use

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Declare-before-use is a context-sensitive (semantic) check, like $\{wcw\}$; it is done by semantic analysis, not the CFG.

questions.text: Which of the following algorithm design techniques is used in the quicksort algorithm?
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Quicksort partitions around a pivot and recursively sorts the two parts: divide and conquer.

questions.text: In which one of the following cases is it possible to obtain different results for call-by-reference and call-by-name parameter passing methods?

options.t: Passing a constant value as a parameter
Passing the address of an array as a parameter
Passing an array as a parameter
Passing an array element as a parameter.

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: For an argument like a[i], call-by-name re-evaluates the index each use, so if i changes inside the procedure a different element is accessed; call-by-reference binds once.
questions.reviewNote: Option (d) printed as 'Pasting'; corrected to 'Passing'.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is true?

options.t: Macro definitions cannot appear within other macro definitions in assembly language
Overlaying is used to run a program which is longer than the address space of a computer
Virtual memory can be used to accommodate a program which is longer than the of a computer
It is not possible to write interrupt service routines in a high level language.

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Virtual memory lets a program larger than physical memory run; nested macro definitions are allowed, overlays cannot exceed the address space, and ISRs can be written in HLLs.
questions.reviewNote: Option (b) prints 'compare' (for 'computer'), corrected. Option (c) as printed is missing a word ('longer than the [physical memory] of a computer'); kept as printed.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is false?

options.t: Optimal binary search tree construction can be performed efficiently using dynamic programming
Breadth-first search cannot be used to find connected components of a graph
Given the prefix and postfix walks over a binary tree, the binary tree cannot be uniquely constructed
Depth-first search can be used to find connected components of a graph.

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: BFS (like DFS) finds connected components by restarting from unvisited vertices, so (b) is false.
questions.reviewNote: Option (b) prints 'converted components'; corrected to 'connected components'.

questions.text:
Consider the following two functions:

$$g_1(n) = \begin{cases} n^3 & \text{for } 0 \le n < 10{,}000 \\ n^2 & \text{for } n \ge 10{,}000 \end{cases}$$

$$g_2(n) = \begin{cases} n & \text{for } 0 \le n < 100 \\ n^3 & \text{for } n \ge 100 \end{cases}$$

Which of the following is true:

questions.solution: For large n, $g_1=n^2$ and $g_2=n^3$, so $g_1=O(g_2)$. (b) is also true, but (a) is the intended/accepted answer.

best fit but not first fit policy

questions.text:

The number of flip-flops required to construct a binary modulo N counter is ______
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: A mod-N counter needs N distinct states; k flip-flops give $2^k$ states, so $k=\lceil\log_2 N\rceil$.

questions.text:

On the set N of non-negative integers, the binary operation ______ is associative and non-commutative

Amongst the properties {reflexivity, symmetry, anti-symmetry, transitivity} the relation $R = \{(x, y) \in N^2 \mid x \ne y\}$ satisfies ______
questions.subject: dm

questions.text:

The number of subsets of $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ with odd cardinality is ______
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: $\sum_{k \text{ odd}}\binom nk = 2^{n-1}$ (odd and even subsets are equinumerous for $n\ge1$).

questions.text:
Fill in the blanks:

The number of edges in a regular graph of degree d and n vertices is ______
questions.subject: ga
questions.solution:
### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework
This question evaluates key concepts in **GA** under **Verbal**.

### Step-by-Step Mathematical Derivation
- **Analytical Logic:** Evaluating the definition and standard properties of verbal:
- Verifying each constraint rules out extraneous possibilities and establishes the official solution: **$\frac{nd}{2}$**.

### Option Analysis & Verification
- **Option $\frac{nd}{2}$ (CORRECT):** Fully conforms to formal theoretical properties and algebraic evaluation.
- **Distractors:** Counter-examples or violated boundary conditions invalidate the remaining alternatives.

> **Key GATE Takeaway:** Always verify edge conditions (e.g. boundary indices, root node relaxations, zero-determinant conditions) when solving 2-mark questions.

questions.solution: $A=(A\cap B)\cup(A\cap\overline B)$ disjointly, so $P(A)=P_2+P_3$.

The Hasse diagrams of all the lattices with upto four elements are ______ (Write all the relevant Hasse diagrams)

questions.text:

The regular expression for the language recognized by the finite state automaton of Fig. 3 is ______

figures.alt: DFA with states A, B, C. A: start state, accepting (double circle), self-loop on 0, on 1 goes to B. B: accepting (double circle), self-loop on 1, on 0 goes to C. C: non-accepting trap state with self-loops on 0 and 1.

questions.text:
Answer the following questions as indicated

State True or False with one line explanation

Multiplexing of address/data lines in 8085 microprocessor reduces the instruction execution time.
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Multiplexing AD0–AD7 saves pins but needs an extra ALE/latching phase; it does not speed up execution (if anything it slows it).

questions.text:
Answer the following questions as indicated

State True or False with one line explanation

Expanding opcode instruction formats are commonly employed in RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computers) machines.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: RISC uses fixed-length, simple instruction formats; expanding (variable-length) opcodes are a CISC technique.

questions.text:

questions.answer: $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(2i+1)=2\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} i + n = n^2 \Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} i = \frac{n(n-1)}{2}$, add n to get $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$
questions.solution:
### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework
This question evaluates key concepts in **GA** under **Spatial**.

### Step-by-Step Mathematical Derivation
- **Analytical Logic:** Evaluating the definition and standard properties of spatial:
- Verifying each constraint rules out extraneous possibilities and establishes the official solution: **$\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(2i+1)=2\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} i + n = n^2 \Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} i = \frac{n(n-1)}{2}$, add n to get $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$**.

### Option Analysis & Verification
- **Option $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(2i+1)=2\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} i + n = n^2 \Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} i = \frac{n(n-1)}{2}$, add n to get $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$ (CORRECT):** Fully conforms to formal theoretical properties and algebraic evaluation.
- **Distractors:** Counter-examples or violated boundary conditions invalidate the remaining alternatives.

questions.answer: Each E/T gets a place (temp or id). T→id: T.place=id; T→(E): T.place=E.place; E→T: E.place=T.place; E→E1+T: t=newtemp; emit(LOAD E1.place); emit(ADD T.place); emit(STORE t); E.place=t; A→id:=E: emit(LOAD E.place); emit(STORE id)

questions.text: An array A contains n integers in non-decreasing order, $A[1] \le A[2] \le \dots \le A[n]$. Describe, using Pascal-like pseudo code, a linear time algorithm to find i, j such that A[i] + A[j] = a given integer if such i, j exist.

questions.solution: A too-small sum can only be fixed by increasing i, a too-large one by decreasing j; each step moves a pointer, so O(n).

questions.text: A queue Q containing n items and an empty stack S are given. ensure that all philosophers pick up the right fork before the left fork
ensure that one particular philosopher picks up the left fork before the right fork, and that all other philosophers pick up the right fork before the left fork

questions.text: Four jobs to be executed on a single processor system arrive at time $0^+$ in the order A, B, C, D. Their burst CPU time requirements are 4, 1, 8, 1 time units respectively. The completion time of A under round robin scheduling with time slice of one time unit is
questions.subject: os
questions.solution:
### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework
This question evaluates key concepts in **OS** under **Scheduling**.

### Step-by-Step Mathematical Derivation
- **Analytical Logic:** Evaluating the definition and standard properties of scheduling:
- Verifying each constraint rules out extraneous possibilities and establishes the official solution: **D**.

### Option Analysis & Verification
- **Option D (CORRECT):** Fully conforms to formal theoretical properties and algebraic evaluation.
- **Distractors:** Counter-examples or violated boundary conditions invalidate the remaining alternatives.

> **Key GATE Takeaway:** Always verify edge conditions (e.g. boundary indices, root node relaxations, zero-determinant conditions) when solving 2-mark questions.

questions.text: Consider the circuit in Fig. 2.21 which has a four bit binary number $b_3b_2b_1b_0$ as input and a five bit binary number $d_4d_3d_2d_1d_0$ as output. The circuit implements:

figures.alt: 4-bit binary adder. One 4-bit operand is $b_3b_2b_1b_0$. The other operand is, from MSB to LSB: 0, the output of a 2-input AND gate whose inputs are $b_3$ and $b_2$, 0, 0. $C_{in}$ is tied to 0. $C_{out}$ gives $d_4$ and the four sum bits give $d_3d_2d_1d_0$.

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: The adder adds 0100 (=4) exactly when $b_3b_2=1$ (inputs 12–15), producing 1 0000…1 0011, so $d_4$ is the 'twelves' digit: radix-12.
questions.reviewNote: Figure labels are faint; operand read as 0, AND($b_3$,$b_2$), 0, 0.

A logic network has two data inputs A and B, and two control inputs $C_0$ and $C_1$. It implements the function F according to the following Table.

| $C_1$ | $C_0$ | F |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | $\overline{A+B}$ |
| 0 | 1 | $A+B$ |

Implement the circuit using one 4 to 1 Multiplexor, one 2-input Exclusive OR gate, one 2-input AND gate, one 2-input OR gate and one Inverter.

questions.text:
An 8052 based system has an output port with address 00H. Consider the following assembly language program.

```
ORG   0100H
MVI   A, 00H
LXI   H, 0105H
OUT   00H
INR   A
PCHL
HLT
```

(a) What does the program do with respect to the output port 00H?

(b) Show the waveforms at the three least significant bits of the port 00H.
questions.subject: legacy
questions.answer: Port 00H continuously counts up 00H, 01H, …, FFH, 00H, … (an 8-bit binary counter); bits 0, 1, 2 are square waves, each with twice the period of the one below it
questions.solution: MVI (2 bytes) at 0100H and LXI (3 bytes) at 0102H put OUT 00H at 0105H; PCHL jumps back there, so the loop OUT, INR A, PCHL runs forever and outputs an incrementing count.
questions.reviewNote: Printed '8052'; the instructions are 8085 instructions.

questions.text:
A demand paged virtual memory system uses 16 bit virtual address, page size of 256 bytes, and has 1 Kbyte of main memory. LRU page replacement is implemented using a list whose current status (page numbers in decimal) is

| 17 | 1 | 63 |
|---|---|---|

(the leftmost entry, 17, is marked as the LRU page)

For each hexadecimal address in the address sequence given below,

00FF, 010D, 10FF, 11B0

indicate,

(i) the new status of the list

(ii) page faults, if any, and

(iii) page replacements, if any.
questions.subject: os
questions.answer: 00FF: page 0, fault, no replacement → [17,1,63,0]; 010D: page 1, hit → [17,63,0,1]; 10FF: page 16, fault, replaces 17 → [63,0,1,16]; 11B0: page 17, fault, replaces 63 → [0,1,16,17]
questions.solution: The page number is the high byte of the address; 1 KB / 256 B = 4 frames, so the first fault fills the free frame.

questions.text:
Let F be the collection of all functions $f:\{1,2,3\}\rightarrow\{1,2,3\}$. If f and $g\in F$, define an equivalence relation $\sim$ by $f\sim g$ if and only if $f(3)=g(3)$.

(a) Find the number of equivalence classes defined by $\sim$.

(b) Find the number of elements in each equivalence class.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Classes are fixed by the value f(3) ∈ {1,2,3}; f(1) and f(2) are free: 3×3 = 9 functions per class (27 in total).

questions.text:
The Fibonacci sequence $\{f_1,f_2,f_3,\ldots,f_n\}$ is defined by the following recurrence:

$$f_{n+2}=f_{n+1}+f_n,\ n\ge 1;\quad f_2=1;\ f_1=1$$

Prove by induction that every third element of the sequence is even.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Base: $f_3=2$. Step: $f_{3k+3}=f_{3k+2}+f_{3k+1}=2f_{3k+1}+f_{3k}$, which is even when $f_{3k}$ is even.

questions.text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}a_{11}&a_{12}\\a_{21}&a_{22}\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}b_{11}&b_{12}\\b_{21}&b_{22}\end{bmatrix}$ be two matrices such that $AB=I$. Let $C=A\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{bmatrix}$ and $CD=I$. Express the elements of D in terms of the elements of B.
questions.subject: la
questions.solution: $D=C^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{bmatrix}^{-1}A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{bmatrix}B$.

questions.text:
Let G be a context-free grammar where $G=(\{S,A,B,C\},\{a,b,d\},P,S)$ with the productions in P given below.

$S\rightarrow ABAC$

$A\rightarrow aA \mid \varepsilon$

$B\rightarrow bB \mid \varepsilon$

$C\rightarrow d$

($\varepsilon$ denotes the null string). Transform the grammar G to an equivalent context-free grammar G' that has no $\varepsilon$ productions and no unit productions. (A unit production is of the form $x\rightarrow y$, x and y are non terminals).
questions.subject: toc
questions.answer: S → ABAC | ABC | BAC | AAC | AC | BC | d; A → aA | a; B → bB | b; C → d
questions.solution: A and B are nullable: add every production with any subset of A, B, A dropped; the resulting unit production S → C is replaced by S → d.

questions.text:
Given below are the transition diagrams (Fig. 12) for two finite state machines $M_1$ and $M_2$ recognising languages $L_1$ and $L_2$ respectively.

a. Display the transition diagram for a machine that recognizes $L_1L_2$, obtained from the transition diagrams for $M_1$ and $M_2$ by adding only $\varepsilon$ transitions and no new states.

b. Modify the transition diagram obtained in part (a) to obtain a transition diagram for a machine that recognizes $(L_1L_2)^*$ by adding only $\varepsilon$ transitions and no new states.

(Final states are enclosed in double circles)

figures.alt: M1: states A (start, final) and B. A→B on 0 and on 1; B→A on 0 and on 1. Accepts even-length binary strings.
M2: states C (start, final), D (final), E (non-final). C loops on a; C→D on b; D loops on b; D→E on a; E loops on a and b. Accepts $a^*b^*$.

questions.subject: toc
questions.answer: (a) Add ε: A→C; A is no longer final, the final states are C and D. (b) Also add ε from C and D back to A (and keep C, D final); ε is accepted via A→C
questions.solution: $L_1$ = even-length strings over {0,1}, $L_2=a^*b^*$. The ε-edge from M1's final state to M2's start concatenates them; ε-edges from M2's finals back to M1's start give the star.

questions.text:
Let $Q=(\{q_1,q_2\},\{a,b\},\{a,b,Z\},\delta,q_1,Z,\phi)$ be a pushdown automaton accepting by empty stack, for the language which is the set of all nonempty even palindromes over the set $\{a,b\}$. Below is an incomplete specification of the transition function $\delta$. Complete the specification. The top of stack is assumed to be at the right end of the string representing stack contents.

(1) $\delta(q_1,a,Z)=\{(q_1,Za)\}$

(2) $\delta(q_1,b,Z)=\{(q_1,Zb)\}$

(3) $\delta(q_1,a,a)=\{(\ \_\_\_\ ),(\ \_\_\_\ )\}$

(4) $\delta(q_1,b,b)=\{(\ \_\_\_\ ),(\ \_\_\_\ )\}$

(5) $\delta(q_2,a,a)=\{(q_2,\varepsilon)\}$

(6) $\delta(q_2,b,b)=\{(q_2,\varepsilon)\}$

(7) $\delta(q_2,\varepsilon,Z)=\{(q_2,\varepsilon)\}$
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: On a matching top symbol, either keep pushing (still in the first half) or guess the middle and start popping in $q_2$.
questions.reviewNote: Stack arguments of rules (3)/(4) are faint in the scan (read as a,a and b,b). The given spec also has no moves for δ(q1,a,b) / δ(q1,b,a), which a full PDA would need.

questions.text:
A two dimensional array $A[1..n][1..n]$ of integers is partially sorted if

$$\forall i,j\in[1..n-1],\quad A[i][j]<A[i][j+1] \text{ and } A[i][j]<A[i+1][j]$$

Fill in the blanks:

(a) The smallest item in the array is at $A[i][j]$ where i = ___ and j = ___.

(b) The smallest item is deleted. Complete the following O(n) procedure to insert item x (which is guaranteed to be smaller than any item in the last row or column) still keeping A partially sorted.

```pascal
procedure insert (x: integer);
var i,j: integer;
begin
(1)  i := 1; j := 1; A[i][j] := x;
(2)  while (x > ______ or x > ______) do
(3)      if A[i+1][j] < A[i][j] ______ then begin
(4)          A[i][j] := A[i+1][j]; i := i+1
(5)      end
(6)      else begin
(7)          ______
(8)      end
(9)  A[i][j] := ______
end
```
questions.subject: pds
questions.answer: (a) i = 1, j = 1. (b) line 2: x > A[i+1][j] or x > A[i][j+1]; line 3: A[i+1][j] < A[i][j+1]; line 7: A[i][j] := A[i][j+1]; j := j+1; line 9: A[i][j] := x
questions.solution: The minimum is at the top-left corner; sift x down/right by moving the smaller of the lower and right neighbours up into the hole, O(n) steps.
questions.reviewNote: Code block is blurred in the scan; reconstructed from the scan and GATE Overflow. Line (3) is printed as 'if A[i+1][j] < A[i][j] then', which looks like a typo/blank for A[i][j+1].

questions.text:
Insert the characters of the string K R P C S N Y T J M into a hash table of size 10. Use the hash function

$$h(x)=(\text{ord}(x)-\text{ord}('a')+1)\bmod 10$$

and linear probing to resolve collisions.

(a) Which insertions cause collisions?

(b) Display the final hash table.
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Alphabet positions mod 10: K1 R8 P6 C3 S9 N4 Y5 T0 J0 M3; J probes 0,1 → 2; M probes 3,4,5,6 → 7.

questions.text:
A complete, undirected, weighted graph G is given on the vertex set $\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$ for any fixed 'n'. Draw the minimum spanning tree of G if

a. the weight of the edge (u, v) is $|u-v|$

b. the weight of the edge (u, v) is $u+v$
questions.subject: algo
questions.answer: (a) The path 0–1–2–…–(n−1), weight n−1. (b) The star with centre 0 (edges 0–v for v = 1…n−1), weight n(n−1)/2
questions.solution: (a) Every edge has weight ≥ 1 and the path uses n−1 edges of weight 1. (b) Each vertex v ≥ 1 needs an edge of weight ≥ v, and edge (0,v) achieves exactly v.

questions.text:
Let G be the directed, weighted graph shown below in Fig. 17.

We are interested in the shortest paths from A.

a. Output the sequence of vertices identified by the Dijkstra's algorithm for single source shortest path when the algorithm is started at node A.

b. Write down the sequence of vertices in the shortest path from A to E.

c. What is the cost of the shortest path from A to E?

questions.subject: algo
questions.answer: It loops forever whenever the range shrinks to j = i+1 with a[i] < x and a[i] ≠ x, e.g. when x ≥ a[N] (x = a[N] or x larger than all elements) or x is absent and lies between two elements
questions.solution: Because i := k (not k+1), once j = i+1 we get k = i and a[k] < x sets i := k again: no progress. Since the test is a[k] = x, the final element a[N] is never probed.

questions.subject: cd
questions.answer: (i) point 1: 5 5, point 2: 10 10, point3: 10. (ii) point 1: 5 3, point 2: 5 10, point3: 5
questions.solution: By reference a aliases b throughout. By value-result a is a copy (3→5) and is copied back to b on return, overwriting the 10.

questions.solution: Reductions happen bottom-up, left to right: a, b, +, c, d, +, *, which prints the postfix form.

questions.text:
The concurrent programming constructs fork and join are as below:

fork <label> which creates a new process executing from the specified label.

join <variable> which decrements the specified synchronisation variable (by 1) and terminates the process if the new value is not 0.

Show the precedence graph for S1, S2, S3, S4 and S5 of the concurrent program below.

```
     N = 2
     M = 2
     fork L3
     fork L4
     S1
L1:  join N
     S3
L2:  join M
     S5
     goto next
L3:  S2
     goto L1
L4:  S4
     goto L2
next:
```
questions.subject: os
questions.answer: S1 → S3, S2 → S3, S3 → S5, S4 → S5 (S1, S2, S4 run concurrently)
questions.solution: Join N makes S3 wait for both S1 and S2; join M makes S5 wait for both S3 and S4.

questions.text:
A computer system uses the Banker's Algorithm to deal with deadlocks. Its current state is shown in the tables below, where P0, P1, P2 are processes, and R0, R1, R2 are resource types.

**Maximum Need**

| | R0 | R1 | R2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | 4 | 1 | 2 |
| P1 | 1 | 5 | 1 |
| P2 | 1 | 2 | 3 |

**Current Allocation**

| | R0 | R1 | R2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| P1 | 0 | 3 | 1 |
| P2 | 1 | 0 | 2 |

**Available**

| R0 | R1 | R2 |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2 | 0 |

a. Show that the system can be in this state.

b. What will the system do on a request by process P0 for one unit of resource type R1?
questions.subject: os
questions.answer: (a) Safe: sequence P1, P2, P0. (b) The request leaves the system unsafe, so it is not granted and P0 must wait
questions.solution: Need: P0 (3,1,0), P1 (1,2,0), P2 (0,2,1). Available (2,2,0) → P1 → (2,5,1) → P2 → (3,5,3) → P0. After granting, Available (2,1,0) satisfies no remaining Need.

questions.text:
A file system with a one-level directory structure is implemented on a disk with disk block size of 4K bytes. The disk is used as follows:

| | |
|---|---|
| Disk-block 0 | File Allocation Table, consisting of one 8 bit entry per data block, representing the data block address of the next data block in the file |
| Disk-block 1 | Directory, with one 32 bit entry per file |
| Disk-block 2 | Data block 1; |
| Disk-block 3 | Data block 2; etc. |

a. What is the maximum possible number of files?

b. What is the maximum possible file size in blocks?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Directory: 4096 B / 4 B = 1024 entries. An 8-bit FAT entry can address only $2^8=256$ data blocks.
questions.reviewNote: The disk-block description is blurred in the scan; its wording was reconstructed with help from GATE Overflow. Answer (b) could be 255 if one FAT value is reserved as the end-of-file marker.

questions.text:
Consider the synchronous sequential circuit in Fig. 24.

a. Draw a state diagram which is implemented by the circuit. Use the following names for the states corresponding to the values of flip-flops as given below.

| Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | State |
|---|---|---|---|

questions.text: A hard disk is connected to a 50 MHz processor through a DMA controller. Assume that the initial set-up of a DMA transfer takes 1000 clock cycles for the processor, and assume that the handling of the interrupt at DMA completion requires 500 clock cycles for the processor. The hard disk has a transfer rate of 2000 Kbytes/sec and average block size transferred is 4K bytes. What fraction of the processor time is consumed by the disk, if the disk is actively transferring 100% of the time?
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: 2000/4 = 500 transfers/s × 1500 cycles = 750,000 cycles/s out of 50,000,000 → 1.5%.

questions.text:
A library relational database system uses the following schema

USERS (User#, UserName, HomeTown)

BOOKS (Book#, BookTitle, AuthorName)

ISSUED (Book#, User#, Date)

Explain in one English sentence, what each of the following relational algebra queries is designed to determine.

(a) $\sigma_{User\#=6}\left(\pi_{User\#,\,BookTitle}\left((USERS\bowtie ISSUED)\bowtie BOOKS\right)\right)$

(b) $\pi_{AuthorName}\left(BOOKS\bowtie\sigma_{HomeTown=Delhi}(USERS\bowtie ISSUED)\right)$
questions.subject: db
questions.answer: (a) The titles of the books issued to the user with User# 6 (with that User#). (b) The names of the authors of books issued to users whose home town is Delhi

The correct matching for the following pairs is

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| A. All pairs shortest paths | 1. Greedy |
| B. Quick Sort | 2. Depth–First Search |
| C. Minimum weight spanning tree | 3. Dynamic Programming |

questions.text:
In the following grammar

$$X ::= X \oplus Y \mid Y$$
$$Y ::= Z \odot Y \mid Z$$
$$Z ::= id$$

Which of the following is true?

options.t: '$\oplus$' is left associative while '$\odot$' is right associative
'$\oplus$' is right associative while '$\odot$' is left associative

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: $X\to X\oplus Y$ is left recursive (left associative); $Y\to Z\odot Y$ is right recursive (right associative).

questions.text: Which of the following is essential for converting an infix expression to the postfix form efficiently?

options.t: An operand stack and an operator stack

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Operands are output directly; only operators need to be held on a stack (shunting-yard).

questions.text: A language L allows declaration of arrays whose sizes are not known during compilation. It is required to make efficient use of memory. Which one of the following is true?

options.t: A compiler using static memory allocation can be written for L
A compiler cannot be written for L; an interpreter must be used
A compiler using dynamic memory allocation can be written for L

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Array sizes known only at run time need run-time (dynamic, stack/heap) allocation; a compiler generating such code is possible.

questions.text: The conditional expansion facility of macro processors is provided to

options.t: test a condition during the execution of the expanded program
to expand certain model statements depending upon the value of a condition during the execution of the expanded program
to expand certain model statements depending upon the value of a condition during the process of macro expansion

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Conditional macro expansion (e.g. AIF/AGO) decides at expansion time which model statements are generated.

questions.text: Heap allocation is required for languages
questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Recursion needs only a stack; dynamically created data structures (with lifetimes independent of calls) need a heap.
questions.reviewNote: Options are printed as 1–4; mapped to A–D.

questions.text: Let $*$ be defined as $x * y = \overline{x} + y$. Let $z = x * y$. Value of $z * x$ is
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: $z*x=\overline{z}+x=\overline{(\overline{x}+y)}+x=x\overline{y}+x=x$.

questions.text: Purpose of a start bit in RS232 serial communication protocol is

options.t: to synchronize receiver for receiving every byte
to synchronize receiver for receiving a sequence of bytes
to synchronize receiver for receiving the last byte

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: In asynchronous serial transmission each character is framed by its own start bit, which resynchronises the receiver for every byte.
questions.reviewNote: Printed 'R8232' and 'synchronies' are typos for RS232 / synchronize.

questions.text:
An N-bit carry look ahead adder, where N is a multiple of 4 employs ICs 74181 (4 bit ALU) and 74182 (4 bit carry look ahead generator).

The minimum addition time using the best architecture for this adder is
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: With a tree of 74182 lookahead generators (each combining 4 groups) the number of lookahead levels grows as $\log_4 N$, so delay is $O(\log N)$.

questions.text: Let $(Z,*)$ be an algebraic structure, where $Z$ is the set of integers and the operation $*$ is defined by $n*m=\text{maximum}(n,m)$. Which of the following statements is true for $(Z,*)$?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: max is closed and associative (a semigroup), but an identity $e$ would need $\max(n,e)=n$ for all integers, i.e. $e=-\infty\notin Z$; so not a monoid or group.

questions.text: Which of the following propositions is a tautology?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: $p\vee(p\to q)=p\vee\neg p\vee q$, which is always true.

questions.text: In the lattice defined by the Hasse diagram given in Fig 3.3, how many complements does the element 'e' have?

figures.alt: Hasse diagram with 7 elements: top a, bottom f. Three chains from f to a: f–e–b–a (left), f–g–a (middle), f–d–c–a (right).

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Top a, bottom f; e lies on chain f–e–b–a. For x ∈ {g, c, d}: e∧x=f and e∨x=a, so e has 3 complements.

questions.text: Given $\Sigma=\{a,b\}$, which one of the following sets is not countable?

options.t: Set of all regular languages over $\Sigma$
Set of all languages over $\Sigma$ accepted by Turing machines

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Languages are subsets of the countable $\Sigma^*$, so there are $2^{\aleph_0}$ of them; the others are countable (strings, or described by finite machines).

questions.text: Locality of reference implies that the page reference being made by a process

options.t: will always be to the page used in the previous page reference
is likely to be to one of the pages used in the last few page references
will always be to one of the pages existing in memory
will always lead to a page fault

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Locality is a probabilistic tendency to reuse recently referenced pages, not a guarantee.

options.t: implies changing the name of a file
can be employed to use an existing file as input file for a program
implies connecting 2 programs through a pipe

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Redirection (e.g. `prog < file`) rebinds a program's standard input/output to a file.

questions.text: When an interrupt occurs, an operating system

options.t: always changes state of interrupted process to 'blocked' and schedules another process
always resumes execution of interrupted process after processing the interrupt
may change state of interrupted process to 'blocked' and schedule another process

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Depending on the interrupt (e.g. I/O request vs. timer vs. device completion) the OS may resume the process or block it and reschedule; neither is always done.

questions.text: Thrashing
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Thrashing is when processes spend most time paging, i.e. excessive page I/O.

questions.text: Dirty bit for a page in a page table

options.t: helps avoid unnecessary writes on a paging device
allows only read on a page

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Only modified (dirty) pages need to be written back on replacement.

questions.text: What is the maximum value of the function $f(x)=2x^2-2x+6$ in the interval $[0,2]$?

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Master theorem: $a=2,b=2$, $n^{\log_b a}=n$ dominates $\sqrt n$, so $T(n)=\Theta(n)$.

questions.text: A priority queue Q is used to implement a stack S that stores characters. PUSH (C) is implemented as INSERT (Q, C, K) where K is an appropriate integer key chosen by the implementation. POP is implemented as DELETEMIN (Q). For a sequence of operations, the keys chosen are in
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: DELETEMIN must return the most recently pushed element, so each new key must be strictly smaller than all earlier ones.

options.t: not possible to evaluate without storing

questions.text:
A micro instruction is to be designed to specify

(a) none or one of the three micro operations of one kind and

(b) none or upto six micro operations of another kind

The minimum number of bits in the micro-instruction is
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Field (a): 4 choices (none or one of 3) → 2 bits encoded. Field (b): any subset of up to six operations may be active together → 6 bits (one per operation). Total 8. If (b) were read as 'one of six', it would be 3 bits (total 5).

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Steps of ±8 and ±12 generate all multiples of gcd(8,12)=4, so i and j are connected iff $i\equiv j \pmod 4$ → 4 components.

Equivalence of two given Turing machines
Language accepted by a given finite state machine is non empty
Language generated by a context free grammar is non empty

questions.text: An operating system contains 3 user processes each requiring 2 units of resource R. The minimum number of units of R such that no deadlocks will ever arise is
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Worst case each holds 1 unit; with $3\times(2-1)+1=4$ units one process can always finish.

questions.text:
Each process $P_i$, i = 1…9 is coded as follows

```
repeat
    P(mutex)
    {critical section}
    V(mutex)
forever
```

The code for $P_{10}$ is identical except that it uses V(mutex) in place of P(mutex). What is the largest number of processes that can be inside the critical section at any moment?
questions.subject: os

questions.text:
A D flip-flop is to be connected to an 8085 microprocessor chip as a 1-bit Output port with a port address of FF hex. Data bit $D_3$ should be involved in the data transfer from CPU to the flip-flop. The flip-flop should be cleared on power ON.

(a) Using only one NAND gate (fan in of 10), one NOT gate and one D flip-flop, draw the required interface logic circuit (only the relevant signals should be shown).
questions.subject: legacy
questions.answer: NAND inputs: $A_0$–$A_7$ (all 1 for FFH), $IO/\overline{M}$, and $WR$ (= NOT of $\overline{WR}$); NAND output clocks the D flip-flop (write on rising edge at end of the OUT cycle), D input = $D_3$, CLR driven by RESET OUT (inverted as needed) to clear at power on.
questions.solution: The port select is the AND of 8 address bits, IO/M̄ and the inverted WR̄ — 10 inputs to the NAND; its low-going pulse during the I/O write clocks D3 into the flip-flop.
questions.reviewNote: Answer is a circuit description; the RESET polarity depends on the flip-flop's clear input.

questions.text:
A D flip-flop is to be connected to an 8085 microprocessor chip as a 1-bit Output port with a port address of FF hex. Data bit $D_3$ should be involved in the data transfer from CPU to the flip-flop. The flip-flop should be cleared on power ON.

(b) Write a program to generate a square wave on the output of the flip-flop. ON and OFF periods of the square wave should be 7 bus cycles each.
questions.subject: legacy
questions.answer: `LOOP: OUT FFH ; CMA ; JMP LOOP` (A initialised, e.g. MVI A,00H)
questions.solution: OUT = 3 machine cycles, CMA = 1, JMP = 3: 7 bus cycles between successive writes, and CMA toggles $D_3$ each time.

questions.text:
Let $L=(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n)$, $n\ge0$ be a list whose Pascal representation is

```pascal
type list = record
  next : ↑list; val : integer end
```

The following function returns a list in which $a_{2i}$ and $a_{2i-1}$, $1\le i\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ are interchanged. Complete the function by filling in the boxes. Write the line number and the content of the box in your answer sheet.

```pascal
1  function change (p : ↑list) : ↑list;
2  var q, t : ↑list;
3  begin
4    if p = nil then change := p
5    else if p↑.next = nil then change := [ ]
6    else begin
7      q := p↑.next;
8      [ ] := q;
9      t := q↑.next;
10     [ ] := p;
11     [ ] := change(t)
12   end
13 end
```
questions.subject: pds
questions.answer: Line 5: p; Line 8: change; Line 10: q↑.next; Line 11: p↑.next
questions.solution: Single node returns itself; otherwise q (second node) becomes the new head, q↑.next points to p, and p↑.next is the recursively changed rest t.

questions.text:
Consider a graph whose vertices are points in the plane with integer co-ordinates (x, y) such that $1\le x\le n$ and $1\le y\le n$, where $n\ge2$ is an integer. Two vertices $(x_1,y_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)$ are adjacent iff $|x_1-x_2|\le1$ and $|y_1-y_2|\le1$. The weight of an edge $\{(x_1,y_1),(x_2,y_2)\}$ is $\sqrt{(x_1-x_2)^2+(y_1-y_2)^2}$.

(a) What is the weight of a minimum weight spanning tree in this graph? Write only the answer without any explanations.
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Edges have weight 1 (horizontal/vertical) or $\sqrt2$ (diagonal); the unit edges alone span the $n^2$ vertices, so the MST uses $n^2-1$ unit edges.
questions.reviewNote: The scan prints only '|x1 − x2| ≤ 1'; the full adjacency condition ('and |y1 − y2| ≤ 1') was taken from GeeksforGeeks/GATE Overflow.

questions.text:
Consider a graph whose vertices are points in the plane with integer co-ordinates (x, y) such that $1\le x\le n$ and $1\le y\le n$, where $n\ge2$ is an integer. Two vertices $(x_1,y_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)$ are adjacent iff $|x_1-x_2|\le1$ and $|y_1-y_2|\le1$. The weight of an edge $\{(x_1,y_1),(x_2,y_2)\}$ is $\sqrt{(x_1-x_2)^2+(y_1-y_2)^2}$.

(b) What is the weight of a maximum weight spanning tree in this graph? Write only the answer without any explanations.

questions.solution: Diagonal edges preserve the parity of x+y and connect each parity class, giving a spanning forest of 2 trees with $n^2-2$ edges of weight $\sqrt2$; one unit edge joins them.

questions.text:
Consider the grammar

$S\to bSe$

$S\to PQR$

$P\to bPc$

$P\to\varepsilon$

$Q\to cQd$

$Q\to\varepsilon$

$R\to dRe$

$R\to\varepsilon$

where S, P, Q, R are non-terminal symbols with S being the start symbol; b, c, d, e are terminal symbols and 'ε' is the empty string. This grammar generates strings of the form $b^ic^jd^ke^m$ for some $i,j,k,m\ge0$.

(a) What is the condition on the values of i, j, k, m?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: With s uses of $S\to bSe$ and p, q, r uses of the P, Q, R rules: $i=s+p$, $j=p+q$, $k=q+r$, $m=r+s$, so $i+k=j+m$ (and every such tuple is achievable).

(b) Find the smallest string that has two parse trees.

questions.text:
Consider a hash table with n buckets, where external (overflow) chaining is used to resolve collisions. The hash function is such that the probability that a key value is hashed to a particular bucket is $1/n$. The hash table is initially empty and K distinct values are inserted in the table.

(a) What is the probability that bucket number 1 is empty after the K th insertion?
questions.subject: prob
questions.solution: Each of the K keys independently misses bucket 1 with probability $(n-1)/n$.

questions.text:
Consider a hash table with n buckets, where external (overflow) chaining is used to resolve collisions. The hash function is such that the probability that a key value is hashed to a particular bucket is $1/n$. The hash table is initially empty and K distinct values are inserted in the table.

(b) What is the probability that no collision has occurred in any of the K insertions?
questions.subject: prob
questions.solution: The i-th key must go to one of the $n-i+1$ still-empty buckets: $\prod_{i=0}^{K-1}\frac{n-i}{n}$.

questions.text:
Consider a hash table with n buckets, where external (overflow) chaining is used to resolve collisions. The hash function is such that the probability that a key value is hashed to a particular bucket is $1/n$. The hash table is initially empty and K distinct values are inserted in the table.

questions.text:
An operating system handles requests to resources as follows.

A process (which asks for some resources, uses them for some time and then exits the system) is assigned a unique timestamp when it starts. The timestamps are monotonically increasing with time. Let us denote the timestamp of a process P by TS(P).

When a process P requests for a resource the OS does the following:

(i) If no other process is currently holding the resource, the OS awards the resource to P.

(ii) If some process Q with TS(Q) < TS(P) is holding the resource, the OS makes P wait for the resource.

(iii) If some process Q with TS(Q) > TS(P) is holding the resource, the OS restarts Q and awards the resource to P.

(Restarting means taking back the resources held by a process, killing it and starting it again with the same timestamp)

When a process releases a resource, the process with the smallest timestamp (if any) amongst those waiting for the resource is awarded the resource.

(a) Can a deadlock ever arise? If yes, show how. If not, prove it.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: A process only ever waits for a process with a smaller (older) timestamp, so any wait-for chain has strictly decreasing timestamps and cannot form a cycle.

(ii) If some process Q with TS(Q) < TS(P) is holding the resource, the OS makes P wait for the resource.

(iii) If some process Q with TS(Q) > TS(P) is holding the resource, the OS restarts Q and awards the resource to P.

(Restarting means taking back the resources held by a process, killing it and starting it again with the same timestamp)

When a process releases a resource, the process with the smallest timestamp (if any) amongst those waiting for the resource is awarded the resource.

(b) Can a process P ever starve? If yes, show how. If not, prove it.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: A restarted process keeps its timestamp; as older processes finish, P eventually becomes the oldest in the system, after which it is never restarted and is always preferred on release.

$$\frac{n(n-3)}{2}$$

questions.solution: Base n=3: 0 diagonals. Adding a vertex between two adjacent vertices adds n−2 new diagonals from it plus the old edge becoming a diagonal: n(n−3)/2 + (n−1) = (n+1)(n−2)/2.

questions.text: Let R be a binary relation on $A=\{a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h\}$ represented by following two component digraph. Find the smallest integers m and n such $m<n$ and $R^m=R^n$.

figures.alt: Directed graph with two components: a 3-cycle a→b→c→a, and a 5-cycle d→e→f→g→h→d.

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: R is a 3-cycle (a,b,c) plus a 5-cycle (d,e,f,g,h); R^k repeats with period lcm(3,5) = 15, so R^1 = R^16.

questions.text:
Suppose $A=\{a, b, c, d\}$ and $\Pi_1$ is the following partition of A

$\Pi_1=\{\{a, b, c\}, \{d\}\}$

List the ordered pairs of the equivalence relations induced by $\Pi_1$

### Option Analysis & Verification
- **Option {(a,a),(a,b),(a,c),(b,a),(b,b),(b,c),(c,a),(c,b),(c,c),(d,d)} (CORRECT):** Fully conforms to formal theoretical properties and algebraic evaluation.

questions.text:
Suppose $A=\{a, b, c, d\}$ and $\Pi_1$ is the following partition of A

$\Pi_1=\{\{a, b, c\}, \{d\}\}$

Draw the graph of the above equivalence relation
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Self-loops on all four vertices, a, b, c pairwise joined in both directions; d isolated apart from its loop.

questions.text:
Suppose $A=\{a, b, c, d\}$ and $\Pi_1$ is the following partition of A

$\Pi_1=\{\{a, b, c\}, \{d\}\}$

Let $\Pi_2=\{\{a\}, \{b\}, \{c\}, \{d\}\}$, $\Pi_3=\{\{a, b, c, d\}\}$ and $\Pi_4=\{\{a, b\}, \{c, d\}\}$

Draw a Poset diagram of the poset $\langle\{\Pi_1, \Pi_2, \Pi_3, \Pi_4\}, \text{refines}\rangle$
questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: Π2 at the bottom, Π1 and Π4 incomparable above it, Π3 at the top
questions.solution: Π2 refines every partition, every partition refines Π3; Π1 and Π4 do not refine each other.

questions.text:
Let $(A, *)$ be a semi-group. Furthermore, for every a and b in A, if $a\ne b$, then $a*b\ne b*a$.

Show that for every a in A

$a*a=a$
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: (a*a)*a = a*(a*a) by associativity; the hypothesis (contrapositive: x*y = y*x ⇒ x = y) gives a*a = a.

questions.text:
Let $(A, *)$ be a semi-group. Furthermore, for every a and b in A, if $a\ne b$, then $a*b\ne b*a$.

Show that for every a, b in A

$a*b*a=a$
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Using idempotence, (a*b*a)*a = a*b*a = a*(a*b*a), so a*b*a commutes with a and hence equals a.

questions.text:
Let $(A, *)$ be a semi-group. Furthermore, for every a and b in A, if $a\ne b$, then $a*b\ne b*a$.

Show that for every a, b, c in A

$a*b*c=a*c$
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Show (a*b*c)*(a*c) = (a*c)*(a*b*c) using part (b) (e.g. both reduce to a*c via a*x*a = a and c*y*c = c), hence a*b*c = a*c.

questions.text:
Let $M=(\{q_0, q_1\}, \{0,1\}, \{z_0, X\}, \delta, q_0, z_0, \phi)$ be a Pushdown automaton where $\delta$ is given by

$\delta(q_0, 1, z_0)=\{(q_0, Xz_0)\}$

$\delta(q_0, \epsilon, z_0)=\{(q_0, \epsilon)\}$

$\delta(q_0, 1, X)=\{(q_0, XX)\}$

$\delta(q_1, 1, X)=\{(q_1, \epsilon)\}$

$\delta(q_0, 0, z_0)=\{(q_1, X)\}$

$\delta(q_1, 0, z_0)=\{(q_0, z_0)\}$

What is the language accepted by this PDA by empty store?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: As printed, 0 can only be read with z0 on top, so after any 1 the X's can never be popped; this gives just {ε, 01}. If the fifth rule is δ(q0,0,X)={(q1,X)}, the PDA matches 1^n 0 1^n blocks separated by 0.
questions.reviewNote: Transitions as printed make the PDA almost trivial ({ε, 01}); the fifth rule is probably δ(q0,0,X) in the original. Answer left open.

questions.text:
Let $M=(\{q_0, q_1\}, \{0,1\}, \{z_0, X\}, \delta, q_0, z_0, \phi)$ be a Pushdown automaton where $\delta$ is given by

$\delta(q_0, 1, z_0)=\{(q_0, Xz_0)\}$

$\delta(q_0, \epsilon, z_0)=\{(q_0, \epsilon)\}$

$\delta(q_0, 1, X)=\{(q_0, XX)\}$

$\delta(q_1, 1, X)=\{(q_1, \epsilon)\}$

$\delta(q_0, 0, z_0)=\{(q_1, X)\}$

$\delta(q_1, 0, z_0)=\{(q_0, z_0)\}$

Describe informally the working of the PDA.
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: In q0 it pushes an X per 1; on 0 it moves to q1 and pops an X per 1, returning to q0 on 0 when the bottom marker is exposed and emptying the stack by ε-move.
questions.reviewNote: Depends on the intended transition function (see 65(a)).

questions.text:
Answer the following:

Let $G_1=(N, T, P, S_1)$ be a CFG where, $N=\{S_1, A, B\}$, $T=\{a, b\}$ and P is given by

$S_1\rightarrow aS_1b$, $S_1\rightarrow aBb$, $S_1\rightarrow aAb$, $B\rightarrow Bb$, $A\rightarrow aA$, $B\rightarrow b$, $A\rightarrow a$

What is $L(G_1)$?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: S1 wraps a^k…b^k around aB b (extra b's, j>i) or aAb (extra a's, i>j).

questions.text:
Let $G_1=(N, T, P, S_1)$ be a CFG where, $N=\{S_1, A, B\}$, $T=\{a, b\}$ and P is given by

$S_1\rightarrow aS_1b$, $S_1\rightarrow aBb$, $S_1\rightarrow aAb$, $B\rightarrow Bb$, $A\rightarrow aA$, $B\rightarrow b$, $A\rightarrow a$

Use the grammar in Part (a) to give a CFG for $L_2=\{a^ib^ja^kb^l \mid i, j, k, l\ge 1,\ i=j \text{ or } k=l\}$ by adding not more than 5 productions rules.
questions.subject: toc
questions.answer: S → E S1 | S1 E | E E; E → aEb | ab
questions.solution: E generates a^n b^n; S1 generates a^i b^j with i≠j; the three S-rules cover i=j only, k=l only, and both.

questions.text:
Let $G_1=(N, T, P, S_1)$ be a CFG where, $N=\{S_1, A, B\}$, $T=\{a, b\}$ and P is given by

$S_1\rightarrow aS_1b$, $S_1\rightarrow aBb$, $S_1\rightarrow aAb$, $B\rightarrow Bb$, $A\rightarrow aA$, $B\rightarrow b$, $A\rightarrow a$

Is $L_2$ inherently ambiguous?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Strings a^n b^n a^m b^m (i=j and k=l) can be derived via both alternatives; like {a^ib^jc^k | i=j or j=k}, L2 is inherently ambiguous.

questions.text:
Answer the following:

Draw the schematic of an 8085 based system that can be used to measure the width of a pulse. Assume that the pulse is given as a TTL compatible signal by the source which generates it.
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Feed the pulse to an input port bit (or SID / RST 7.5) and poll it; count loop iterations of known T-states while the pulse is high.

questions.text: Write the 8085 Assembly Language program to measure the width of the pulse. State all your assumptions clearly.
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Wait for the rising edge, increment a register pair in a fixed-length loop until the falling edge; width = count × loop time.

questions.text:
Design a synchronous counter to go through the following states:

1, 4, 2, 3, 1, 4, 2, 3, 1, 4, …
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Tabulate next states for 001, 100, 010, 011 and treat 000, 101, 110, 111 as don't-cares.

questions.text: Calculate the total time required to read 35 sectors on a 2 sided floppy disk. Assume that each track has 8 sectors and the track to track step time is 8 milliseconds. The first sector to be read is sector 3 on track 10. Assume that the diskette is soft sectored and the controller has a 1 sector buffer. The diskette spins at 300 RPM and initially, the head is on track 10
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: 300 RPM ⇒ 200 ms per revolution, 25 ms per sector; 35 sectors starting at sector 3 of track 10 span cylinders 10, 11 and 12 (14 + 16 + 5 sectors) with two track steps; total depends on assumptions about side switching and buffer-induced interleave.
questions.reviewNote: Answer depends on unstated assumptions (side switching, rotational latency, 1-sector buffer effect); not solved.

questions.text:
For a set-associative Cache Organization, the parameters are as follows

$t_c$ – Cache access time

$t_m$ – Main memory access time

$l$ – number of sets

b – block size

$k*b$ – set size

Calculate the hit ratio for a loop executed 100 times where the size of the loop is $n*b$, and $n=k*m$ is a non-zero integer and $1<m\le l$.

Give the value of the hit ratio for $l=1$.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: The loop spans n = k·m blocks mapped over the sets; whether blocks conflict depends on the mapping and replacement policy assumed.
questions.reviewNote: Problem statement is under-specified (mapping/replacement policy); answer not derived.

```c
q := p -> next
p -> next := q -> next
q -> next := (q -> next) -> next

```

$3 * \log(x+1) - a/2$

questions.text:
Draw the binary tree with node labels a, b, c, d, e, f and g for which the inorder and postorder transversals result in the following sequences.

Inorder: a f b c d g e

Postorder: a f c g e d b
questions.subject: pds
questions.answer: Root b; left subtree f with left child a; right subtree d with left child c and right child e, where e has left child g
questions.solution: Root = last of postorder (b); split inorder into {a,f} and {c,d,g,e} and recurse (roots f and d, then e).

Derive a recurrence relation of the size of the smallest AVL tree with height h.
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: A minimal AVL tree of height h has a root with minimal subtrees of heights h−1 and h−2.

questions.text: What is the size of the smallest AVL tree with height 8?

questions.solution: N: 1, 2, 4, 7, 12, 20, 33, 54, 88 for h = 0..8 (height of a single node = 0).
