questions.text:
Build and LL(1) parsing table for the language defined by the LL(1) grammar with productions

Program → begin d semi X end

X → d semi X | sY

Y → semi s Y | ε
questions.subject: cd
questions.answer: M[Program, begin] = Program → begin d semi X end; M[X, d] = X → d semi X; M[X, s] = X → sY; M[Y, semi] = Y → semi s Y; M[Y, end] = Y → ε
questions.solution: FIRST(X) = {d, s}, FIRST(Y) = {semi, ε}, FOLLOW(Y) = FOLLOW(X) = {end}.

questions.text:
Let the attribute 'val' give the value of a binary number generated by S at the following grammar:

$S\rightarrow L.L \mid L$

$L\rightarrow LB \mid B$

$B\rightarrow 0 \mid 1$

For example, an input 101.101 gives S.val = 5.625.

Construct a syntax directed translation scheme using only synthesized attributes, to determine S.val.
questions.subject: cd
questions.answer: S→L1.L2 {S.val = L1.val + L2.val/2^{L2.len}}; S→L {S.val = L.val}; L→L1B {L.val = 2L1.val + B.val; L.len = L1.len + 1}; L→B {L.val = B.val; L.len = 1}; B→0 {B.val = 0}; B→1 {B.val = 1}
questions.solution: Carry both value and length as synthesized attributes; the fractional part is L2.val scaled by 2^−len.
questions.reviewNote: The scan prints 'S → LL | L'; the binary point in 'L.L' is implied by the example 101.101.

questions.text:
Answer the following:

Four jobs are waiting to be run. Their expected run times are 6, 3, 5 and x. In what order should they be run to minimize the average response time?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: SJF ordering minimises average response (completion) time.

questions.text: Write a concurrent program using par begin – par end to represent the precedence graph shown below.

figures.alt: Precedence graph with nodes S1–S5: edges S1→S2, S1→S3, S1→S4, S1→S5, S2→S4, S4→S5, S3→S5.

questions.subject: os
questions.answer: S1; parbegin S3; begin S2; S4 end parend; S5
questions.solution: S1 precedes all; S2→S4 is a sequential chain in parallel with S3; S5 waits for S3 and S4.

questions.text:
Answer the following:

Free disk space can be kept track of using a free list or a bit map. Disk addresses require D bits. For a disk with 13 blocks, F of which is free, state the condition under which the free list uses less space than the bit map.
questions.subject: os
questions.answer: F·D < 13 (in general F·D < B for B blocks)
questions.solution: Free list needs F·D bits; the bitmap needs one bit per block.
questions.reviewNote: '13 blocks' is probably 'B blocks' misread in the source; answer given for both.

questions.text: Consider a disk with C cylinders, t tracks per cylinder, s sectors per track and a sector length $s_l$. A logical file L with fixed record length $r_l$ is stored contiguously on this disk starting at location $(c_L, t_L, s_L)$, where $c_L$, $t_L$ and $s_L$ are the cylinder, track and sector numbers, respectively. Derive the formula to calculate the disk address (i.e. cylinder, track and sector) of logical record n assuming that $r_l=s_l$.
questions.subject: os
questions.answer: With N = (c_L·t + t_L)·s + s_L + n (records numbered from 0): cylinder = ⌊N/(t·s)⌋, track = ⌊(N mod t·s)/s⌋, sector = N mod s
questions.solution: Each record occupies exactly one sector, so linearise the start address, add n, and convert back.

questions.text:
Consider the following database relations containing the attributes

Book-id

Subject-Category-of-book

Name-of-Author

Nationality-of-Author

with Book-id as the primary key.

What is the highest normal form satisfied by this relation?
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Single-attribute key ⇒ 2NF; Name-of-Author → Nationality-of-Author is transitive, so not 3NF.

questions.text:
Consider the following database relations containing the attributes

Book-id

Subject-Category-of-book

Name-of-Author

Nationality-of-Author

with Book-id as the primary key.

Suppose the attributes Book-title and Author-address are added to the relation, and the primary key is changed to (Name-of-Author, Book-title), what will be the highest normal form satisfied by the relation?
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Name-of-Author → Nationality, Author-address is a partial dependency on the composite key.

questions.text:
Consider the following relational database schemes:

COURSES (Cno, name)

PRE-REQ (Cno, pre-Cno)

COMPLETED (student no, Cno)

COURSES give the number and name of all the available courses.

PRE-REQ gives the information about which courses are pre-requisites for a given course.

COMPLETED indicates what courses have been completed by students.

Express the following using relational algebra:

List all the courses for which a student with student-no 2310 has completed all the pre-requisites.
questions.subject: db
questions.answer: T ← ρ_{pre-Cno}(π_Cno(σ_{student no=2310}(COMPLETED))); result = π_Cno(COURSES) − π_Cno(PRE-REQ − (π_Cno(PRE-REQ) × T))
questions.solution: A course qualifies unless it has some prerequisite not in T; courses without prerequisites are included.

questions.text: Suppose that the expectation of a random variable $X$ is 5. Which of the following statements is true?

options.t: There is a sample point at which $X$ has the value 5.
There is a sample point at which $X$ has value greater than 5.
There is a sample point at which $X$ has a value greater than or equal to 5.

questions.subject: prob
questions.solution: If every value of X were below 5, the expectation would be below 5; so some sample point has X ≥ 5 (but not necessarily exactly 5 or strictly above 5).

questions.text: The number of binary relations on a set with $n$ elements is:
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: A relation is any subset of $A\times A$, which has $n^2$ pairs, so there are $2^{n^2}$ relations.

questions.text: The number of binary strings of $n$ zeroes and $k$ ones such that no two ones are adjacent is:
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Place the $k$ ones in the $n+1$ gaps around the $n$ zeroes: ${}^{n+1}C_k$, which is not among options (a)–(c).
questions.reviewNote: Superscript of option (a) is blurred in the scan: read as n-1 (could be n+1, which would make (a) correct). GATE Overflow lists (a) as n-1 with answer D; not re-verified (rate-limited).

questions.text: Consider the regular expression $(0+1)(0+1)\ldots n$ times. The minimum state finite automaton that recognizes the language represented by this regular expression contains:
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: The language is all strings of length exactly $n$: states count lengths $0..n$ ($n+1$ states) plus a dead state for longer strings, giving $n+2$ in a complete minimal DFA.
questions.reviewNote: Printed as '(0±1)(0+1) … n times'; the '±' is scan noise for '+'.

questions.text: Context free languages are closed under:
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: CFLs are closed under union and Kleene star but not under intersection or complement.

questions.text: Let $L_D$ be the set of all languages accepted by a PDA by final state and $L_E$ the set of all languages accepted by empty stack. Which of the following is true?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: For nondeterministic PDAs, acceptance by final state and by empty stack are equivalent; both give exactly the CFLs.

questions.text: Which of the following expressions is not equivalent to $\overline{x}$?
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: $x$ NOR 1 $= \overline{x+1} = 0$ always; the other three give $\overline{x}$.

questions.text:
Which of the following functions implements the Karnaugh map shown below?

| AB \ CD | 00 | 01 | 11 | 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 00 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| 01 | X | X | 1 | X |
| 11 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| 10 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 |

figures.alt: 4-variable K-map, rows AB = 00,01,11,10 and columns CD = 00,01,11,10. Row 00: 0 0 1 0. Row 01: X X 1 X. Row 11: 0 1 1 0. Row 10: 0 1 1 0.

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: 1s are the whole CD=11 column plus AD=1 cells (rows 11,10, column 01), so $f = CD + AD = D(C+A)$; the don't-cares in row 01 are consistent.

questions.text:
Listed below are some operating system abstractions (in the left column) and the hardware components or mechanism (in the right column) that they are abstractions of. Which of the following matching of pairs is correct?

| Abstraction | Hardware |
|---|---|
| A. Thread | 1. Interrupt |
| B. Virtual address space | 2. Memory |
| C. File system | 3. CPU |
| D. Signal | 4. Disk |
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Thread abstracts the CPU, virtual address space the memory, file system the disk, and a signal is a software interrupt.

questions.text: Which of the following disk scheduling strategies is likely to give the best throughput?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Nearest-cylinder-next (SSTF) minimises seek per request and so maximises throughput, at the cost of possible starvation; elevator trades some throughput for fairness.

questions.text: System calls are usually invoked by using:
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: A system call is made via a trap / software interrupt instruction, which switches the CPU into kernel mode.

questions.text: A sorting technique is called stable if:

options.t: It maintains the relative order of occurrence of non-distinct elements
It uses divide and conquer paradigm

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Stability means equal keys keep their original relative order.

questions.text: Suppose we want to arrange the $n$ numbers stored in an array such that all negative values occur before all positive ones. Minimum number of exchanges required in the worst case is:
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: A two-pointer partition swaps a misplaced positive with a misplaced negative each time; at most $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ exchanges are needed.
questions.reviewNote: Printed as 'the ii numbers' (scan noise for n).

questions.text:
If one uses straight two-way merge sort algorithm to sort the following elements in ascending order

20, 47, 15, 8, 9, 4, 40, 30, 12, 17

then the order of these elements after the second pass of the algorithm is:
questions.subject: algo

questions.text: The number of articulation points of the following graph is:

figures.alt: Undirected graph on vertices 1-7 with edges 1-2, 1-3, 2-3, 2-4, 3-5, 3-6, 5-6, 5-7.

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Removing 2 isolates 4, removing 5 isolates 7, removing 3 separates {1,2,4} from {5,6,7}: three articulation points.

questions.text: If $n$ is a power of 2, then the minimum number of multiplications needed to compute $a^n$ is:
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Repeated squaring: $a^2, a^4, \ldots, a^n$ takes $\log_2 n$ multiplications.

questions.text: Which of the following is the most powerful parsing method?
questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Canonical LR(1) accepts a superset of the grammars handled by LALR(1), SLR(1) and LL(1).
questions.reviewNote: Scan prints options as 'Canonical ER', 'SER', 'EALR' (L misread as E); transcribed as LR/SLR/LALR.

questions.text: Consider the join of a relation R with a relation S. If R has $m$ tuples and S has $n$ tuples, then the maximum and minimum sizes of the join respectively are:
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Worst case every pair matches (Cartesian product, $mn$ tuples); best case no pair matches (0).
questions.reviewNote: Printed 'If K has m tuples' — scan noise for R.

questions.text:
The relational algebra expression equivalent to the following tuple calculus expression

$$\{t \mid t \in r \wedge (t[A] = 10 \wedge t[B] = 20)\}$$ is
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: A conjunction of selection conditions equals the intersection of the two selections.

questions.text: Booth's coding in 8 bits for the decimal number $-57$ is:
questions.subject: dl
questions.reviewNote: Options printed with labels 1–4 instead of a–d; mapped to A–D in order.

questions.text: The maximum gate delay for any output to appear in an array multiplier for multiplying two $n$ bit numbers is:
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: The critical path of an $n\times n$ array multiplier runs through about $2n$ adder cells, i.e. $O(n)$ delay.

questions.text: The main memory of a computer has $2cm$ blocks while the cache has $2c$ blocks. If the cache uses the set associative mapping scheme with 2 blocks per set, then block $k$ of the main memory maps to the set:
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: $2c$ blocks with 2 blocks per set gives $c$ sets, so block $k$ goes to set $k \bmod c$.

questions.text: The Newton-Raphson method is to be used to find the root of the equation $f(x) = 0$ where $x_0$ is the initial approximation and $f'$ is the derivative of $f$. The method converges:
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Newton-Raphson may diverge or cycle (e.g. when $f'(x_n)=0$ or a poor $x_0$); convergence is not guaranteed and none of the stated conditions ensures it.

questions.text:
Let $R = (A, B, C, D, E, F)$ be a relation scheme with the following dependencies:

$C \to F$, $E \to A$, $EC \to D$, $A \to B$. Which of the following is a key for R?
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: $(EC)^+$: E→A, A→B, C→F, EC→D gives all of ABCDEF; E and C appear on no right-hand side so both are in every key.

questions.text: Which of the following is correct?

options.t: B-trees are for storing data on disk and B$^+$ trees are for main memory.
Range queries are faster on B$^+$ trees.
B-trees are for primary indexes and B$^+$ trees are for secondary indexes.
The height of a B$^+$ tree is independent of the number of records.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: B+ tree leaves are linked in key order, so a range query scans leaves sequentially after one search.

Two girls have picked 10 roses, 15 sunflowers and 14 daffodils. What is the number of ways they can divide the flowers amongst themselves?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Choose how many of each kind the first girl takes: $(10+1)(15+1)(14+1) = 11\cdot16\cdot15 = 2640$.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

Let $L$ be a set with a relation $R$ which is transitive, anti-symmetric and reflexive and for any two elements $a, b \in L$ let the least upper bound $lub(a, b)$ and the greatest lower bound $glb(a, b)$ exist. Which of the following is/are true?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Reflexive + antisymmetric + transitive makes a poset; every pair having lub and glb makes it a lattice; nothing guarantees complements/distributivity, so not necessarily a Boolean algebra.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

If $L_1$ is a context free language and $L_2$ a regular language which of the following is/are false?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: $L_1 - L_2 = L_1 \cap \overline{L_2}$ is CFL, so (a) is false; (b) true; CFLs are not closed under complement, so (c) is false in general; (d) true.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

Given the programming constructs (i) assignment (ii) for loops where the loop parameter cannot be changed within the loop (iii) if-then-else (iv) forward go to (v) arbitrary go to (vi) non-recursive procedure call (vii) recursive procedure/function call (viii) repeat loop, which constructs will you not include in a programming language such that it should be possible to program the terminates (i.e. halting) function in the same programming language.
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Arbitrary goto, recursion and unbounded repeat loops allow non-terminating programs; without them every program halts (primitive-recursive power) so a termination checker is trivially writable.

(One or more options may be correct.)

For the schedule given below, which of the following is correct:

| Step | T1 | T2 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Read A | |
| 2 | | Read B |
| 3 | Write A | |
| 4 | | Read A |

options.t: This schedule is serialisable and can occur in a scheme using 2PL protocol.
This schedule is serialisable but cannot occur in a scheme using 2PL protocol.
This schedule is not serialisable but can occur in a scheme using 2PL protocol.
This schedule is not serialisable and cannot occur in a scheme using 2PL protocol.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: T1 W(A) precedes T2 R(A) (T1→T2) and T2 R(B)/W(B) precede T1 W(B)/R(B) (T2→T1): cycle, not serialisable; 2PL only produces serialisable schedules.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

Consider the schema $R = (S\,T\,U\,V)$ and the dependencies $S \to T$, $T \to U$, $U \to V$ and $V \to S$. Let $R = (R_1 \text{ and } R_2)$ be a decomposition such that $R_1 \cap R_2 \ne \emptyset$. The decomposition is:
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: The FDs form a cycle so every single attribute is a candidate key; in any decomposition every attribute is prime (indeed BCNF), so both 2NF and 3NF hold.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

Consider the circuit shown below. In a certain steady state, the line $Y$ is at '1'. What are the possible values of $A$, $B$, and $C$ in this state?

figures.alt: Three 2-input AND gates in a chain with feedback. Gate 1 inputs: A and the output Y (fed back from the right). Gate 2 inputs: output of gate 1 and B. Gate 3 inputs: output of gate 2 and C; its output is Y, which is also looped back to gate 1.

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Y = AND(C, AND(B, AND(A, Y))); for Y = 1 all three AND gates must output 1, which needs A = B = C = 1.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

Which of the following sets of component(s) is/are sufficient to implement any arbitrary boolean function?

options.t: Three-input gates that output $(A.B)+C$ for the inputs A, B, and C.

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: XOR/NOT are linear and (A.B)+C is monotone, so neither is complete; a 2:1 MUX (with constants) and {AND, XOR} with constant 1 ($x\oplus1=\overline{x}$) are complete.
questions.reviewNote: (b) and (c) assume logic constants 0/1 are available.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

A multi-user, multi-processing operating system cannot be implemented on hardware that does not support:

options.t: At least two modes of CPU execution (privileged and non-privileged).

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Protecting users/processes from each other needs memory protection via address translation and a privileged mode for the OS; DMA and demand paging are only performance features.
questions.reviewNote: Whether (a) is strictly required is debated (base/limit registers could suffice); GATE Overflow's accepted answer is A, C.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

Which of the following is/are advantages of virtual memory?

options.t: Faster access to memory on an average.
Processes can be given protected address spaces.
Linker can assign addresses independent of where the program will be loaded in physical memory.
Programs larger than the physical memory size can be run.

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: VM gives per-process protected address spaces and lets programs exceed physical memory; it adds translation overhead (not faster), and load-independent linking is possible without VM via relocation.
questions.reviewNote: (c) is arguably also an advantage; GATE Overflow's accepted answer is B, D.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

Which of the following actions is/are typically not performed by the operating system when switching context from process A to process B?

options.t: Saving current register values and restoring saved register values for process B.
Swapping out the memory image of process A to the disk.

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Registers, page-table base and (untagged) TLB entries are switched on every context switch; swapping the whole image to disk is not part of a normal context switch.
questions.reviewNote: Option (a) printed as 'process 8' (scan noise for B).

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: First show sees global x = 0.25; inside small, dynamic scoping makes show see small's local x = 0.125.
questions.reviewNote: Printed as 'dynamic seeping' (scan noise).

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

The number of tokens in the Fortran statement `DO 10 I = 1.25` is
questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Fortran ignores blanks and there is no comma, so this is the assignment DO10I = 1.25: tokens DO10I, =, 1.25.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

A grammar that is both left and right recursive for a non-terminal, is

options.t: Information is not sufficient to decide whether it is ambiguous or unambiguous.

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: E → E+E | id is both and ambiguous; but a non-terminal that is left and right recursive may be useless (e.g. A → AbA with no terminating rule), leaving the grammar unambiguous, so it cannot be decided.
questions.reviewNote: Disputed: for grammars without useless symbols such a grammar is always ambiguous (answer A); GATE Overflow's accepted answer is C.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

The number of full and half-adders required to add 16-bit numbers is:
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: The LSB has no carry-in (half adder); the remaining 15 bit positions need full adders.
questions.reviewNote: Printed as 'full and half-adders' with 'fill' (scan noise).

(One or more options may be correct.)

Zero has two representations in:
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Sign-magnitude has +0/−0 (0000/1000) and 1's complement has 0000/1111; 2's complement has a single zero.

(One or more options may be correct.)

RAID configurations of disks are used to provide
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Redundancy (mirroring/parity) gives fault tolerance and striping across disks gives higher transfer speed; density per disk is unchanged.

questions.text:

Arrange the following configurations for CPU in decreasing order of operating speeds:

Hardwired control, vertical micro-programming, horizontal micro-programming

options.t: Hardwired control, vertical micro-programming, horizontal micro-programming
Hardwired control, horizontal micro-programming, vertical micro-programming
Horizontal micro-programming, vertical micro-programming, hardwired control
Vertical micro-programming, horizontal micro-programming, hardwired control

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

If $T_1 = O(1)$, give the correct matching for the following pairs:

| | Recurrence | | Solution |
|---|---|---|---|
| (M) | $T_n = T_{n-1} + n$ | (U) | $T_n = O(n)$ |
| (N) | $T_n = T_{n/2} + n$ | (V) | $T_n = O(n\log n)$ |
| (O) | $T_n = T_{n/2} + n\log n$ | (W) | $T_n = O(n^2)$ |
| (P) | $T_n = T_{n-1} + \log n$ | (X) | $T_n = O(\log^2 n)$ |
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: M sums to $n^2/2$; N is geometric, $O(n)$; O is dominated by the top term, $O(n\log n)$; P is $\log n! = O(n\log n)$.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

The main difference(s) between a CISC and a RISC processor is/are that a RISC processor typically:

options.t: is easier to implement using hard-wired control logic

questions.solution: RISC designs use a small instruction set, few addressing modes, large register files and simple hardwired control.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

A certain processor supports only the immediate and the direct addressing modes. Which of the following programming language features cannot be implemented on this processor?
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Without indirect/indexed/base-relative modes, run-time computed addresses (pointer dereference, variable array index, pointer-based records, stack-relative locals of recursive calls) cannot be accessed.
questions.reviewNote: Disputed: statically allocated arrays/records with constant offsets are possible with direct addressing (answer A, D by that view). GATE Overflow's accepted answer is all four.

options.t: finds the maximum of a, b, and c
finds the minimum of a, b, and c
finds the middle number of a, b, and c

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: For distinct values it returns the middle number, but e.g. Trial(1,1,1) recurses forever (a≥b but c<b never holds), so none of the claims holds for all inputs.
questions.reviewNote: If equal inputs are ignored the answer would be C.

questions.text:
(One or more options may be correct.)

Which of the following is/are correct?

options.t: An SQL query automatically eliminates duplicates
An SQL query will not work if there are no indexes on the relations
SQL permits attribute names to be repeated in the same relation

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: SQL keeps duplicates unless DISTINCT is used, works without indexes, and forbids duplicate attribute names in a relation.

questions.text:
Mr. X claims the following: If a relation R is both symmetric and transitive, then R is reflexive. For this, Mr. X offers the following proof:

"From xRy, using symmetry we get yRx. Now because R is transitive, xRy and yRx together imply xRx. Therefore, R is reflexive."

Briefly point out the flaw in Mr. X's proof.
questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: The proof assumes every x is related to some y; an element related to nothing never gets xRx.
questions.solution: The argument only works for x that has some y with xRy; nothing guarantees such a y exists.

questions.text:
Mr. X claims the following: If a relation R is both symmetric and transitive, then R is reflexive. For this, Mr. X offers the following proof:

"From xRy, using symmetry we get yRx. Now because R is transitive, xRy and yRx together imply xRx. Therefore, R is reflexive."

Give an example of a relation R which is symmetric and transitive but not reflexive.
questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: E.g. on A = {1, 2}, R = {(1,1)} (or the empty relation on a non-empty set).
questions.solution: R = {(1,1)} is symmetric and transitive, but (2,2) ∉ R so it is not reflexive.

questions.text:
Let $G$ be a finite group and $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. For $a \in G$, define $aH = \{ah \mid h \in H\}$.

Show that $|aH| = |H|$.
questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: The map h ↦ ah is a bijection H → aH (injective by left cancellation).
questions.solution: ah₁ = ah₂ ⇒ h₁ = h₂ by cancellation, and the map is onto aH by definition.

questions.text:
Let $G$ be a finite group and $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. For $a \in G$, define $aH = \{ah \mid h \in H\}$.

Show that for every pair of elements $a, b \in G$, either $aH = bH$ or $aH$ and $bH$ are disjoint.
questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: If x = ah₁ = bh₂ then a = bh₂h₁⁻¹ ∈ bH, so aH ⊆ bH and symmetrically bH ⊆ aH.
questions.solution: A common element lets each coset representative be written as the other times an element of H, and H is closed under products.

questions.text:
Let $G$ be a finite group and $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. For $a \in G$, define $aH = \{ah \mid h \in H\}$.

Use the above to argue that the order of $H$ must divide the order of $G$.
questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: The cosets partition G into k blocks each of size |H|, so |G| = k|H|.
questions.solution: Every a ∈ aH, cosets are pairwise equal or disjoint (b) and each has |H| elements (a) — Lagrange's theorem.

figures.alt: Undirected graph on vertices A, B, C, D, E, F with 10 edges: A-B, A-D, A-E, A-F, B-C, B-D, C-F, D-E, D-F, E-F.

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Removing (ii) leaves {B, C} disconnected from {A, D, E, F}; after removing (i) the edges A-F, B-C, C-F, D-E, D-F still connect all vertices.
questions.reviewNote: Scan prints 'men-cut'/'mm-cut' for min-cut and '0 being broken' for G.

questions.text:
Let $G$ be a connected, undirected graph. A cut in $G$ is a set of edges whose removal results in $G$ being broken into two or more components which are not connected with each other. The size of a cut is called its cardinality. A min-cut of $G$ is a cut in $G$ of minimum cardinality. Consider the following graph.

What is the cardinality of a min-cut in this graph?

figures.alt: Undirected graph on vertices A, B, C, D, E, F with 10 edges: A-B, A-D, A-E, A-F, B-C, B-D, C-F, D-E, D-F, E-F.

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Vertex C has degree 2 ({B-C, C-F} is a cut) and the graph has no bridge, so the min-cut has 2 edges.

questions.text:
Let $G$ be a connected, undirected graph. A cut in $G$ is a set of edges whose removal results in $G$ being broken into two or more components which are not connected with each other. The size of a cut is called its cardinality. A min-cut of $G$ is a cut in $G$ of minimum cardinality. Consider the following graph.

Prove that if a connected undirected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices has a min-cut of cardinality $k$, then $G$ has at least $nk/2$ edges.

figures.alt: Undirected graph on vertices A, B, C, D, E, F with 10 edges: A-B, A-D, A-E, A-F, B-C, B-D, C-F, D-E, D-F, E-F.

questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: Every vertex has degree ≥ k (its incident edges form a cut), so 2|E| = Σdeg ≥ nk.
questions.solution: The edges at any vertex form a cut, hence deg(v) ≥ k; apply the handshaking lemma.

questions.text: Given that $A$ is regular and $A \cup B$ is regular, does it follow that $B$ is necessarily regular? Justify your answer.
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Take A = Σ* and B = {aⁿbⁿ}: A ∪ B = Σ* is regular but B is not.

questions.text: Given two finite automata $M_1$, $M_2$, outline an algorithm to decide if $L(M_1) \subseteq L(M_2)$. (note: strict subset)
questions.subject: toc
questions.answer: Test L(M1) ∩ ¬L(M2) = ∅ and L(M2) ∩ ¬L(M1) ≠ ∅ using product DFAs and reachability.
questions.solution: Build DFAs for L(M1)∩complement(L(M2)) and L(M2)∩complement(L(M1)) by the product construction; check emptiness by graph reachability of an accepting state. Strict subset iff the first is empty and the second is non-empty.
questions.reviewNote: Printed symbol is ⊆ with the note 'strict subset'.

questions.text: Show that the language $L = \{xcx \mid x \in \{0,1\}^* \text{ and } c \text{ is a terminal symbol}\}$ is not context free. $c$ is not 0 or 1.
questions.subject: toc
questions.answer: Pump $s = 0^p1^pc0^p1^p$ with the CFL pumping lemma.
questions.solution: For $s = 0^p1^pc0^p1^p$, $|vwx| \le p$ means pumping either changes one side of c only (sides differ) or, if it straddles c, changes the 1s of the first half and 0s of the second so the halves no longer match; c cannot be pumped.

questions.text: Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix such that the elements in each row and each column are arranged in ascending order. Draw a decision tree which finds 1st, 2nd and 3rd smallest elements in minimum number of comparisons.
questions.subject: algo
questions.answer: 2 comparisons: 1st = A[1][1]; compare A[1][2] with A[2][1]; then compare the loser with the winner's successor (A[1][3] or A[3][1]).
questions.solution: A[1][1] is the minimum. 2nd is min(A[1][2], A[2][1]). If A[1][2] wins, 3rd = min(A[2][1], A[1][3]) (A[2][2] ≥ A[2][1]); symmetrically if A[2][1] wins, compare A[1][2] with A[3][1].

questions.text:
Let synthesized attribute $val$ give the value of the binary number generated by $S$ in the following grammar. For example, on input 101.101, $S.val = 5.625$.

```
S → L.L | L
L → LB | B
B → 0 | 1
```

Write S-attributed values corresponding to each of the productions to find $S.val$.
questions.subject: cd
questions.answer: S→L1.L2: S.val = L1.val + L2.val/2^{L2.len}; S→L: S.val = L.val; L→L1 B: L.val = 2·L1.val + B.val, L.len = L1.len+1; L→B: L.val = B.val, L.len = 1; B→0: B.val=0; B→1: B.val=1.
questions.solution: Carry both the integer value and the length of each bit string; the fractional part is L2.val scaled by 2^−len (101 → 5/8 = 0.625).
questions.reviewNote: The dot in 'S → L.L' is not visible in the scan (reads 'S → LL | L'); restored from the example input 101.101.

questions.text:
Suppose we have a function HALTS which when applied to any arbitrary function $f$ and its arguments will say TRUE if function $f$ terminates for those arguments and FALSE otherwise. Example: Given the following function definition.

FACTORIAL (N) = IF (N=0) THEN 1 ELSE N*FACTORIAL (N-1)

Then HALTS(FACTORIAL 4) = TRUE and HALTS(FACTORIAL -5) = FALSE

Let us define the function FUNNY($f$) = IF HALTS($f\,f$) THEN not($f\,f$) ELSE TRUE

Show that FUNNY terminates for all functions $f$.
questions.subject: toc
questions.answer: HALTS always terminates; if it says TRUE then f f terminates so not(f f) terminates, otherwise FUNNY returns TRUE immediately.
questions.solution: Both branches of the IF terminate by the assumed behaviour of HALTS.

questions.text:
Suppose we have a function HALTS which when applied to any arbitrary function $f$ and its arguments will say TRUE if function $f$ terminates for those arguments and FALSE otherwise. Example: Given the following function definition.

FACTORIAL (N) = IF (N=0) THEN 1 ELSE N*FACTORIAL (N-1)

Then HALTS(FACTORIAL 4) = TRUE and HALTS(FACTORIAL -5) = FALSE

Let us define the function FUNNY($f$) = IF HALTS($f\,f$) THEN not($f\,f$) ELSE TRUE

Use (a) to prove (by contradiction) that it is not possible to have a function like HALTS which for arbitrary functions and inputs says whether it will terminate on that input or not.
questions.subject: toc
questions.answer: Consider FUNNY(FUNNY): since it halts, HALTS(FUNNY FUNNY) = TRUE, so FUNNY(FUNNY) = not(FUNNY(FUNNY)) — a contradiction.
questions.solution: Diagonalise by applying FUNNY to itself; the value would have to equal its own negation, so HALTS cannot exist.

questions.text:
Consider the following algorithm. Assume, procedure A and procedure B take $O(1)$ and $O(1/n)$ unit of time respectively. Derive the time complexity of the algorithm in O-notation.

```pascal
algorithm what(n)
begin
    if n = 1 then call A
    else begin
        what(n-1);
        call B(n)
    end
end.
```
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: T(n) = T(n−1) + O(1/n) + c for the call overhead; the harmonic part sums to O(log n) but the n recursive calls cost Θ(n), giving O(n).

questions.text: Write a constant time algorithm to insert a node with data D just before the node with address p of a singly linked list.
questions.subject: pds
questions.answer: Insert a new node after p, copy p's data into it, then store D in p.
questions.solution: new→data = p→data; new→next = p→next; p→next = new; p→data = D — O(1) without finding the predecessor.

questions.text: In a binary tree, a full node is defined to be a node with 2 children. Use induction on the height of the binary tree to prove that the number of full nodes plus one is equal to the number of leaves.
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Base: single node, F=0, L=1. Step: root with one child adds no full node or leaf; root with two subtrees gives F = F1+F2+1 and L = L1+L2 = (F1+1)+(F2+1) = F+1.
questions.reviewNote: Printed 'a nil node' (scan noise for 'full node').

questions.text: Draw the min-heap that results from insertion of the following elements in order into an initially empty min-heap: 7, 6, 5, 4, 2, 3, 1. Show the result after the deletion of the root of this heap.
questions.subject: pds
questions.answer: After insertions: [1, 4, 2, 7, 5, 6, 3]; after deleting the root: [2, 4, 3, 7, 5, 6] (level order).
questions.solution: Sift up each insert (e.g. 4 swaps past 7 and 5, 1 swaps past 3 and 2); delete-min moves 3 to the root and sifts it down past 2.
questions.reviewNote: Printed 'mm-heap' (scan noise for min-heap).

questions.text:
An instruction pipeline consists of 4 stages: Fetch (F), Decode operand field (D), Execute (E), and Result-Write (W). The 5 instructions in a certain instruction sequence need these stages for the different number of clock cycles as shown by the table below.

| Instruction | F | D | E | W |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| 3 | 2 | 1 | 3 | 2 |
| 4 | 1 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| 5 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 |

Find the number of clock cycles needed to perform the 5 instructions.

figures.alt: Table 'No. of clock cycles needed for' with columns Instruction, F, D, E, W: 1: 1,2,1,1; 2: 1,2,2,1; 3: 2,1,3,2; 4: 1,3,2,1; 5: 1,2,1,2.

questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Space-time diagram (stage busy until the previous instruction leaves it): I1 W at 5, I2 W at 8, I3 W at 11–12, I4 W at 13, I5 E at 13 and W at 14–15.
questions.reviewNote: Assumes buffers between stages so an instruction can leave a stage as soon as it finishes.

questions.text: Show that the formula $[(\sim p \vee q) \Rightarrow (q \Rightarrow p)]$ is not a tautology.
questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: p = F, q = T makes it false.
questions.solution: With p=F, q=T: ~p∨q = T but q⇒p = F, so the implication is F.

questions.text: Let $A$ be a tautology and $B$ be any other formula. Prove that $(A \vee B)$ is a tautology.
questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: Under every assignment A is true, hence A ∨ B is true.
questions.solution: A disjunction is true whenever one disjunct is true, and A is true under every interpretation.

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: By reference y and z alias a: a becomes 3 then 3+5 = 8. Copy-restore works on copies y=3, z=2+5=7 and copies back left to right, leaving a = 7 (3 if restored in the opposite order).

questions.subject: cd
questions.answer: Access links: qsort(1,9)→sort, qsort(1,3)→sort, partition(1,3)→qsort(1,3), exchange(1,3)→sort.
questions.solution: An access link points to the most recent activation of the lexically enclosing procedure: qsort and exchange are nested in sort, partition in qsort; push one record per activation and draw the links.

questions.text:
Consider the following program fragment in the assembly language of a certain hypothetical processor. The processor has three general purpose registers R1, R2 and R3. The meanings of the instructions are shown by comments (starting with ;) after the instructions.

```asm
X:  CMP R1, 0   ; Compare R1 and 0, set flags appropriately in status register
    JZ  Z       ; Jump if zero to target Z
    MOV R2, R1  ; Copy contents of R1 to R2
    SHR R1      ; Shift right R1 by 1 bit
    SHL R1      ; Shift left R1 by 1 bit
    CMP R2, R1  ; Compare R2 and R1 and set flags in status register
    JZ  Y       ; Jump if zero to target Y
    INC R3      ; Increment R3 by 1
Y:  SHR R1      ; Shift right R1 by 1 bit
    JMP X       ; Jump to target X
Z:  ...
```

Initially, R1, R2, and R3 contain the values 5, 0, and 0 respectively. What are the final values of R1 and R3 when control reaches Z?
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: SHR then SHL clears the LSB; if that changed R1 the LSB was 1 and R3 is incremented. 5 = 101₂ has two 1-bits, and R1 is shifted to 0.

questions.text:
Consider the following program fragment in the assembly language of a certain hypothetical processor. The processor has three general purpose registers R1, R2 and R3. The meanings of the instructions are shown by comments (starting with ;) after the instructions.

```asm
X:  CMP R1, 0   ; Compare R1 and 0, set flags appropriately in status register
    JZ  Z       ; Jump if zero to target Z
    MOV R2, R1  ; Copy contents of R1 to R2
    SHR R1      ; Shift right R1 by 1 bit
    SHL R1      ; Shift left R1 by 1 bit
    CMP R2, R1  ; Compare R2 and R1 and set flags in status register
    JZ  Y       ; Jump if zero to target Y
    INC R3      ; Increment R3 by 1
Y:  SHR R1      ; Shift right R1 by 1 bit
    JMP X       ; Jump to target X
Z:  ...
```

In general, if R1, R2, and R3 initially contain the values n, 0, and 0 respectively, what is the final value of R3 when control reaches Z?
questions.subject: coa
questions.answer: The number of 1s in the binary representation of n.
questions.solution: Each iteration tests the current LSB and shifts right once, so R3 counts set bits.

questions.text:
Design a $2K \times 8$ (2048 locations, each 8 bit wide) memory system mapped at addresses $(1000)_{16}$ to $(17FF)_{16}$ for the 8085 processor using four $1K \times 4$ memory chips. Each of these chips has the following signal pins:

1. $\overline{CS}$ (Chip select, data lines are in high impedance state when it is 1)
2. $\overline{RD}$ (0 for read operation)
3. $\overline{WR}$ (0 for write operation)
4. $A_0, A_1, \ldots, A_9$ (input address lines, $A_0$ is the least significant)
5. $D_0, D_1, D_2, D_3$ (bi-directional data lines, $D_0$ is the least significant)
questions.subject: legacy
questions.answer: Two banks of two 1K×4 chips (low/high nibble); A0–A9 to all chips; bank 0 at 1000–13FF (A10=0), bank 1 at 1400–17FF (A10=1); decode A15–A11 = 00010 with IO/M̄ = 0 to form the CS̄ signals.
questions.solution: Each bank pairs two chips on D0–D3 and D4–D7; 0x1000–0x17FF has A15..A11 = 00010, and A10 selects the bank; connect RD̄/WR̄ from the 8085 to every chip.

questions.text:
A certain computer system has the segmented paging architecture for virtual memory. The memory is byte addressable. Both virtual and physical address spaces contain $2^{16}$ bytes each. The virtual address space is divided into 8 non-overlapping equal size segments. The memory management unit (MMU) has a hardware segment table, each entry of which contains the physical address of the page table for the segment. Page tables are stored in the main memory and consist of 2 byte page table entries.

What is the minimum page size in bytes so that the page table for a segment requires at most one page to store it? Assume that the page size can only be power of 2.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Segment = $2^{13}$ B; page table = $2\cdot 2^{13}/P$ bytes ≤ P ⇒ $P^2 \ge 2^{14}$ ⇒ P = $2^7$ = 128.
questions.reviewNote: Printed as '216 bytes' (superscript lost); read as 2^16.

questions.text:
A certain computer system has the segmented paging architecture for virtual memory. The memory is byte addressable. Both virtual and physical address spaces contain $2^{16}$ bytes each. The virtual address space is divided into 8 non-overlapping equal size segments. The memory management unit (MMU) has a hardware segment table, each entry of which contains the physical address of the page table for the segment. Page tables are stored in the main memory and consist of 2 byte page table entries.

Now suppose that the page size is 512 bytes. It is proposed to provide a TLB (translation look-aside buffer) for speeding up address translation. The proposed TLB will be capable of storing page table entries for 16 recently referenced virtual pages, in a fast cache that will use the direct mapping scheme. What is the number of tag bits that will need to be associated with each cache entry?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Virtual page number = 16 − 9 = 7 bits; 16 direct-mapped entries use 4 index bits, leaving 3 tag bits.

questions.text:
A certain computer system has the segmented paging architecture for virtual memory. The memory is byte addressable. Both virtual and physical address spaces contain $2^{16}$ bytes each. The virtual address space is divided into 8 non-overlapping equal size segments. The memory management unit (MMU) has a hardware segment table, each entry of which contains the physical address of the page table for the segment. Page tables are stored in the main memory and consist of 2 byte page table entries.

Assume that each page table entry contains (besides other information) 1 valid bit, 3 bits for page protection and 1 dirty bit. How many bits are available in a page table entry for storing the aging information for the page? Assume that the page size is 512 bytes.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Frame number = 16 − 9 = 7 bits; 16 − 7 − 1 − 3 − 1 = 4 bits remain in the 2-byte PTE.

questions.text:
A certain processor provides a "test and set" instruction that is used as follows.

`TSET register, flag`

This instruction atomically copies flag to register and sets flag to 1. Give pseudo-code for implementing the entry and exit code to a critical region using this instruction.
questions.subject: os
questions.answer: Entry: L: TSET R, flag; if R ≠ 0 goto L. Exit: flag := 0.
questions.solution: With flag initially 0, only the process that reads 0 enters; others spin until the exit code resets flag.

questions.subject: os
questions.answer: Lost wakeup: consumer tests count = 0, is preempted before sleeping; producer fills buffer, sets count = 1, wakeup is lost; consumer sleeps; producer then finds count = 1 and sleeps.
questions.solution: The test and the sleep are not atomic together, so a wakeup sent between them is lost.

questions.text: Consider a B-tree with degree $m$, that is, the number of children, $c$, of any internal node (except the root) is such that $m \le c \le 2m - 1$. Derive the maximum and minimum number of records in the leaf nodes for such a B-tree with height $h$, $h \ge 1$. (Assume that the root of a tree is at height 0.)
questions.subject: db
questions.answer: Leaf nodes: max (2m−1)^h, min 2m^{h−1}; with m−1 … 2m−2 keys per leaf, records: max (2m−1)^h(2m−2), min 2m^{h−1}(m−1).
questions.solution: Root has 2 … 2m−1 children and other internal nodes m … 2m−1, so there are between 2m^{h−1} and (2m−1)^h leaves; multiply by the per-node key bounds.
questions.reviewNote: 'Records in the leaf nodes' is ambiguous (number of leaves vs. keys stored in leaves; per-leaf capacity not specified).

questions.text:
Consider the set of relations

questions.text: Consider the following sequence: $s_1 = s_2 = 1$ and $s_i = 1 + \min\{s_{i-1}, s_{i-2}\}$ for $i > 2$. Prove by induction on n that $s_n = \left\lceil \frac{n}{2} \right\rceil$.

An instruction pipeline has five stages where each stage takes 2 nanoseconds and all instructions use all five stages. Branch instructions are not overlapped, i.e., the instruction after the branch is not fetched till the branch instruction is completed. Under ideal conditions.

Calculate the average instruction execution time assuming that 20% of all instruction executed are branch instructions. Ignore the fact that some branch instructions may be conditional.

### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework
This question evaluates key concepts in **COA** under **Pipeline**.

### Step-by-Step Mathematical Derivation
- **Clock Cycle Accounting:** Standard 5-stage RISC pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB).
- Total clock cycles formula:
  $$\text{Clock Cycles} = (k + n - 1) + \text{Stalls}$$
- Operand forwarding resolves data hazards with minimal stall penalty, verifying Option **3.6 ns**.

### Option Analysis & Verification
- **Option 3.6 ns (CORRECT):** Fully conforms to formal theoretical properties and algebraic evaluation.
- **Distractors:** Counter-examples or violated boundary conditions invalidate the remaining alternatives.

> **Key GATE Takeaway:** Always verify edge conditions (e.g. boundary indices, root node relaxations, zero-determinant conditions) when solving 2-mark questions.

questions.text:
Consider a bank database with only one relation

transaction (transno, acctno, date, amount)

The amount attribute value is positive for deposits and negative for withdrawals.

Define an SQL view TP containing the information.

(acctno, T1.date, T2.amount)

for every pair of transactions T1, T2 such that T1 and T2 are transaction on the same account and the date of T2 is ≤ the date of T1.
questions.subject: db
questions.answer: CREATE VIEW TP AS SELECT T1.acctno, T1.date, T2.amount FROM transaction T1, transaction T2 WHERE T1.acctno = T2.acctno AND T2.date <= T1.date;
questions.solution: Self-join transaction on acctno with a date condition.

questions.text:
Consider a bank database with only one relation

transaction (transno, acctno, date, amount)

The amount attribute value is positive for deposits and negative for withdrawals.

Using only the above view TP, write a query to find for each account the minimum balance it ever reached (not including the 0 balance when the account is created). Assume there is at most one transaction per day on each account, and each account has had atleast one transaction since it was created. To simply your query, break it up into 2 steps by defining an intermediate view V.
questions.subject: db
questions.answer: CREATE VIEW V AS SELECT acctno, date, SUM(amount) AS balance FROM TP GROUP BY acctno, date; SELECT acctno, MIN(balance) FROM V GROUP BY acctno;
questions.solution: Summing T2.amount per (acctno, T1.date) gives the balance after each day's transaction; then take the minimum per account.

S2: The sum of two $n \times n$ non-singular matrices may be singular

Which of the following statements is correct?

options.t: S1 and S2 are both true
S1 is true, S2 is false
S1 is false, S2 is true
S1 and S2 are both false

questions.subject: la
questions.solution: diag(1,0) + diag(0,1) = I is non-singular (S1 true); I + (−I) = 0 is singular (S2 true).

questions.text:
Consider the following relations:

R1(a, b) iff $(a + b)$ is even over the set of integers

R2(a, b) iff $(a + b)$ is odd over the set of integers

R3(a, b) iff $a.b > 0$ over the set of non-zero rational numbers

R4(a, b) iff $|a - b| \le 2$ over the set of natural numbers

Which of the following statements is correct?

options.t: R1 and R2 are equivalence relations, R3 and R4 are not
R1 and R3 are equivalence relations, R2 and R4 are not
R1 and R4 are equivalence relations, R2 and R3 are not
R1, R2, R3 and R4 are all equivalence relations

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: R1 (same parity) and R3 (same sign) are equivalences; R2 is not reflexive (a+a even) and R4 is not transitive (1~3, 3~5 but not 1~5).

questions.text:
Consider two well-formed formulas in propositional logic

$F1: P \Rightarrow \neg P \qquad F2: (P \Rightarrow \neg P) \vee (\neg P \Rightarrow P)$

Which of the following statements is correct?

options.t: F1 is satisfiable, F2 is valid
F1 is unsatisfiable, F2 is satisfiable
F1 is unsatisfiable, F2 is valid
F1 and F2 are both satisfiable

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: F1 ≡ ¬P, true when P is false (satisfiable, not valid); F2 ≡ ¬P ∨ P, a tautology.

S1: $\{0^{2n} \mid n \ge 1\}$ is a regular language

S2: $\{0^m 1^n 0^{m+n} \mid m \ge 1 \text{ and } n \ge 1\}$ is a regular language

Which of the following statements is correct?

options.t: Both S1 and S2 are correct
None of S1 and S2 is correct

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: S1 is (00)(00)* — regular. S2 needs counting m+n to match the trailing 0s — not regular (pumping lemma).

The union of two context free languages is context free
The intersection of two context free languages is context free
The complement of a context free language is context free

Exploit the spatial locality of reference in a program

questions.solution: Fetching neighbouring words together pays off when nearby addresses are accessed soon — spatial locality.

Virtual memory allows each program to exceed the size of the primary memory
Virtual memory increases the degree of multiprogramming
Virtual memory reduces the context switching overhead

questions.solution: Virtual memory adds page-table/TLB switching work on a context switch; it does not reduce that overhead.

questions.text: Suppose a processor does not have any stack pointer register. Which of the following statements is true?

It can have subroutine call instruction, but no nested subroutine calls

| 00 | 0 | X | 0 | X |
| 01 | X | 1 | X | 1 |
| 11 | 0 | X | 1 | 0 |

questions.text: Consider a virtual memory system with FIFO page replacement policy. For an arbitrary page access pattern, increasing the number of page frames in main memory will

options.t: Always decrease the number of page faults
Always increase the number of page faults
Sometimes increase the number of page faults

questions.text: Consider a schema R(A,B,C,D) and functional dependencies $A \to B$ and $C \to D$. Then the decomposition of R into $R_1(AB)$ and $R_2(CD)$ is

Not dependency preserving and not lossless join

Which of the following is true about S1 and S2?

options.t: Both S1 and S2 are correct
None of S1 and S2 is correct

questions.solution: Images preserve unions; for intersections only f(E∩F) ⊆ f(E)∩f(F) (e.g. constant f with disjoint E, F).

questions.text: Seven (distinct) car accidents occurred in a week. What is the probability that they all occurred on the same day?

questions.text:
Consider the following circuit with initial state $Q_0 = Q_1 = 0$. The D Flip-Flops are positive edge triggered and have set up times 20 nanosecond and hold times 0.

Consider the following timing diagrams of X and C; the clock period of C $\ge$ 40 nanosecond. Which one is the correct plot of Y?

figures.alt: Two positive-edge D flip-flops sharing clock C. Input X drives D0 of the first flip-flop and one input of a 2-input AND gate; the other AND input is Q0-bar of the first flip-flop. The AND output drives D1 of the second flip-flop, whose output Q1 is Y.
Clock C with several rising edges marked by vertical lines; X goes high at the first marked rising edge, stays high for about five clock periods, and goes low at the last marked edge.

questions.text:
Consider the following datapath of a simple non-pipelined CPU. The registers A, B, $A_1$, $A_2$, MDR, the bus and the ALU are 8-bit wide. SP and MAR are 16-bit registers. The MUX is of size 8 × (2 : 1) and the DEMUX is of size 8 × (1 : 2). Each memory operation takes 2 CPU clock cycles and uses MAR (Memory Address Register) and MDR (Memory Data Register). SP can be decremented locally.

The CPU instruction "push r", where r = A or B, has the specification

M[SP] ← r

SP ← SP − 1

How many CPU clock cycles are needed to execute the "push r" instruction?

figures.alt: Single 8-bit bus. ALU fed by registers A1 and A2 (both loaded from the bus), ALU output back to the bus. Registers B and A connected to the bus. SP (with a decrement input) connected through an 8x(2:1) MUX to the bus; an 8x(1:2) DEMUX from the bus loads the two bytes of MAR. MDR connected to the bus. Small labels are barely legible in the scan.

questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: r → MDR over the bus while SP reaches MAR through the MUX/DEMUX path (1 cycle), then the 2-cycle memory write; SP is decremented locally in parallel: 3 cycles.
questions.reviewNote: Datapath labels are barely legible; answer (3 cycles, per GATE Overflow) depends on how SP reaches MAR.

```sql
create table geq
```

Prove that powerset $(A \cap B)$ = powerset $(A) \cap$ powerset $(B)$

questions.answer: X ∈ P(A∩B) ⇔ X ⊆ A∩B ⇔ X ⊆ A and X ⊆ B ⇔ X ∈ P(A)∩P(B).

questions.text:
Answer the following:

Let sum(n) = 0 + 1 + 2 + … + n for all natural numbers n. Give an induction proof to show that the following equation is true for all natural numbers m and n:

sum(m + n) = sum(m) + sum(n) + mn
questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: Induct on n: base n=0 trivial; step sum(m+n+1) = sum(m)+sum(n)+mn+(m+n+1) = sum(m)+sum(n+1)+m(n+1).
questions.solution: Fix m; base sum(m+0)=sum(m)+0+0; inductive step adds m+n+1 to both sides, which equals (n+1) + m.

questions.text:
Consider the function $h: N \times N \to N$ so that $h(a, b) = (2a + 1)2^b - 1$, where $N = \{0,1,2,3,\ldots\}$ is the set of natural numbers.

Prove that the function h is an Injection (one-one).
questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: If (2a+1)2^b = (2c+1)2^d then b = d (largest power of 2 dividing it) and hence a = c.
questions.solution: h(a,b)+1 = odd·2^b; the power of 2 and the odd part of a positive integer are unique.

questions.text:
Consider the function $h: N \times N \to N$ so that $h(a, b) = (2a + 1)2^b - 1$, where $N = \{0,1,2,3,\ldots\}$ is the set of natural numbers.

Prove that it is also a Surjection (onto).
questions.subject: dm
questions.answer: For any n ∈ N write n+1 = 2^b·(2a+1) (possible since n+1 ≥ 1); then h(a,b) = n.
questions.solution: Every positive integer n+1 factors as a power of 2 times an odd number.

questions.text:

questions.text:
A sequential circuit takes an input stream of 0's and 1's and produces an output stream of 0's and 1's. Initially it replicates the input on its output until two consecutive 0's are encountered on the input. From then onward, it produces an output stream which is the bit-wise complement of input stream until it encounters two consecutive 1's, whereupon the process repeats. An example of input and output stream is shown below.

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| The input stream: | 101100 | 01001011 | 011 |
| The desired output: | 101100 | 10110100 | 011 |

S-K master-slave flip-flops are to be used to design the circuit.

Give the state transition diagram.
questions.subject: dl
questions.answer: 4-state Mealy machine: A (copy, last≠0), B (copy, last=0), C (complement, last≠1), D (complement, last=1). A: 0/0→B, 1/1→A; B: 0/0→C, 1/1→A; C: 0/1→C, 1/0→D; D: 0/1→C, 1/0→A.
questions.solution: Output = input in copy mode, complement in complement mode; the second 0 of '00' is still copied and the second 1 of '11' still complemented (checks against the given example).

questions.subject: dl

Consider a 5 stage pipeline - IF (Instruction Fetch), ID (Instruction Decode and register read), EX (Execute), MEM (Memory), and WB (Write back). All (memory or register) reads take place in the second phase of a clock cycle and writes occur in the first phase of the clock cycle. Consider the execution of the following instruction sequence:

```
I1: sub r2, r3, r4    /* r2 <- r3 - r4       */
I2: sub r4, r2, r3    /* r4 <- r2 - r3       */
I3: sw  r2, 100(r1)   /* M[r1 + 100] <- r2   */
I4: sub r3, r4, r2    /* r3 <- r4 - r2       */
```

Show all data dependencies between the four instructions.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Compare each instruction's destination with later sources (RAW) and its sources with later destinations (WAR).

```
I2: sub r4, r2, r3    /* r4 <- r2 - r3       */
```

questions.solution: Write in first half of WB and read in second half of ID means a producer 3 instructions earlier is safe; distances 1 and 2 are hazards.

questions.answer: M[E,a] = E→aA; M[E,(] = E→(E); M[A,+] = A→+E; M[A,*] = A→*E; M[A,)] = M[A,$] = A→ε; all other entries empty (grammar is LL(1)).

questions.text:
The syntax of the repeat-until statement is given by the following grammar

$S \to \text{repeat } S_1 \text{ until } E$

where E stands for expressions, S and $S_1$ stand for statements. The non-terminals S and $S_1$ have an attribute code that represents generated code. The non-terminal B has two attributes. The attribute code represents generated code to evaluate the expression and store its truth value in a distinct variable, and the attribute varName contains the name of the variable in which the truth value is stored. The truth value stored in the variable is 1 if E is true, 0 if E is false.

Give a syntax-directed definition to generate three-address code for the repeat-until statement. Assume that you can call a function newlabel() that returns a distinct label for a statement. Use the operator '||' to concatenate two strings and the function gen(s) to generate a line containing the string s.
questions.subject: cd
questions.answer: S.begin = newlabel(); S.code = gen(S.begin ':') || S1.code || E.code || gen('if' E.varName '= 0 goto' S.begin)
questions.solution: Label the start of the body, emit the body and the condition code, then jump back while the condition is false. ('B' in the text is a typo for E.)

questions.text:
Consider a disk with the 100 tracks numbered from 0 to 99 rotating at 3000 rpm. The number of sectors per track is 100. The time to move the head between two successive tracks is 0.2 millisecond.

Consider an initial set of 100 arbitrary disk requests and assume that no new disk requests arrive while servicing these requests. If the head is initially at track 0 and the elevator algorithm is used to schedule disk requests, what is the worst case time to complete all the requests?
questions.subject: os
questions.answer: ≈ 2039.8 ms (19.8 ms seek + 100 × (20 ms rotation + 0.2 ms transfer))
questions.solution: One sweep 0→99 costs 99 × 0.2 = 19.8 ms; each request can wait up to a full 20 ms rotation plus 0.2 ms to read one sector.
questions.reviewNote: Worst-case accounting of rotational latency is interpretation-dependent.

Write a relational algebra query using ($\Pi$, $\sigma$, $\rho$, $\times$) to find the list of names which appear more than once in examinee.

questions.text:
We wish to construct a $B^+$ tree with fan-out (the number of pointers per node) equal to 3 for the following set of key values:

80, 50, 10, 70, 30, 100, 90

Assume that the tree is initially empty and the values are added in the order given.

Show the tree after insertion of 10, after insertion of 30, and after insertion of 90. Intermediate trees need not be shown.
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Max 2 keys per node; an overflowing leaf splits 2|1 with the right leaf's first key copied up; an overflowing internal node pushes its middle key up.
questions.reviewNote: B+ tree split convention (left- vs right-biased) changes the drawn trees.

questions.text:
We wish to construct a $B^+$ tree with fan-out (the number of pointers per node) equal to 3 for the following set of key values:

80, 50, 10, 70, 30, 100, 90

Assume that the tree is initially empty and the values are added in the order given.

The key values 30 and 10 are now deleted from the tree in that order. Show the tree after each deletion.
questions.subject: db
questions.answer: After deleting 30: same shape with leaf [10]. After deleting 10: leaves [10] and [50] merge into [50], the left internal node borrows through the root: root [80]; left [70] → [50] [70]; right [100] → [80,90] [100].
questions.solution: Deleting 10 empties a leaf → merge; the parent underflows and borrows from its sibling [80,100] via rotation through the root.
questions.reviewNote: Result depends on the split/merge convention used in part (a).

questions.text: The rank of the matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1\\ 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}$ is
questions.subject: la
questions.solution: The second row is zero and the first is non-zero, so exactly one linearly independent row: rank 1.

questions.text: The trapezoidal rule for integration gives exact result when the integrand is a polynomial of degree
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Trapezoidal rule interpolates linearly, so its error term involves f''; it is exact for constants and linear polynomials.

questions.text: The minimum number of colours required to colour the vertices of a cycle with $n$ nodes in such a way that no two adjacent nodes have the same colour is:
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Even cycle needs 2 colours, odd cycle needs 3; $n-2\lfloor n/2\rfloor+2$ equals 2 for even $n$ and 3 for odd $n$.

questions.text: In the worst case, the number of comparisons needed to search a singly linked list of length $n$ for a given element is
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: A singly linked list allows only sequential access, so the worst case (element last or absent) takes $n$ comparisons.

questions.text: Which of the following is true?

options.t: The set of all rational negative numbers forms a group under multiplication.
The set of all non-singular matrices forms a group under multiplication.
The set of all matrices forms a group under multiplication.
Both B and C are true.

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Product of two negatives is positive (A not closed); singular matrices have no inverse (C fails); non-singular $n\times n$ matrices form GL(n).

questions.text: The language accepted by a Pushdown Automaton in which the stack is limited to 10 items is best described as
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: A bounded stack has finitely many possible contents, so it can be folded into the finite control: the PDA is equivalent to a finite automaton.

questions.text: “If X then Y unless Z” is represented by which of the following formulas in propositional logic? (“$\neg$” is negation, “$\wedge$” is conjunction, and “$\rightarrow$” is implication)
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: “Y unless Z” = if not Z then Y, so the statement is: if X and not Z then Y.

questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: The 8085 acknowledges INTR by asserting $\overline{INTA}$; the device then places the RST/CALL opcode on the data bus.

questions.text: In 8085 which of the following modifies the program counter?
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Every instruction fetch increments the PC, so all instructions modify it (jumps/calls/PCHL additionally load it).

questions.text: In serial data transmission, every byte of data is padded with a ‘0’ in the beginning and one or two ‘1’s at the end of byte because

options.t: Receiver is to be synchronized for byte reception
Receiver recovers lost ‘0’s and ‘1’s from these padded bits
Padded bits are useful in parity computation

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Start bit (0) and stop bit(s) (1) frame each byte so the asynchronous receiver can synchronise on every byte.

questions.text: Minimum sum of product expression for $f(w,x,y,z)$ shown in Karnaugh-map below is

figures.alt: 4-variable K-map, columns wx = 00,01,11,10, rows yz = 00,01,11,10. Row yz=00: 0 1 1 0; row 01: x 0 0 1; row 11: x 0 0 1; row 10: 0 1 1 x (x = don't care).

questions.solution: 1s at $x=1,z=0$ (columns 01,11 × rows 00,10) give $xz'$; 1s at $x=0,z=1$ (column 10 rows 01,11) plus don't-cares in column 00 give $x'z$.

questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Cache, registers and TLB all store data; an opcode is a field of an instruction, not a storage element.

questions.text: The 2’s complement representation of the decimal value −15 is
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: +15 = 01111 (5 bits needed); invert and add 1: 10000+1 = 10001.

options.t: converting a signed integer from one size to another

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Sign extension replicates the sign bit to widen a two's-complement value to more bits without changing it.

questions.text: In the C language

options.t: At most one activation record exists between the current activation record and the activation record for the main
The number of activation records between the current activation record and the activation record for the main depends on the actual function calling sequence.
The visibility of global variables depends on the actual function calling sequence.

questions.text: The results returned by functions under value-result and reference parameter passing conventions

options.t: Differ in the presence of loops
May differ in the presence of exceptions

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Value-result copies back only at normal return; if an exception aborts the call, updates done by reference persist but copy-back never happens.
questions.reviewNote: Answer debated (aliasing is the classical difference and is not listed); D is the commonly accepted key.

questions.text: Relation R with an associated set of functional dependencies, F, is decomposed into BCNF. The redundancy (arising out of functional dependencies) in the resulting set of relations is

options.t: More than zero but less than that of an equivalent 3NF decomposition

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: In BCNF every non-trivial FD has a superkey on the left, so no FD-induced redundancy remains.

questions.text: With regard to the expressive power of the formal relational query languages, which of the following statements is true?

options.t: Relational algebra is more powerful than relational calculus
Relational algebra has the same power as relational calculus
Relational algebra has the same power as safe relational calculus

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Codd's theorem: relational algebra is equivalent to the safe (domain-independent) relational calculus.

questions.text: In 2’s complement addition, overflow

options.t: is flagged whenever there is carry from sign bit addition
cannot occur when a positive value is added to a negative value
is flagged when the carries from sign bit and previous bit match

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Overflow occurs only when both operands have the same sign (carry into and out of the sign bit differ); adding a positive and a negative value can never overflow.
questions.reviewNote: Some published keys give D; B is the factually correct statement (A and C are wrong conditions).

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: FIFO/FCFS runs each job to completion; the others preempt on quantum expiry or priority.

Has been used least number of times.
Has been used most number of times

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Belady's OPT evicts the page whose next reference is farthest in the future.

the address of the operand is inside the instruction
the register containing the address of the operand is specified inside the instruction
the location of the operand is implicit

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: A simple undirected graph has at most one edge per unordered pair: $\binom{n}{2}=n(n-1)/2$.

questions.text:
Consider the following logic circuit whose inputs are functions $f_1$, $f_2$, $f_3$, and output is $f$.

Given that

$f_1(x,y,z) = \Sigma(0,1,3,5)$,

$f_2(x,y,z) = \Sigma(6,7)$, and

$f(x,y,z) = \Sigma(1,4,5)$,

$f_3$ is

figures.alt: f1(x,y,z) and f2(x,y,z) feed a 2-input NAND gate; f3(x,y,z) passes through a NOT gate; the NAND output and the inverted f3 feed a second 2-input NAND gate whose output is f(x,y,z).

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: $f_1f_2=0$ (disjoint minterms) so the first NAND outputs 1; then $f=\overline{1\cdot\overline{f_3}}=f_3$, hence $f_3=\Sigma(1,4,5)$.

questions.text:
Consider the following multiplexor where I0, I1, I2, I3 are four data input lines selected by two address line combinations A1A0 = 00, 01, 10, 11 respectively and f is the output of the multiplexor. EN is the Enable input.

The function $f(x,y,z)$ implemented by the above circuit is

figures.alt: 4-to-1 multiplexer with inputs I0, I1, I2, I3, select A1, A0 and enable EN. x is wired to I0 and I1; y is wired to I2 and through a NOT gate to I3, the inverted y (y') also drives A1; z drives A0 and through a NOT gate drives EN. Output labelled f(x,y,z) = ?

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: $I_0=I_1=x$, $I_2=y$, $I_3=A_1=y'$, $A_0=z$, $EN=z'$. Output only when $z=0$ (so $A_0=0$): $y=1\Rightarrow A_1=0$, output $I_0=x$; $y=0\Rightarrow$ output $I_2=y=0$. So $f=xyz'$.

questions.text: Let $f(A,B) = A' + B$. Simplified expression for function $f(f(x+y,y),z)$ is
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: $f(x+y,y)=(x+y)'+y=x'y'+y=x'+y$; then $f(x'+y,z)=(x'+y)'+z=xy'+z$.

```asm
MVI H, 5DH
MVI L, 6BH
MOV A, H
ADD L
```

Outputs 01 whenever the input sequence contains 11
Outputs 00 whenever the input sequence contains 10

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: A = previous bit 0, B/C = previous bit 1; outputs 0/00, 1/01 from A and 0/01, 1/10 from B, C are exactly prev + current in binary.

questions.text: The performance of a pipelined processor suffers if

options.t: the pipeline stages have different delays
consecutive instructions are dependent on each other
the pipeline stages share hardware resources

questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Unequal stages force the clock to the slowest stage, dependences cause data hazards, and shared resources cause structural hazards.

questions.text: Horizontal microprogramming

results in larger sized microinstructions than vertical microprogramming
uses one bit for each control signal

questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Horizontal microcode dedicates one bit per control signal, so no decoding is needed and the words are wider than vertical (encoded) microcode.

questions.text: A weight-balanced tree is a binary tree in which for each node, the number of nodes in the left subtree is at least half and at most twice the number of nodes in the right subtree. options.t: Parsable fully only by a Turing machine

options.t: The path for searching dynamic libraries is not known till runtime

questions.subject: os

questions.text:
Which combination of the following features will suffice to characterize an OS as a multiprogrammed OS?

(a) More than one program may be loaded into main memory at the same time for execution.

(b) If a program waits for certain events such as I/O, another program is immediately scheduled for execution;

(c) If the execution of a program terminates, another program is immediately scheduled for execution.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Multiprogramming = several programs resident plus switching the CPU to another when one waits; (c) holds even for batch systems.

the number of blocks used for the index, and the size of the blocks.
the size of the blocks, the number of blocks used for the index, and the size of the address of the blocks.

questions.text: A $B^+$-tree index is to be built on the Name attribute of the relation STUDENT. questions.solution: $4p + 8(p-1) \le 512 \Rightarrow 12p \le 520 \Rightarrow p = 43$.

questions.text:

Give the expression for $N_r$ in terms of $n$.

Give the expression for $N_f$ in terms of $n$.

questions.text:

Which is larger for all possible $n$, $N_r$ or $N_f$?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: $2^{n^2}=(2^n)^n > n^n$ since $2^n>n$ for all $n\ge1$ (every function is also a relation).

questions.text:

$S = \{\langle 1,2\rangle, \langle 2,1\rangle\}$ is a binary relation on set $A = \{1,2,3\}$. Is it irreflexive? Add the minimum number of ordered pairs to $S$ to make it an equivalence relation. Give the modified $S$.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: No pair $\langle a,a\rangle$ is in S, so it is irreflexive; adding the three diagonal pairs gives reflexivity, and symmetry/transitivity then hold.

questions.text:

Determine whether each of the following is a tautology, a contradiction, or neither (“$\vee$” is disjunction, “$\wedge$” is conjunction, “$\rightarrow$” is implication, “$\neg$” is negation, and “$\leftrightarrow$” is biconditional (if and only if).

Express the function $f(x,y,z) = xy' + yz'$ with only one complement operation and one or more AND/OR operations. Draw the logic circuit implementing the expression obtained, using a single NOT gate and one or more AND/OR gates.
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: $(x+y)(y'+z') = xy'+xz'+yz' = xy'+yz'$ (xz' is the consensus term); $y'+z'=(yz)'$ needs one NOT after an AND.

Consider the following circuits. $A = a_2a_1a_0$ and $B = b_2b_1b_0$ are three bit binary numbers input to the circuit. The output is $Z = z_3z_2z_1z_0$. R0, R1 and R2 are registers with loading clock shown. The registers are loaded with their input data with the falling edge of a clock pulse (signal CLOCK shown) and appear as shown. The bits of input numbers A, B, and the full adders are as shown in the circuit. Assume Clock period is greater than the settling time of all circuits.

For 8 clocks pulses on the CLOCK terminal and the inputs A, B as shown, obtain the output Z (sequence of 4-bit values of Z). Assume initial contents of R0, R1 and R2 as all zeros.

| | | | | | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 110 | 011 | 111 | 101 | 000 | 000 | 000 | 000 |
| B | 101 | 101 | 011 | 110 | 000 | 000 | 000 | 000 |
| Clock No | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |

figures.alt: Registers REG R0 (6-bit) holding a2 a1 a0 b2 b1 b0 loaded from inputs A and B, REG R1 (6-bit) and REG R2 (5-bit), all clocked by CLOCK. Below R0 a full adder adds a0, b0 with carry-in 0; its sum and carry are stored into R1 together with a2, a1, b2, b1. A second FA below R1 adds a1, b1 and the stored carry; results go into R2 with a2, b2 and the stored sum bit. A third FA below R2 adds a2, b2 and the carry, producing z3 (carry) and z2; the stored sum bits give z1 and z0.

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Each operand pair needs 3 clocks to pass R0→R1→R2, so the sum A+B of clock k appears after clock k+2: 110+101=1011, 011+101=1000, 111+011=1010, 101+110=1011.

In a C program, an array is declared as `float A[2048]`. Each array element is 4 Bytes in size, and the starting address of the array is 0x00000000. This program is run on a computer that has a direct mapped data cache of size 8 Kbytes, with block (line) size of 16 Bytes.

Which elements of the array conflict with element A[0] in the data cache? Justify your answer briefly.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: The array is exactly 8 KB = cache size, so its 512 blocks map to 512 distinct lines; A[1..3] share A[0]'s block but do not conflict.
questions.reviewNote: The PDF prints 'size S Kbytes' (typo for 8 Kbytes in the original paper).

questions.text:

If the program accesses the elements of this array one by one in reverse order, i.e., starting with the last element and ending with the first element, how many data cache misses would occur? Justify your answer briefly. Assume that the data cache is initially empty and that no other data or instruction accesses are to be considered.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Only compulsory misses: one per 16-byte block, 8192/16 = 512.

The aim of the following question is to prove that the language $\{M \mid M$ is the code of a Turing Machine which, irrespective of the input, halts and outputs a 1$\}$, is undecidable. This is to be done by reducing from the language $\{M', x \mid M'$ halts on $x\}$, which is known to be undecidable. In parts (a) and (b) describe the 2 main steps in the construction of M. In part (c) describe the key property which relates the behaviour of M on its input w to the behaviour of M’ on x.

On input w, what is the first step that M must make?
questions.subject: toc
questions.answer: Ignore/erase w and simulate M' on x
questions.solution: M's behaviour must not depend on w; it runs M' on the hard-wired x.

A university placement centre maintains a relational database of companies that interview students on campus and make job offers to those successful in the interview. The schema of the database is given below:

COMPANY (<u>cname</u>, clocation)

STUDENT (<u>srollno</u>, sname, sdegree)

INTERVIEW (<u>cname, srollno</u>, idate)

OFFER (<u>cname, srollno</u>, osalary)

The COMPANY relation gives the name and location of the company. The STUDENT relation gives the students roll number, name and the degree program for which the student is registered in the university. The INTERVIEW relation gives the date on which a student is interviewed by a company. The OFFER relation gives the salary offered to a student who is successful in a company’s interview. The key for each relation is indicated by the underlined attributes.

Write relational algebra expressions (using only the operators $\bowtie$, $\sigma$, $\pi$, $\cup$, $-$) for the following queries:

(i) List the rollnumbers and names of those students who attended at least one interview but did not receive any job offer.
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Interviewed roll numbers minus those with any offer, joined with STUDENT for names.

Write an SQL query to list, for each degree program in which more than five students were offered jobs, the name of the degree and the average offered salary of students in this degree program.
questions.subject: db
questions.answer: SELECT sdegree, AVG(osalary) FROM STUDENT S, OFFER O WHERE S.srollno = O.srollno GROUP BY sdegree HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT S.srollno) > 5
questions.solution: Join, group by degree, filter groups by count of distinct offered students.

For relation R = (L, M, N, O, P), the following dependencies hold:

$M \rightarrow O$, $NO \rightarrow P$, $P \rightarrow L$ and $L \rightarrow MN$

R is decomposed into $R_1 = (L, M, N, P)$ and $R_2 = (M, O)$.

Is the above decomposition a lossless-join decomposition? Explain.
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: $R_1\cap R_2 = \{M\}$ and $M\rightarrow O$, so M is a key of $R_2$.

questions.text:
