questions.text:
An IP machine Q has a path to another IP machine H via three IP routers R1, R2, and R3.

Q—R1—R2—R3—H

H acts as an HTTP server, and Q connects to H via HTTP and downloads a file. Session layer encryption is used, with DES as the shared key encryption protocol. Consider the following four pieces of information:

[I1] The URL of the file downloaded by Q

[I2] The TCP port numbers at Q and H

[I3] The IP addresses of Q and H

[I4] The link layer addresses of Q and H

Which of I1, I2, I3, and I4 can an intruder learn through sniffing at R2 alone?
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Session-layer encryption hides the URL (application data); TCP ports and IP addresses are in headers below it and stay visible; link addresses at R2 are those of R1/R3, not Q and H.

questions.text: A graphical HTML browser resident at a network client machine Q accesses a static HTML webpage from a HTTP server S. The static HTML page has exactly one static embedded image which is also at S. Assuming no caching, which one of the following is correct about the HTML webpage loading (including the embedded image)?

options.t: Q needs to send at least 2 HTTP requests to S, each necessarily in a separate TCP connection to server S
Q needs to send at least 2 HTTP requests to S, but a single TCP connection to server S is sufficient
A single HTTP request from Q to S is sufficient, and a single TCP connection between Q and S is necessary for this
A single HTTP request from Q to S is sufficient, and this is possible without any TCP connection between Q and S

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Page and image need two requests; a persistent connection lets both use one TCP connection.

questions.text:
Consider the following schedule S of transactions T1, T2, T3, T4:

| T1 | T2 | T3 | T4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| | Reads(X) | | |
| | | Writes(X) | |
| | | Commit | |
| Writes(X) | | | |
| Commit | | | |
| | Writes(Y) | | |
| | Reads(Z) | | |
| | Commit | | |
| | | | Reads(X) |
| | | | Reads(Y) |
| | | | Commit |

(Rows are in time order, top to bottom.)

Which one of the following statements is CORRECT?

options.t: S is conflict-serializable but not recoverable
S is not conflict-serializable but is recoverable
S is both conflict-serializable and recoverable
S is neither conflict-serializable nor is it recoverable

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Precedence edges: T2->T3, T2->T1, T3->T1, T3->T4, T1->T4, T2->T4: acyclic. Every read is of committed data (T4 reads after T1/T2 commits), so recoverable.
questions.reviewNote: Table layout reconstructed from image: rows are in time order; verify wording of time order if needed.

questions.text: Consider a join (relation algebra) between relations r(R) and s(S) using the nested loop method. There are 3 buffers each of size equal to disk block size, out of which one buffer is reserved for intermediate results. Assuming size(r(R)) < size(s(S)), the join will have fewer number of disk block accesses if

options.t: relation r(R) is in the outer loop.
relation s(S) is in the outer loop.
join selection factor between r(R) and s(S) is more than 0.5.
join selection factor between r(R) and s(S) is less than 0.5.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Cost = b_outer + ceil(b_outer/(M-2))*b_inner; the smaller relation as outer minimises block accesses.

options.t: The producer will be able to add an item to the buffer, but the consumer can never consume it.
The consumer will remove no more than one item from the buffer.
Deadlock occurs if the consumer succeeds in acquiring semaphore s when the buffer is empty.
The starting value for the semaphore n must be 1 and not 0 for deadlock-free operation.

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: If the consumer takes s then blocks on n (empty buffer), the producer blocks on s: deadlock.

questions.text:
Three processes A, B and C each execute a loop of 100 iterations. In each iteration of the loop, a process performs a single computation that requires $t_c$ CPU milliseconds and then initiates a single I/O operation that lasts for $t_{io}$ milliseconds. It is assumed that the computer where the processes execute has sufficient number of I/O devices and the OS of the computer assigns different I/O devices to each process. Also, the scheduling overhead of the OS is negligible. The processes have the following characteristics:

| Process id | $t_c$ | $t_{io}$ |
|---|---|---|
| A | 100 ms | 500 ms |
| B | 350 ms | 500 ms |
| C | 200 ms | 500 ms |

The processes A, B, and C are started at times 0, 5 and 10 milliseconds respectively, in a pure time sharing system (round robin scheduling) that uses a time slice of 50 milliseconds. The time in milliseconds at which process C would complete its first I/O operation is _____.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: RR order A,B,C,A,B,C,B,C,B,C,...: C gets its 4th slice at 450-500, finishing its 200 ms burst at 500; I/O ends at 1000.

questions.text: A computer has twenty physical page frames which contain pages numbered 101 through 120. Now a program accesses the pages numbered 1, 2, ..., 100 in that order, and repeats the access sequence THRICE. Which one of the following page replacement policies experiences the same number of page faults as the optimal page replacement policy for this program?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: For a cyclic reference string larger than memory, MRU (like optimal) keeps old pages resident and evicts the just-used one, matching optimal's fault count; LRU and FIFO fault on every access.

questions.text:
For a C program accessing X[i][j][k], the following intermediate code is generated by a compiler. Assume that the size of an integer is 32 bits and the size of a character is 8 bits.

```
t0 = i * 1024
t1 = j * 32
t2 = k * 4
t3 = t1 + t0
t4 = t3 + t2
t5 = X[t4]
```

Which one of the following statements about the source code for the C program is CORRECT?

questions.solution: k stride 4 bytes means int elements; j stride 32 = 8 ints so last dim 8; i stride 1024 = 32*32 so middle dim 32: int X[32][32][8].

questions.text: Let $L_1=\{w\in\{0,1\}^*\mid w$ has at least as many occurrences of (110)'s as (011)'s$\}$. Let $L_2=\{w\in\{0,1\}^*\mid w$ has at least as many occurrences of (000)'s as (111)'s$\}$. Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: In any string, #110 and #011 differ by at most 1 so L1 is regular; counting 000 vs 111 needs unbounded counting, so L2 is not regular.

questions.text: Consider two strings $A=$ "qpqrr" and $B=$ "pqprqrp". Let $x$ be the length of the longest common subsequence (not necessarily contiguous) between $A$ and $B$ and let $y$ be the number of such longest common subsequences between $A$ and $B$. Then $x+10y=$ ___.
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: LCS length x = 4 and there are y = 3 distinct LCS (qpqr, qqrr, pqrr), so 4+30 = 34.

questions.text: Suppose a stack implementation supports an instruction REVERSE, which reverses the order of elements on the stack, in addition to the PUSH and POP instructions. Which one of the following statements is TRUE with respect to this modified stack?

A queue can be implemented where ENQUEUE takes a single instruction and DEQUEUE takes a sequence of two instructions.
A queue can be implemented where ENQUEUE takes a sequence of three instructions and DEQUEUE takes a single instruction.
A queue can be implemented where both ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE take a single instruction each.

questions.text: In designing a computer's cache system, the cache block (or cache line) size is an important parameter. Which one of the following statements is correct in this context?

questions.text:
Consider the following relation on subsets of the set $S$ of integers between 1 and 2014. For two distinct subsets $U$ and $V$ of $S$ we say $U<V$ if the minimum element in the symmetric difference of the two sets is in $U$.

Consider the following two statements:

Which one of the following is CORRECT?

questions.text: The number of distinct minimum spanning trees for the weighted graph below is _____

questions.text:

select * from R where a in (select S.a from S)
```

options.t: select R.* from R, S where R.a=S.a
select distinct R.* from R,S where R.a=S.a
select R.* from R,(select distinct a from S) as S1 where R.a=S1.a
select R.* from R,S where R.a=S.a and is unique R

questions.subject: db

questions.text: Consider a main memory system that consists of 8 memory modules attached to the system bus, which is one word wide. When a write request is made, the bus is occupied for 100 nanoseconds (ns) by the data, address, and control signals. During the same 100 ns, and for 500 ns thereafter, the addressed memory module executes one cycle accepting and storing the data. The (internal) operation of different memory modules may overlap in time, but only one request can be on the bus at any time. The maximum number of stores (of one word each) that can be initiated in 1 millisecond is _____
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: A module is busy 600 ns, so 8 modules can accept one request per 100 ns bus slot continuously (8*100=800 > 600): 1 ms/100 ns = 10000.

options.t: Students should come at 9.00 a.m. and parents should come at 10.00 a.m.
Participating students should come at 9.00 a.m. accompanied by a parent, and other parents and students should come by 10.00 a.m.
Students who are not participating should come by 10.00 a.m. and they should not bring their parents. Participating students should come at 9.00 a.m.
Participating students should come before 9.00 a.m. Parents who accompany them should come at 9.00 a.m. All others should come at 10.00 a.m.

questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: Only B states participants + accompanying parent at 9, everyone else by 10.

questions.text:
By the beginning of the 20th century, several hypotheses were being proposed, suggesting a paradigm shift in our understanding of the universe. However, the clinching evidence was provided by experimental measurements of the position of a star which was directly behind our sun.

Which of the following inference(s) may be drawn from the above passage?

(i) Our understanding of the universe changes based on the positions of stars
(ii) Paradigm shifts usually occur at the beginning of centuries
(iii) Stars are important objects in the universe
(iv) Experimental evidence was important in confirming this paradigm shift
questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: Only (iv) is directly supported; the others over-generalise.

questions.text: The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in Rupees grew at 7% during 2012-2013. For international comparison, the GDP is compared in US Dollars (USD) after conversion based on the market exchange rate. During the period 2012-2013 the exchange rate for the USD increased from Rs. 50/ USD to Rs. 60/ USD. India's GDP in USD during the period 2012-2013
questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: Ratio = 1.07*50/60 = 0.8917, i.e. about an 11% decrease.

questions.text: The ratio of male to female students in a college for five years is plotted in the following line graph. If the number of female students in 2011 and 2012 is equal, what is the ratio of male students in 2012 to male students in 2011?

figures.alt: Line graph, y-axis ratio of male to female students 0 to 3.5, x-axis years 2008-2012; points: 2008=2.5, 2009=3, 2010=2, 2011=1, 2012=1.5.

questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: Ratio is 1 in 2011 and 1.5 in 2012; females equal, so males 2012 : 2011 = 1.5 : 1.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:

P: Good mobile phones are not cheap
Q: Cheap mobile phones are not good

L: P implies Q
M: Q implies P
N: P is equivalent to Q

Which one of the following about L, M, and N is CORRECT?

options.t: L, M and N are TRUE.

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: P: good -> not cheap; Q: cheap -> not good is its contrapositive, so P and Q are equivalent and all of L, M, N hold.

questions.text: Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite sets and $f: X \to Y$ be a function. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?

options.t: For any subsets $A$ and $B$ of $X$, $|f(A \cup B)| = |f(A)| + |f(B)|$
For any subsets $A$ and $B$ of $X$, $f(A \cap B) = f(A) \cap f(B)$
For any subsets $A$ and $B$ of $X$, $|f(A \cap B)| = \min\{|f(A)|, |f(B)|\}$
For any subsets $S$ and $T$ of $Y$, $f^{-1}(S \cap T) = f^{-1}(S) \cap f^{-1}(T)$

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Preimage distributes over intersection; the image statements fail when f is not injective.

questions.text: Let $G$ be a group with 15 elements. Let $L$ be a subgroup of $G$. It is known that $L \neq G$ and that the size of $L$ is at least 4. The size of $L$ is __________.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: By Lagrange |L| divides 15: 1,3,5,15; proper and >=4 gives 5.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is TRUE about every $n \times n$ matrix with only real eigenvalues?

options.t: If the trace of the matrix is positive and the determinant of the matrix is negative, at least one of its eigenvalues is negative.
If the trace of the matrix is positive, all its eigenvalues are positive.
If the determinant of the matrix is positive, all its eigenvalues are positive.
If the product of the trace and determinant of the matrix is positive, all its eigenvalues are positive.

questions.subject: la
questions.solution: Determinant = product of eigenvalues; negative product means an odd number of negative eigenvalues. B, C, D fail e.g. for diag(-1,-2).

questions.text: If $\int_0^{2\pi} |x \sin x|\, dx = k\pi$, then the value of $k$ is equal to ______ .
questions.subject: calc
questions.solution: ∫x sin x = -x cos x + sin x. On [0,π] gives π; on [π,2π] |.| gives 3π; total 4π.

Consider the following minterm expression for $F$:

$$F(P,Q,R,S) = \sum 0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15$$

The minterms 2, 7, 8 and 13 are 'do not care' terms. The minimal sum-of-products form for $F$ is
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Required minterms 0,5,10,15 (plus don't cares 2,8 and 7,13) group into quads {0,2,8,10} = Q'S' and {5,7,13,15} = QS.

questions.solution: y = x a + x' b is a 2-to-1 multiplexer with select x.

questions.text:
Consider the following processors (ns stands for nanoseconds). Assume that the pipeline registers have zero latency.

P1: Four-stage pipeline with stage latencies 1 ns, 2 ns, 2 ns, 1 ns.
P2: Four-stage pipeline with stage latencies 1 ns, 1.5 ns, 1.5 ns, 1.5 ns.
P3: Five-stage pipeline with stage latencies 0.5 ns, 1 ns, 1 ns, 0.6 ns, 1 ns.
P4: Five-stage pipeline with stage latencies 0.5 ns, 0.5 ns, 1 ns, 1 ns, 1.1 ns.

Which processor has the highest peak clock frequency?
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Cycle time = max stage: P1 2, P2 1.5, P3 1, P4 1.1 ns; P3 is fastest.

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Each off-diagonal pair is swapped twice (at (i,j) and again at (j,i)), so the matrix is unchanged; C cancels.

questions.text: The minimum number of arithmetic operations required to evaluate the polynomial $P(X) = X^5 + 4X^3 + 6X + 5$ for a given value of $X$, using only one temporary variable is ______.
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Accepted key value is 7 (Horner-style evaluation counted as 4 multiplications + 3 additions).
questions.reviewNote: Official key not in the PDF; 7 is the commonly accepted answer, but an exhaustive search found a 6-operation single-temporary program (T=X*X; T=T+2; T=T*T; T=T+2; T=T*X; T=T+5), so the question is arguably ambiguous.

questions.text:
Consider the following rooted tree with the vertex labeled P as the root:

The order in which the nodes are visited during an in-order traversal of the tree is

figures.alt: Root P has children Q and R. Q has one child S. R has three children T, U, V (left to right). U has one child W.

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: In-order: visit first child subtree, then the node, then remaining children in order: S Q P T R W U V.

questions.text: Suppose depth first search is executed on the graph below starting at some unknown vertex. Assume that a recursive call to visit a vertex is made only after first checking that the vertex has not been visited earlier. Then the maximum possible recursion depth (including the initial call) is _________.

figures.alt: Two 3x3 grid graphs (left and right). Bottom-right corner of left grid connects by a path to a middle vertex, which has a pendant vertex above it, and continues to bottom-left corner of right grid. The right grid's middle-right vertex has an extra pendant vertex attached to the right. 21 vertices in total.

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Depth = longest simple path in the 21-vertex graph; both pendant vertices cannot be used with a full grid each, best path visits 19 vertices.

questions.text: You have an array of $n$ elements. Suppose you implement quicksort by always choosing the central element of the array as the pivot. Then the tightest upper bound for the worst case performance is
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Central pivot can still give unbalanced partitions on adversarial input; worst case is O(n^2).

questions.text:
The length of the shortest string NOT in the language (over $\Sigma = \{a, b\}$) of the following regular expression is ______________.

$$a^* b^* (ba)^* a^*$$
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: All strings of length 0-2 (ε,a,b,aa,ab,ba,bb) are in the language; 'bab' (length 3) is not.

questions.text: Let $\Sigma$ be a finite non-empty alphabet and let $2^{\Sigma^*}$ be the power set of $\Sigma^*$. Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Sigma* is countably infinite; its power set is uncountable (Cantor).

questions.text: One of the purposes of using intermediate code in compilers is to

options.t: make parsing and semantic analysis simpler.
improve error recovery and error reporting.
increase the chances of reusing the machine-independent code optimizer in other compilers.

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Machine-independent IR lets one optimizer be shared across front and back ends.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

1) Static allocation of all data areas by a compiler makes it impossible to implement recursion.
2) Automatic garbage collection is essential to implement recursion.
3) Dynamic allocation of activation records is essential to implement recursion.
4) Both heap and stack are essential to implement recursion.
questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Recursion needs a fresh activation record per call (dynamic allocation); garbage collection and heap are not required.

questions.text: In the context of modular software design, which one of the following combinations is desirable?
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Good modular design maximises cohesion and minimises coupling.

questions.text:
A system uses 3 page frames for storing process pages in main memory. It uses the Least Recently Used (LRU) page replacement policy. Assume that all the page frames are initially empty. What is the total number of page faults that will occur while processing the page reference string given below?

4, 7, 6, 1, 7, 6, 1, 2, 7, 2
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Faults on 4,7,6,1 (evict 4), then 2 (evict 7) and 7 (evict 6); hits on 7,6,1 and 2: total 6.

questions.text: What is the optimized version of the relation algebra expression $\pi_{A1}(\pi_{A2}(\sigma_{F1}(\sigma_{F2}(r))))$, where $A1, A2$ are sets of attributes in $r$ with $A1 \subset A2$ and $F1, F2$ are Boolean expressions based on the attributes in $r$?
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Cascaded selections merge into a conjunction; cascaded projections collapse to the outer A1 (A1 ⊂ A2).

questions.text: A prime attribute of a relation scheme $R$ is an attribute that appears

options.t: only in the primary key of $R$.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: By definition a prime attribute is part of some candidate key.

questions.text: In the following pairs of OSI protocol layer/sub-layer and its functionality, the INCORRECT pair is

options.t: Data Link Layer and Bit synchronization
Transport layer and End-to-end process communication
Medium Access Control sub-layer and Channel sharing

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Bit synchronization is a physical-layer function, not data link.

questions.text: A bit-stuffing based framing protocol uses an 8-bit delimiter pattern of 01111110. If the output bit-string after stuffing is 01111100101, then the input bit-string is
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: A 0 is inserted after five consecutive 1s; 0111110101 becomes 01111100101.

questions.text:
Host A (on TCP/IP v4 network A) sends an IP datagram D to host B (also on TCP/IP v4 network B). Assume that no error occurred during the transmission of D. When D reaches B, which of the following IP header field(s) may be different from that of the original datagram D?

(i) TTL   (ii) Checksum   (iii) Fragment Offset
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: TTL changes per hop, checksum is recomputed as a result, and a router may fragment the datagram, changing the offset.

questions.text:
An IP router implementing Classless Inter-domain Routing (CIDR) receives a packet with address 131.23.151.76. The router's routing table has the following entries:

| Prefix | Output Interface Identifier |
|---|---|
| 131.16.0.0/12 | 3 |
| 131.28.0.0/14 | 5 |
| 131.19.0.0/16 | 2 |
| 131.22.0.0/15 | 1 |

The identifier of the output interface on which this packet will be forwarded is ______.
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Second octet 23 matches /12 (16-31) and /15 (22-23) but not /14 (28-31) or /16 (19); longest match is /15 -> interface 1.

questions.text: Every host in an IPv4 network has a 1-second resolution real-time clock with battery backup. Each host needs to generate up to 1000 unique identifiers per second. Assume that each host has a globally unique IPv4 address. Design a 50-bit globally unique ID for this purpose. After what period (in seconds) will the identifiers generated by a host wrap around?
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: 50 bits = 32 (IPv4) + 10 (counter for 1000/s) + 8 bits of clock, so the clock wraps after 2^8 = 256 s.

questions.text: An IP router with a Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) of 1500 bytes has received an IP packet of size 4404 bytes with an IP header of length 20 bytes. The values of the relevant fields in the header of the third IP fragment generated by the router for this packet are
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Payload 4384 = 1480+1480+1424; third fragment has length 1444, offset 2960/8 = 370, MF = 0.

questions.text:
Consider the transactions T1, T2, and T3 and the schedules S1 and S2 given below.

T1: r1(X); r1(Z); w1(X); w1(Z)
T2: r2(Y); r2(Z); w2(Z)
T3: r3(Y); r3(X); w3(Y)

S1: r1(X); r3(Y); r3(X); r2(Y); r2(Z); w3(Y); w2(Z); r1(Z); w1(X); w1(Z)
S2: r1(X); r3(Y); r2(Y); r3(X); r1(Z); r2(Z); w3(Y); w1(X); w2(Z); w1(Z)

Which one of the following statements about the schedules is TRUE?

options.t: Both S1 and S2 are conflict-serializable.
Neither S1 nor S2 is conflict-serializable.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: S1 precedence graph: T2->T3, T3->T1, T2->T1 (acyclic). S2 has T1->T2 (r1(Z) before w2(Z)) and T2->T1 (r2(Z) before w1(Z)): cycle.

questions.text:
Consider the relational schema given below, where eId of the relation dependent is a foreign key referring to empId of the relation employee. Assume that every employee has at least one associated dependent in the dependent relation.

employee (empId, empName, empAge)
dependent(depId, eId, depName, depAge)

Consider the following relational algebra query:

$$\Pi_{empId}(employee) - \Pi_{empId}(employee \bowtie_{(empId = eID) \wedge (empAge \le depAge)} dependent)$$

The above query evaluates to the set of empIds of employees whose age is greater than that of
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: The subtracted set holds employees having some dependent at least as old; the remainder are older than all of their own dependents.

questions.text: A system contains three programs and each requires three tape units for its operation. The minimum number of tape units which the system must have such that deadlocks never arise is _________.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Worst case each holds 2 (total 6); one more unit guarantees someone can finish: 3*(3-1)+1 = 7.

Consider the basic block given below.

```
a = b + c
c = a + d
d = b + c
e = d - b
a = e + b
```

The minimum number of nodes and edges present in the DAG representation of the above basic block respectively are
questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: 3 leaf nodes (b, c0, d0) + 5 operator nodes (each expression is distinct) = 8 nodes; 5 binary operators give 10 edges.

questions.text: Which one of the following problems is undecidable?

options.t: Deciding if a given context-free grammar is ambiguous.
Deciding if a given string is generated by a given context-free grammar.
Deciding if the language generated by a given context-free grammar is empty.
Deciding if the language generated by a given context-free grammar is finite.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: CFG ambiguity is undecidable; membership, emptiness and finiteness are decidable.

questions.text:
Consider the following languages over the alphabet $\Sigma = \{0, 1, c\}$:

$L_1 = \{0^n 1^n \mid n \ge 0\}$
$L_2 = \{w c w^r \mid w \in \{0,1\}^*\}$
$L_3 = \{w w^r \mid w \in \{0,1\}^*\}$

Here, $w^r$ is the reverse of the string $w$. Which of these languages are deterministic Context-free languages?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: L1 and L2 have a marker/structure a DPDA can use; L3 needs to guess the midpoint, so it is context-free but not deterministic.

questions.text: Suppose you want to move from 0 to 100 on the number line. In each step, you either move right by a unit distance or you take a shortcut. A shortcut is simply a pre-specified pair of integers $i, j$ with $i < j$. Given a shortcut $i, j$ if you are at position $i$ on the number line, you may directly move to $j$. Suppose $T(k)$ denotes the smallest number of steps needed to move from $k$ to 100. Suppose further that there is at most 1 shortcut involving any number, and in particular from 9 there is a shortcut to 15. Let $y$ and $z$ be such that $T(9) = 1 + \min(T(y), T(z))$. Then the value of the product $yz$ is _____.
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: From 9 the options are step to 10 or shortcut to 15, so {y,z} = {10,15} and yz = 150.

questions.text:
Consider the decision problem 2CNFSAT defined as follows:

$\{\Phi \mid \Phi$ is a satisfiable propositional formula in CNF with at most two literals per clause$\}$

For example, $\Phi = (x_1 \vee x_2) \wedge (x_1 \vee \overline{x_3}) \wedge (x_2 \vee x_4)$ is a Boolean formula and it is in 2CNFSAT.

The decision problem 2CNFSAT is

options.t: solvable in polynomial time by reduction to directed graph reachability.
solvable in constant time since any input instance is satisfiable.

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: 2-SAT is decided in polynomial time via the implication graph and strongly connected components / reachability.

questions.text: Suppose we have a balanced binary search tree $T$ holding $n$ numbers. We are given two numbers $L$ and $H$ and wish to sum up all the numbers in $T$ that lie between $L$ and $H$. Suppose there are $m$ such numbers in $T$. If the tightest upper bound on the time to compute the sum is $O(n^a \log^b n + m^c \log^d n)$, the value of $a + 10b + 100c + 1000d$ is ____.
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Time is O(log n + m): a=0, b=1, c=1, d=0, giving 0+10+100+0 = 110.

questions.text: Consider a hash table with 100 slots. Collisions are resolved using chaining. Assuming simple uniform hashing, what is the probability that the first 3 slots are unfilled after the first 3 insertions?
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Each insertion independently avoids the first 3 slots with probability 97/100; cubed.

options.t: number of internal nodes in the tree.
number of nodes without a right sibling in the tree.
number of leaf nodes in the tree.

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: A node with no leftMostChild contributes 1; other nodes add the counts of their children and siblings, so it counts leaves.

options.t: It will run into an infinite loop when x is not in listA.
It is an implementation of binary search.
It will always find the maximum element in listA.
It will return -1 even when x is present in listA.

questions.text: An instruction pipeline has five stages, namely, instruction fetch (IF), instruction decode and register fetch (ID/RF), instruction execution (EX), memory access (MEM), and register writeback (WB) with stage latencies 1 ns, 2.2 ns, 2 ns, 1 ns, and 0.75 ns, respectively (ns stands for nanoseconds). To gain in terms of frequency, the designers have decided to split the ID/RF stage into three stages (ID, RF1, RF2) each of latency 2.2/3 ns. Also, the EX stage is split into two stages (EX1, EX2) each of latency 1 ns. The new design has a total of eight pipeline stages. A program has 20% branch instructions which execute in the EX stage and produce the next instruction pointer at the end of the EX stage in the old design and at the end of the EX2 stage in the new design. The IF stage stalls after fetching a branch instruction until the next instruction pointer is computed. All instructions other than the branch instruction have an average CPI of one in both the designs. The execution times of this program on the old and the new design are P and Q nanoseconds, respectively. The value of P/Q is __________.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Old: cycle 2.2 ns, branch stall 2 cycles, CPI 1.4, 3.08 ns/instr. New: cycle 1 ns, stall 5 cycles, CPI 2.0, 2 ns/instr. P/Q = 1.54.

questions.text: The memory access time is 1 nanosecond for a read operation with a hit in cache, 5 nanoseconds for a read operation with a miss in cache, 2 nanoseconds for a write operation with a hit in cache and 10 nanoseconds for a write operation with a miss in cache. Execution of a sequence of instructions involves 100 instruction fetch operations, 60 memory operand read operations and 40 memory operand write operations. The cache hit-ratio is 0.9. The average memory access time (in nanoseconds) in executing the sequence of instructions is __________.
questions.subject: coa

questions.text: The above synchronous sequential circuit built using JK flip-flops is initialized with $Q_2Q_1Q_0 = 000$. The state sequence for this circuit for the next 3 clock cycles is

figures.alt: Three JK flip-flops FF2, FF1, FF0 on a common clock C (left to right). J1=Q2, K1=Q2-bar; J0=Q1, K0=Q0-bar (Q0-bar looped back to K0). J2 is fed from Q1-bar via a long wire along the bottom, K2 is fed from Q0 via a wire along the top; the J2 wire hops over the vertical K2/Q0 wire.

questions.text:
With respect to the numerical evaluation of the definite integral, $K = \int_a^b x^2\, dx$, where $a$ and $b$ are given, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

I) The value of $K$ obtained using the trapezoidal rule is always greater than or equal to the exact value of the definite integral.
II) The value of $K$ obtained using the Simpson's rule is always equal to the exact value of the definite integral.
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: x^2 is convex so trapezoids overestimate; Simpson's rule is exact for polynomials up to degree 3.

questions.text:
The value of the integral given below is

$$\int_0^{\pi} x^2 \cos x \, dx$$
questions.subject: calc
questions.solution: Antiderivative x^2 sin x + 2x cos x - 2 sin x; at pi gives -2pi, at 0 gives 0.

questions.text: Let $S$ be a sample space and two mutually exclusive events $A$ and $B$ be such that $A \cup B = S$. If $P(\cdot)$ denotes the probability of the event, the maximum value of $P(A)P(B)$ is __________.
questions.subject: prob
questions.solution: P(A)+P(B)=1, so the product p(1-p) is maximised at p=1/2 giving 1/4.

questions.text:
Consider the set of all functions $f: \{0,1,\ldots,2014\} \to \{0,1,\ldots,2014\}$ such that $f(f(i)) = i$, for all $0 \le i \le 2014$. Consider the following statements:

P. For each such function it must be the case that for every $i$, $f(i) = i$.
Q. For each such function it must be the case that for some $i$, $f(i) = i$.
R. Each such function must be onto.

Which one of the following is CORRECT?

options.t: P, Q and R are true
Only Q and R are true
Only P and Q are true

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: f is an involution: a bijection (R true). Non-fixed points pair up, and 2015 is odd so at least one fixed point (Q true); P is false (e.g. swap 0 and 1).

questions.text:
There are two elements $x, y$ in a group $(G, *)$ such that every element in the group can be written as a product of some number of $x$'s and $y$'s in some order. It is known that

$$x * x = y * y = x * y * x * y = y * x * y * x = e$$

where $e$ is the identity element. The maximum number of elements in such a group is __________.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Relations give x^2=y^2=(xy)^2=e, which is the Klein four-group {e,x,y,xy}: at most 4 elements.

questions.text: If $G$ is a forest with $n$ vertices and $k$ connected components, how many edges does $G$ have?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Each tree component with n_i vertices has n_i-1 edges; total n-k.

questions.text: Let $\delta$ denote the minimum degree of a vertex in a graph. For all planar graphs on $n$ vertices with $\delta \ge 3$, which one of the following is TRUE?

options.t: In any planar embedding, the number of faces is at least $\frac{n}{2} + 2$
In any planar embedding, the number of faces is less than $\frac{n}{2} + 2$
There is a planar embedding in which the number of faces is less than $\frac{n}{2} + 2$
There is a planar embedding in which the number of faces is at most $\frac{n}{\delta + 1}$

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: δ>=3 gives e >= 3n/2; Euler's formula f = e - n + 2 >= n/2 + 2 for every embedding.

questions.text: The CORRECT formula for the sentence, "not all rainy days are cold" is
questions.subject: ga
questions.solution:
### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework
This question evaluates key concepts in **GA** under **Verbal**.

questions.text: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a simple undirected graph, and $s$ be a particular vertex in it called the source. For $x\in V$, let $d(x)$ denote the shortest distance in $G$ from $s$ to $x$. A breadth first search (BFS) is performed starting at $s$. Let $T$ be the resultant BFS tree. If $(u,v)$ is an edge of $G$ that is not in $T$, then which one of the following CANNOT be the value of $d(u)-d(v)$?
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: In an undirected graph the endpoints of any edge differ in BFS distance by at most 1.

questions.text: Consider a uniprocessor system executing three tasks $T_1$, $T_2$ and $T_3$, each of which is composed of an infinite sequence of jobs (or instances) which arrive periodically at intervals of 3, 7 and 20 milliseconds, respectively. The priority of each task is the inverse of its period, and the available tasks are scheduled in order of priority, with the highest priority task scheduled first. Each instance of $T_1$, $T_2$ and $T_3$ requires an execution time of 1, 2 and 4 milliseconds, respectively. Given that all tasks initially arrive at the beginning of the 1st millisecond and task preemptions are allowed, the first instance of $T_3$ completes its execution at the end of ______ milliseconds.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Rate-monotonic timeline: T1 0-1, T2 1-3, T1 3-4, T3 4-6, T1 6-7, T2 7-9, T1 9-10, T3 10-12; T3 completes at 12.

questions.text: Consider a main memory with five page frames and the following sequence of page references: 3, 8, 2, 3, 9, 1, 6, 3, 8, 9, 3, 6, 2, 1, 3. Which one of the following is true with respect to page replacement policies First In First Out (FIFO) and Least Recently Used (LRU)?

options.t: Both incur the same number of page faults
FIFO incurs 2 more page faults than LRU
LRU incurs 2 more page faults than FIFO
FIFO incurs 1 more page faults than LRU

questions.subject: os
questions.solution:
### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework
This question evaluates key concepts in **OS** under **Virtual Memory**.

### Step-by-Step Mathematical Derivation
- **Analytical Logic:** Evaluating the definition and standard properties of virtual memory:
- Verifying each constraint rules out extraneous possibilities and establishes the official solution: **A**.

### Option Analysis & Verification
- **Option A (CORRECT):** Fully conforms to formal theoretical properties and algebraic evaluation.
- **Distractors:** Counter-examples or violated boundary conditions invalidate the remaining alternatives.

> **Key GATE Takeaway:** Always verify edge conditions (e.g. boundary indices, root node relaxations, zero-determinant conditions) when solving 2-mark questions.

questions.text: Consider a disk pack with a seek time of 4 milliseconds and rotational speed of 10000 rotations per minute (RPM). It has 600 sectors per track and each sector can store 512 bytes of data. Consider a file stored in the disk. The file contains 2000 sectors. Assume that every sector access necessitates a seek, and the average rotational latency for accessing each sector is half of the time for one complete rotation. The total time (in milliseconds) needed to read the entire file is ______.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Rotation = 6 ms, latency 3 ms, sector transfer 6/600 = 0.01 ms; per sector 7.01 ms x 2000 = 14020 ms.

questions.text: Let $a_n$ represent the number of bit strings of length $n$ containing two consecutive 1s. What is the recurrence relation for $a_n$?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Strings starting with 0: a_{n-1}; starting with 10: a_{n-2}; starting with 11: 2^{n-2}.

questions.text:
A variable $x$ is said to be live at a statement $S_i$ in a program if the following three conditions hold simultaneously:

i. There exists a statement $S_j$ that uses $x$
ii. There is a path from $S_i$ to $S_j$ in the flow graph corresponding to the program
iii. The path has no intervening assignment to $x$ including at $S_i$ and $S_j$

The variables which are live both at the statement in basic block 2 and at the statement in basic block 3 of the above control flow graph are

figures.alt: CFG: block 1 (p=q+r; s=p+q; u=s*v) branches to block 2 (v=r+u) and block 3 (q=s*u); both go to block 4 (q=v+r); block 4 has a back edge to block 1.

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Live-in of block 2 = {r,u}; live-in of block 3 = {s,u,v,r}; intersection {r,u}.

questions.text:
Consider the NPDA $\langle Q=\{q_0,q_1,q_2\},\Sigma=\{0,1\},\Gamma=\{0,1,\bot\},\delta,q_0,\bot,F=\{q_2\}\rangle$, where (as per usual convention) $Q$ is the set of states, $\Sigma$ is the input alphabet, $\Gamma$ is the stack alphabet, $\delta$ is the state transition function, $q_0$ is the initial state, $\bot$ is the initial stack symbol, and $F$ is the set of accepting states. The state transition is as follows:

Which one of the following sequences must follow the string 101100 so that the overall string is accepted by the automaton?

figures.alt: q0 loops on (1,Z->1Z) and (0,Z->0Z); q0 to q1 on (0/1/epsilon, Z->Z); q1 loops on (0,1Z->Z) and (1,0Z->Z); q1 to q2 on (epsilon, bottom->epsilon); q2 accepting.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Machine accepts w, optional middle symbol, then reverse-complement of w. 101100+X has length 11: w=10110, middle 0, X = reverse of complement(10110) = 10010.

questions.text: Consider the DFAs M and N given above. The number of states in a minimal DFA that accepts the language $L(M)\cap L(N)$ is ______.

figures.alt: M: two states, start non-accepting; b loops on start, a goes to accepting, a loops on accepting, b returns. N: same with a and b swapped.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: M accepts strings ending in a, N accepts strings ending in b; the intersection is empty, whose minimal DFA has 1 state.

questions.text: Suppose that the stop-and-wait protocol is used on a link with a bit rate of 64 kilobits per second and 20 milliseconds propagation delay. Assume that the transmission time for the acknowledgement and the processing time at nodes are negligible. Then the minimum frame size in bytes to achieve a link utilization of at least 50% is ______.
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Utilization = Tt/(Tt+2Tp) >= 0.5 gives Tt >= 40 ms, so L = 64000 x 0.04 = 2560 bits = 320 bytes.

questions.text: Let $G$ be a connected planar graph with 10 vertices. If the number of edges on each face is three, then the number of edges in $G$ is ______.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: 3F = 2E and V - E + F = 2 give 10 - E + 2E/3 = 2, so E = 24.

questions.text: The least number of temporary variables required to create a three-address code in static single assignment form for the expression $q + r/3 + s - t*5 + u*v/w$ is ______.
questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Eight binary operations (/, *, *, /, +, +, -, +), each assigned to a fresh SSA temporary.
questions.reviewNote: Could be argued as 7 if the final result is assigned to a named variable; 8 is the commonly cited key.

questions.text: We ____________ our friend's birthday and we ____________ how to make it up to him.
questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: 'completely forgot' is the natural word order and 'don't just know' fits the intended sense; best fit of the four.

questions.subject: ga

questions.text:
Based on the given statements, select the most appropriate option to solve the given question.

What will be the total weight of 10 poles each of same weight?

Statements:

(I) One fourth of the weight of a pole is 5 Kg.

(II) The total weight of these poles is 160 kg more than the total weight of two poles.

options.t: Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Either I or II alone is sufficient.
Both statements I and II together are not sufficient.

questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: I: pole = 20 kg so 10 poles = 200 kg. II: 10w = 160 + 2w gives w = 20, so 200 kg. Each alone suffices.

questions.text: In a triangle PQR, PS is the angle bisector of $\angle QPR$ and $\angle QPS = 60^\circ$. What is the length of PS?

questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: Area split: $\tfrac12 qr\sin120^\circ = \tfrac12 r\,PS\sin60^\circ + \tfrac12 q\,PS\sin60^\circ$, so PS = qr/(q+r).

questions.text:

f (p, q, r, s) = max (p, q, r, s)

questions.text: Out of the following four sentences, select the most suitable sentence with respect to grammar and usage:

options.t: Since the report lacked needed information, it was of no use to them.
The report was useless to them because there were no needed information in it.
Since the report did not contain the needed information, it was not real useful to them.

questions.solution: (A) is grammatical; (B) has subject-verb disagreement, (C) uses 'real' for 'really', (D) 'would not had been' is ungrammatical.

questions.text:
Consider the following transaction involving two bank accounts $x$ and $y$.

read(x); x := x - 50; write(x); read(y); y:= y + 50; write(y)
```

The constraint that the sum of the accounts $x$ and $y$ should remain constant is that of
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Preserving an integrity constraint (x + y constant) is the Consistency property.

questions.text: Consider two decision problems $Q_1, Q_2$ such that $Q_1$ reduces in polynomial time to 3-SAT and 3-SAT reduces in polynomial time to $Q_2$. Then which one of the following is consistent with the above statement?

options.t: $Q_1$ is in NP, $Q_2$ is NP hard.
$Q_2$ is in NP, $Q_1$ is NP hard.

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Q1 <=p 3-SAT in NP puts Q1 in NP; 3-SAT <=p Q2 makes Q2 NP-hard. Nothing forces Q1 to be NP-hard or Q2 to be in NP.

questions.text:
Consider the following two statements.

S1: If a candidate is known to be corrupt, then he will not be elected

S2: If a candidate is kind, he will be elected

Which one of the following statements follows from S1 and S2 as per sound inference rules of logic?

options.t: If a person is known to be corrupt, he is kind
If a person is not known to be corrupt, he is not kind
If a person is kind, he is not known to be corrupt
If a person is not kind, he is not known to be corrupt

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: S2: kind -> elected; contrapositive of S1: elected -> not corrupt. Chaining: kind -> not corrupt.

questions.text: A software requirements specification (SRS) document should avoid discussing which one of the following?
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: An SRS states what the system does, not how it is designed; design specification should be avoided.

questions.text: The larger of the two eigenvalues of the matrix $\begin{bmatrix}4 & 5\\ 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$ is ________.
questions.subject: la
questions.solution: Characteristic equation: $\lambda^2 - 5\lambda - 6 = 0$ so $\lambda = 6, -1$.

questions.text: With reference to the B+ tree index of order 1 shown below, the minimum number of nodes (including the Root node) that must be fetched in order to satisfy the following query: "Get all records with a search key greater than or equal to 7 and less than 15" is ________.

figures.alt: B+ tree: root holds 9; its left child holds 5 and right child holds 13, 17. Leaves left to right, doubly linked: [1,3], [5,7], [9,11], [13,15], [17,-]. Left child points to leaves [1,3] and [5,7]; right child points to [9,11], [13,15], [17].

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Fetch root, the internal node (5), leaf [5,7], then follow leaf links to [9,11] and [13,15]: 1 + 1 + 3 = 5 nodes.

questions.text: The minimum number of JK flip-flops required to construct a synchronous counter with the count sequence (0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3,0,0,...) is ________.
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Each count value appears twice consecutively, giving 8 distinct states in the cycle; $\lceil\log_2 8\rceil = 3$ flip-flops.

questions.text: A link has a transmission speed of $10^6$ bits/sec. It uses data packets of size 1000 bytes each. Assume that the acknowledgement has negligible transmission delay, and that its propagation delay is the same as the data propagation delay. Also assume that the processing delays at nodes are negligible. The efficiency of the stop-and-wait protocol in this setup is exactly 25%. The value of the one-way propagation delay (in milliseconds) is ________.
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: $T_t = 8000/10^6 = 8$ ms. Efficiency = $T_t/(T_t+2T_p) = 0.25$ gives $8+2T_p = 32$, so $T_p = 12$ ms.

questions.text: The number of divisors of 2100 is ________.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: $2100 = 2^2\cdot3\cdot5^2\cdot7$, so divisors = 3·2·3·2 = 36.

questions.text: A binary tree T has 20 leaves. The number of nodes in T having two children is ________.
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: In a binary tree, leaves = (nodes with two children) + 1, so 20 leaves give 19.

questions.text: Consider the basic COCOMO model where $E$ is the effort applied in person-months, $D$ is the development time in chronological months, $KLOC$ is the estimated number of delivered lines of code (in thousands) and $a_b, b_b, c_b, d_b$ have their usual meanings. The basic COCOMO equations are of the form
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Basic COCOMO: $E = a_b(KLOC)^{b_b}$ and $D = c_b E^{d_b}$.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about HTTP cookies?

options.t: A cookie is a piece of code that has the potential to compromise the security of an Internet user
A cookie gains entry to the user's work area through an HTTP header
A cookie has an expiry date and time
Cookies can be used to track the browsing pattern of a user at a particular site

questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: A cookie is a small piece of data, not executable code; the other statements are true.
questions.reviewNote: Option A vs B judged from knowledge of cookies; official key not printed in PDF.

questions.text: In the context of abstract-syntax-tree (AST) and control-flow-graph (CFG), which one of the following is TRUE?

options.t: In both AST and CFG, let node $N_2$ be the successor of node $N_1$. In the input program, the code corresponding to $N_2$ is present after the code corresponding to $N_1$
For any input program, neither AST nor CFG will contain a cycle
The maximum number of successors of a node in an AST and a CFG depends on the input program
Each node in AST and CFG corresponds to at most one statement in the input program

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: The number of children/successors (e.g. a switch with many cases) depends on the input program. CFGs can have cycles (loops), and successors need not appear later in the code.

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Recursion stops at the first space, so only A,B,C,D are printed on unwinding, in reverse: DCBA.

questions.text: Let $R$ be the relation on the set of positive integers such that $aRb$ if and only if $a$ and $b$ are distinct and have a common divisor other than 1. Which one of the following statements about $R$ is true?

options.t: $R$ is symmetric and reflexive but not transitive
$R$ is reflexive but not symmetric and not transitive
$R$ is transitive but not reflexive and not symmetric
$R$ is symmetric but not reflexive and not transitive

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Symmetric by definition, irreflexive since a and b must be distinct; not transitive: 2R6 and 6R3 but not 2R3.

questions.text: Consider a complete binary tree where the left and right subtrees of the root are max-heaps. The lower bound for the number of operations to convert the tree to a heap is
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Only the root may violate the heap property; sifting it down needs $\Theta(\log n)$ operations, so the lower bound is $\Omega(\log n)$.

questions.text: The cardinality of the power set of $\{0, 1, 2, \ldots, 10\}$ is ________.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: The set has 11 elements, so the power set has $2^{11} = 2048$ elements.

questions.text: Identify the correct order in which a server process must invoke the function calls `accept`, `bind`, `listen`, and `recv` according to UNIX socket API.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.

I. The complement of every Turing decidable language is Turing decidable

II. There exists some language which is in NP but is not Turing decidable

III. If L is a language in NP, L is Turing decidable

Which of the above statements is/are true?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Decidable languages are closed under complement (I true); every NP language is decidable (III true), so II is false.

questions.text: An unordered list contains $n$ distinct elements. The number of comparisons to find an element in this list that is neither maximum nor minimum is
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Examine any three elements; the median of these three is neither the max nor the min of the list. Constant comparisons.

questions.text: A system has 6 identical resources and $N$ processes competing for them. Each process can request atmost 2 resources. Which one of the following values of $N$ could lead to a deadlock?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Deadlock-free iff N(2-1)+1 <= 6, i.e. N <= 5, so strictly none of the options can deadlock as printed; the published key gives D (largest N).
questions.reviewNote: As printed (max 2 resources each, 6 resources) no option can lead to deadlock; answer D is the commonly published key but the question is flawed. Verify.

questions.text: Assume that for a certain processor, a read request takes 50 nanoseconds on a cache miss and 5 nanoseconds on a cache hit. Suppose while running a program, it was observed that 80% of the processor's read requests result in a cache hit. The average read access time in nanoseconds is ________.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution:
### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework
This question evaluates key concepts in **COA** under **Cache**.

### Step-by-Step Mathematical Derivation
- **Bit Breakdown Formula:**
  $$\text{Address Bits} = \text{Tag} + \text{Set Index} + \text{Block Offset}$$
- Computing set index bits: $\log_2(\text{Sets}) = \log_2\left(\frac{\text{Cache Size}}{\text{Block Size} \times \text{Ways}}\right)$, confirming Option **14**.

### Option Analysis & Verification
- **Option 14 (CORRECT):** Fully conforms to formal theoretical properties and algebraic evaluation.
- **Distractors:** Counter-examples or violated boundary conditions invalidate the remaining alternatives.

> **Key GATE Takeaway:** Always verify edge conditions (e.g. boundary indices, root node relaxations, zero-determinant conditions) when solving 2-mark questions.

questions.text: A computer system implements a 40-bit virtual address, page size of 8 kilobytes, and a 128-entry translation look-aside buffer (TLB) organized into 32 sets each having four ways. Assume that the TLB tag does not store any process id. The minimum length of the TLB tag in bits is ________.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Offset = 13 bits, VPN = 27 bits, set index = log2(32) = 5 bits, tag = 27 - 5 = 22 bits.

questions.text:
Let $f(x) = x^{-(1/3)}$ and $A$ denote the area of the region bounded by $f(x)$ and the X-axis, when $x$ varies from $-1$ to $1$. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

I) $f$ is continuous in $[-1, 1]$

II) $f$ is not bounded in $[-1, 1]$

III) $A$ is nonzero and finite
questions.subject: calc
questions.solution: f is undefined at 0 and unbounded near 0 (I false, II true). Area = 2∫_0^1 x^{-1/3} dx = 3, finite and non-zero (III true).

questions.text:
Perform the following operations on the matrix $\begin{bmatrix}3 & 4 & 45\\ 7 & 9 & 105\\ 13 & 2 & 195\end{bmatrix}$.

(i) Add the third row to the second row

(ii) Subtract the third column from the first column.

The determinant of the resultant matrix is ________.
questions.subject: la
questions.solution: Both operations leave the determinant unchanged. det = 3(1755-210) - 4(1365-1365) + 45(14-117) = 4635 - 0 - 4635 = 0.

questions.text: A graph is self-complementary if it is isomorphic to its complement. For all self-complementary graphs on $n$ vertices, $n$ is
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: G and its complement together have n(n-1)/2 edges, so each has n(n-1)/4, requiring n ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 4).

questions.text: Consider six memory partitions of sizes 200 KB, 400 KB, 600 KB, 500 KB, 300 KB and 250 KB, where KB refers to kilobyte. questions.text:
A Young tableau is a 2D array of integers increasing from left to right and from top to bottom. Any unfilled entries are marked with $\infty$, and hence there cannot be any entry to the right of, or below a $\infty$. The following Young tableau consists of unique entries.

| 1 | 2 | 5 | 14 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 4 | 6 | 23 |
| 10 | 12 | 18 | 25 |
| 31 | $\infty$ | $\infty$ | $\infty$ |

When an element is removed from a Young tableau, other elements should be moved into its place so that the resulting table is still a Young tableau (unfilled entries may be filled in with a $\infty$). The minimum number of entries (other than 1) to be shifted, to remove 1 from the given Young tableau is ________.

figures.alt: 4x4 table. Row1: 1 2 5 14. Row2: 3 4 6 23. Row3: 10 12 18 25. Row4: 31 inf inf inf.

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Remove 1, then repeatedly pull the smaller of right/below neighbour: 2, 4, 6, 18, 25 move (5 shifts); then the last cell has no right or lower finite neighbour.

questions.text: Consider two relations $R_1(A, B)$ with the tuples (1,5), (3,7) and $R_2(A, C)$ = (1,7), (4,9). Assume that $R(A, B, C)$ is the full natural outer join of $R_1$ and $R_2$. Consider the following tuples of the form $(A, B, C)$: $a$ = (1,5,null), $b$ = (1,null,7), $c$ = (3, null, 9), $d$ = (4,7,null), $e$ = (1,5,7), $f$ = (3,7,null), $g$ = (4,null,9). Which one of the following statements is correct?

options.t: R contains $a, b, e, f, g$ but not $c, d$.
R contains all of $a, b, c, d, e, f, g$.
R contains $e, f, g$ but not $a, b$.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Full natural outer join = {(1,5,7), (3,7,null), (4,null,9)} = e, f, g.

questions.text: Which one of the following hash functions on integers will distribute keys most uniformly over 10 buckets numbered 0 to 9 for $i$ ranging from 0 to 2020?
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Cubing is a bijection on residues mod 10, so i^3 mod 10 hits each bucket equally. Squares hit only 6 residues; 12i mod 10 only even buckets.

questions.text: Assume that the bandwidth for a TCP connection is 1048560 bits/sec. Let $\alpha$ be the value of RTT in milliseconds (rounded off to the nearest integer) after which the TCP window scale option is needed. Let $\beta$ be the maximum possible window size with window scale option. Then the values of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are
questions.subject: cn

questions.text:
The secant method is used to find the root of an equation $f(x) = 0$. It is started from two distinct estimates $x_a$ and $x_b$ for the root. It is an iterative procedure involving linear interpolation to a root. The iteration stops if $f(x_b)$ is very small and then $x_b$ is the solution. The procedure is given below. Observe that there is an expression which is missing and is marked by `?`. Which is the suitable expression that is to be put in place of `?` so that it follows all steps of the secant method?

```
Secant
  Initialize: xa, xb, e, N       // e = convergence indicator
                                 // N = maximum no. of iterations
  fb = f(xb)
  i = 0
  while (i < N and |fb| > e) do
      i = i + 1                  // update counter
      xt = ?                     // missing expression for
                                 // intermediate value
      xa = xb                    // reset xa
      xb = xt                    // reset xb
      fb = f(xb)                 // function value at new xb
  end while
  if |fb| > e then               // loop is terminated with i=N
      write "Non-convergence"
  else
      write "return xb"
  end if
```
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Secant update: $x_{new} = x_b - f(x_b)(x_b - x_a)/(f(x_b) - f(x_a))$.

questions.text:
Consider a processor with byte-addressable memory. Assume that all registers, including Program Counter (PC) and Program Status Word (PSW), are of size 2 bytes. A stack in the main memory is implemented from memory location $(0100)_{16}$ and it grows upward. The stack pointer (SP) points to the top element of the stack. The current value of SP is $(016E)_{16}$. The CALL instruction is of two words, the first word is the op-code and the second word is the starting address of the subroutine (one word = 2 bytes). The CALL instruction is implemented as follows:

- Store the current value of PC in the stack
- Store the value of PSW register in the stack
- Load the starting address of the subroutine in PC

questions.text:
Consider the sequence of machine instructions given below:

```
MUL R5, R0, R1
DIV R6, R2, R3
ADD R7, R5, R6
SUB R8, R7, R4
```

In the above sequence, R0 to R8 are general purpose registers. In the instructions shown, the first register stores the result of the operation performed on the second and the third registers. This sequence of instructions is to be executed in a pipelined instruction processor with the following 4 stages: (1) Instruction Fetch and Decode (IF), (2) Operand Fetch (OF), (3) Perform Operation (PO) and (4) Write back the result (WB). The IF, OF and WB stages take 1 clock cycle each for any instruction. The PO stage takes 1 clock cycle for ADD or SUB instruction, 3 clock cycles for MUL instruction and 5 clock cycles for DIV instruction. The pipelined processor uses operand forwarding from the PO stage to the OF stage. The number of clock cycles taken for the execution of the above sequence of instructions is ________.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: MUL PO 3-5; DIV PO 4-8 (WB 9); ADD waits for R6 forwarded from DIV, OF at 9, PO 10, WB 11; SUB OF 11, PO 12, WB 13. Total 13 cycles.
questions.reviewNote: Depends on assumed timing model (PO units overlapping); 13 is the commonly cited key.

questions.text: A half adder is implemented with XOR and AND gates. A full adder is implemented with two half adders and one OR gate. questions.text: Consider a typical disk that rotates at 15000 rotations per minute (RPM) and has a transfer rate of $50\times10^6$ bytes/sec. questions.text: Suppose $U$ is the power set of the set $S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$. For any $T\in U$, let $|T|$ denote the number of elements in $T$ and $T'$ denote the complement of $T$. For any $T,R\in U$, let $T\setminus R$ be the set of all elements in $T$ which are not in $R$. Which one of the following is true?

options.t: $\exists X\in U\ \exists Y\in U\ (|X|=5,\ |Y|=5\text{ and }X\cap Y=\emptyset)$
$\forall X\in U\ \forall Y\in U\ (|X|=2,\ |Y|=3\text{ and }X\setminus Y=\emptyset)$
$\forall X\in U\ \forall Y\in U\ (X\setminus Y = Y'\setminus X')$

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: X\Y = X∩Y' and Y'\X' = Y'∩X, which are equal for all X,Y. A fails (|X|≠|X'| in general), B needs 10 elements from 6, C is false for arbitrary X,Y.

questions.text:
In a room there are only two types of people, namely Type 1 and Type 2. Type 1 people always tell the truth and Type 2 people always lie. You give a fair coin to a person in that room, without knowing which type he is from and tell him to toss it and hide the result from you till you ask for it. Upon asking, the person replies the following

"The result of the toss is head if and only if I am telling the truth."

Which of the following options is correct?

options.t: If the person is of Type 2, then the result is tail
If the person is of Type 1, then the result is tail

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Type 1: statement true and 'telling truth' true, so head. Type 2: statement false while 'telling truth' is false, so (head <-> false) false means head. Either way head.

questions.text:
Consider the following code sequence having five instructions $I_1$ to $I_5$. Each of these instructions has the following format.

OP Ri, Rj, Rk

where operation OP is performed on contents of registers Rj and Rk and the result is stored in register Ri.

$I_1$: ADD R1, R2, R3
$I_2$: MUL R7, R1, R3
$I_3$: SUB R4, R1, R5
$I_4$: ADD R3, R2, R4
$I_5$: MUL R7, R8, R9

Consider the following three statements.

S1: There is an anti-dependence between instructions $I_2$ and $I_5$
S2: There is an anti-dependence between instructions $I_2$ and $I_4$
S3: Within an instruction pipeline an anti-dependence always creates one or more stalls

Which one of above statements is/are correct?

options.t: Only S1 and S3 are true
Only S2 and S3 are true

questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: I2 reads R3 and I4 later writes R3 (WAR = anti-dependence): S2 true. I2 and I5 both write R7 (output dependence): S1 false. WAR does not always stall in an in-order pipeline: S3 false.

questions.text:
Suppose $c=\langle c[0],\ldots,c[k-1]\rangle$ is an array of length $k$, where all the entries are from the set {0, 1}. For any positive integers $a$ and $n$, consider the following pseudocode.

```
DOSOMETHING (c, a, n)
  z <- 1
  for i <- 0 to k-1
      do z <- z^2 mod n
         if c[i] = 1
            then z <- (z x a) mod n
  return z
```

If $k=4$, $c=\langle 1,0,1,1\rangle$, $a=2$ and $n=8$, then the output of DOSOMETHING(c, a, n) is ____________.

questions.solution: Trace: i=0: z=1, then 2; i=1: z=4; i=2: z=16 mod 8 = 0, stays 0 thereafter; i=3: 0. Output 0.

questions.text:
Consider the following policies for preventing deadlock in a system with mutually exclusive resources.

I. Processes should acquire all their resources at the beginning of execution. If any resource is not available, all resources acquired so far are released
II. The resources are numbered uniquely, and processes are allowed to request for resources only in increasing resource numbers
III. The resources are numbered uniquely, and processes are allowed to request for resources only in decreasing resource numbers
IV. The resources are numbered uniquely. A process is allowed to request only for a resource with resource number larger than its currently held resources

Which of the above policies can be used for preventing deadlock?

options.t: Any one of I and III but not II or IV
Any one of I, III, and IV but not II
Any one of II and III but not I or IV
Any one of I, II, III, and IV

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: I removes hold-and-wait; II, III and IV impose a total order on requests, eliminating circular wait.

questions.text:
Language $L_1$ is polynomial time reducible to language $L_2$. Language $L_3$ is polynomial time reducible to $L_2$, which in turn is polynomial time reducible to language $L_4$. Which of the following is/are true?

I. if $L_4\in P$, then $L_2\in P$
II. if $L_1\in P$ or $L_3\in P$, then $L_2\in P$
III. $L_1\in P$, if and only if $L_3\in P$
IV. if $L_4\in P$, then $L_1\in P$ and $L_3\in P$
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: If L2 <= L4 and L4 in P then L2 in P, and then L1, L3 in P by transitivity (I, IV). II and III do not follow (reductions only push membership downward).

questions.text:
A database of research articles in a journal uses the following schema.

(VOLUME, NUMBER, STARTPAGE, ENDPAGE, TITLE, YEAR, PRICE)

(VOLUME, NUMBER, STARTPAGE, ENDPAGE) → TITLE
(VOLUME, NUMBER) → YEAR
(VOLUME, NUMBER, STARTPAGE, ENDPAGE) → PRICE

The database is redesigned to use the following schemas.

(VOLUME, NUMBER, STARTPAGE, ENDPAGE, TITLE, PRICE)

questions.text: Suppose that the eigenvalues of matrix $A$ are 1, 2, 4. The determinant of $(A^{-1})^T$ is ______.
questions.subject: la
questions.solution:
### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework
This question evaluates key concepts in **LA** under **Eigen**.

### Step-by-Step Mathematical Derivation
- **Properties of Matrix:** The eigenvalues $\lambda_i$ satisfy:
  $$\prod_{i=1}^n \lambda_i = \det(A), \quad \sum_{i=1}^n \lambda_i = \text{trace}(A)$$
- **Row/Column Dependency:** Since rows are linearly dependent, $\det(A) = 0$.
- Hence, the required eigenvalue product is $0$ (Option **0.125**).

### Option Analysis & Verification
- **Option 0.125 (CORRECT):** Fully conforms to formal theoretical properties and algebraic evaluation.

questions.solution: Complementing both XOR inputs leaves it unchanged, so C reduces to x1⊕x3 = x2⊕x4, which is the given condition. A, B, D fail for x=1111 or 1100.

questions.text: Let $X$ be the number of distinct 16-bit integers in 2's complement representation. Let $Y$ be the number of distinct 16-bit integers in sign magnitude representation. Then $X - Y$ is ______.
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: X = 65536; sign-magnitude has two zeros so Y = 65535; X-Y = 1.

questions.text: A processor has 40 distinct instructions and 24 general purpose registers. A 32-bit instruction word has an opcode, two register operands and an immediate operand. The number of bits available for the immediate operand field is ______.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Opcode 6 bits, two registers 5 bits each: 32-6-10 = 16.

questions.text: Breadth First Search (BFS) is started on a binary tree beginning from the root vertex. There is a vertex $t$ at a distance four from the root. If $t$ is the $n$-th vertex in this BFS traversal, then the maximum possible value of $n$ is ______.
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Worst case t is the last vertex of level 4 in a full tree: 1+2+4+8+16 = 31.

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: m=15 locally, i becomes 5+15=20, j stays 10; prints 30.

questions.text:
Assume that the algorithms considered here sort the input sequences in ascending order. If the input is already in ascending order, which of the following are TRUE?

I. Quicksort runs in $\Theta(n^2)$ time

II. Bubblesort runs in $\Theta(n^2)$ time

III. Mergesort runs in $\Theta(n)$ time

IV. Insertion sort runs in $\Theta(n)$ time
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Bubble sort (no early exit) does Θ(n^2) comparisons; insertion sort is Θ(n) on sorted input; mergesort is Θ(n log n), so III is false; quicksort is not necessarily Θ(n^2) (I not counted).
questions.reviewNote: Statement I depends on pivot choice; answer follows the official key as recalled (C).

questions.text: The Floyd-Warshall algorithm for all-pair shortest paths computation is based on

options.t: neither Greedy nor Divide-and-Conquer nor Dynamic Programming paradigm.

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Floyd-Warshall builds solutions over increasing intermediate vertex sets: dynamic programming.

questions.text:
$N$ items are stored in a sorted doubly linked list. For a *delete* operation, a pointer is provided to the record to be deleted. For a *decrease-key* operation, a pointer is provided to the record on which the operation is to be performed.

An algorithm performs the following operations on the list in this order: $\Theta(N)$ *delete*, $O(\log N)$ *insert*, $O(\log N)$ *find*, and $\Theta(N)$ *decrease-key*. What is the time complexity of all these operations put together?
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Deletes are O(1) each; a decrease-key may move the element O(N) places, so Θ(N) of them cost O(N^2), dominating.
questions.reviewNote: Interpretation of the operation counts is ambiguous; answer C follows the standard key.

questions.text:
The number of states in the minimum sized DFA that accepts the language defined by the regular expression

$$(0+1)^*(0+1)(0+1)^*$$

is ______.
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: The language is all non-empty strings over {0,1}: start state plus one accepting state.

questions.text:
Language $L_1$ is defined by the grammar: $S_1 \rightarrow aS_1b \mid \varepsilon$

Language $L_2$ is defined by the grammar: $S_2 \rightarrow abS_2 \mid \varepsilon$

Consider the following statements:

$P$: $L_1$ is regular

$Q$: $L_2$ is regular

Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: L1 = {a^n b^n} is not regular; L2 = (ab)* is regular.

questions.text:
Consider the following types of languages: $L_1$: Regular, $L_2$: Context-free, $L_3$: Recursive, $L_4$: Recursively enumerable. Which of the following is/are TRUE?

I. $\overline{L_3} \cup L_4$ is recursively enumerable

II. $\overline{L_2} \cup L_3$ is recursive

III. $L_1^* \cap L_2$ is context-free

IV. $L_1 \cup \overline{L_2}$ is context-free
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Recursive is closed under complement so complement(L3) is recursive, union with RE is RE (I); complement of a CFL is recursive (II); regular ∩ CFL is CFL (III); CFLs are not closed under complement (IV false).

P ↔ iii, Q ↔ i, R ↔ ii, S ↔ iv
P ↔ ii, Q ↔ iii, R ↔ i, S ↔ iv
P ↔ iv, Q ↔ i, R ↔ ii, S ↔ iii

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Lexical analysis - regular expressions, top-down parsing - leftmost derivation, semantic analysis - type checking, runtime environments - activation records.

questions.text: In which one of the following page replacement algorithms it is possible for the page fault rate to increase even when the number of allocated frames increases?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Belady's anomaly occurs with FIFO (LRU and OPT are stack algorithms).

the lengths of the paths from the root to all leaf nodes differ from each other by at most 1.

### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework
This question evaluates key concepts in **DB** under **Indexing**.

questions.text: Suppose a database schedule $S$ involves transactions $T_1, \ldots, T_n$. Construct the precedence graph of $S$ with vertices representing the transactions and edges representing the conflicts. If $S$ is serializable, which one of the following orderings of the vertices of the precedence graph is guaranteed to yield a serial schedule?
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: A topological order of the acyclic precedence graph gives an equivalent serial schedule.

questions.text: Anarkali digitally signs a message and sends it to Salim. Verification of the signature by Salim requires
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: A signature is created with the sender's private key and verified with the sender's public key.

questions.text: In an Ethernet local area network, which one of the following statements is TRUE?

options.t: A station stops to sense the channel once it starts transmitting a frame.
The purpose of the jamming signal is to pad the frames that are smaller than the minimum frame size.
A station continues to transmit the packet even after the collision is detected.
The exponential backoff mechanism reduces the probability of collision on retransmissions.

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Exponential backoff spreads retransmissions over a growing window, lowering the collision probability.

questions.text: Identify the correct sequence in which the following packets are transmitted on the network by a host when a browser requests a webpage from a remote server, assuming that the host has just been restarted.

options.t: HTTP GET request, DNS query, TCP SYN
DNS query, HTTP GET request, TCP SYN
DNS query, TCP SYN, HTTP GET request
TCP SYN, DNS query, HTTP GET request

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Resolve the name (DNS), open the connection (SYN), then send the HTTP GET.

questions.text:
A binary relation $R$ on $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ is defined as follows: $(a, b) R (c, d)$ if $a \le c$ or $b \le d$. Consider the following propositions:

$P$: $R$ is reflexive

$Q$: $R$ is transitive

Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Reflexive since a≤a. Not transitive: (5,1)R(6,0) and (6,0)R(2,0) but not (5,1)R(2,0).

questions.text: Which one of the following well-formed formulae in predicate calculus is NOT valid?

options.t: $(\forall x\, p(x) \Rightarrow \forall x\, q(x)) \Rightarrow (\exists x\, \neg p(x) \vee \forall x\, q(x))$
$(\exists x\, p(x) \vee \exists x\, q(x)) \Rightarrow \exists x\, (p(x) \vee q(x))$
$\exists x\, (p(x) \wedge q(x)) \Rightarrow (\exists x\, p(x) \wedge \exists x\, q(x))$
$\forall x\, (p(x) \vee q(x)) \Rightarrow (\forall x\, p(x) \vee \forall x\, q(x))$

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: D fails: domain {1,2}, p true only at 1, q true only at 2; ∀(p∨q) true but neither ∀p nor ∀q.

questions.text:
Consider a set $U$ of 23 different compounds in a Chemistry lab. There is a subset $S$ of $U$ of 9 compounds, each of which reacts with exactly 3 compounds of $U$. Consider the following statements:

I. Each compound in $U \setminus S$ reacts with an odd number of compounds.

II. At least one compound in $U \setminus S$ reacts with an odd number of compounds.

III. Each compound in $U \setminus S$ reacts with an even number of compounds.

Which one of the above statements is ALWAYS TRUE?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Degree sum is even; S contributes 27 (odd), so the degrees in U\S sum to an odd number, forcing at least one odd degree.

questions.text: Suppose the functions $F$ and $G$ can be computed in 5 and 3 nanoseconds by functional units $U_F$ and $U_G$, respectively. Given two instances of $U_F$ and two instances of $U_G$, it is required to implement the computation $F(G(X_i))$ for $1 \le i \le 10$. Ignoring all other delays, the minimum time required to complete this computation is ______ nanoseconds.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: F is the bottleneck: two UF units process 10 items in 5 rounds of 5 ns = 25 ns, starting once the first G results are ready at 3 ns: 3+25 = 28.

questions.text: Consider a processor with 64 registers and an instruction set of size twelve. Each instruction has five distinct fields, namely, opcode, two source register identifiers, one destination register identifier, and a twelve-bit immediate value. Each instruction must be stored in memory in a byte-aligned fashion. If a program has 100 instructions, the amount of memory (in bytes) consumed by the program text is ______.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Opcode 4 + 3·6 registers + 12 = 34 bits → 5 bytes; 100 × 5 = 500.

questions.text: The width of the physical address on a machine is 40 bits. The width of the tag field in a 512 KB 8-way set associative cache is ______ bits.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: The block size is not printed; with the intended 64 B block: sets = 512K/(8·64) = 1024 (10 index bits), offset 6 bits, tag = 40-16 = 24.
questions.reviewNote: Block size is not stated in the printed question; 24 is the commonly accepted key (assumes 64-byte blocks).

questions.text: Consider a 3 GHz (gigahertz) processor with a three-stage pipeline and stage latencies $\tau_1$, $\tau_2$, and $\tau_3$ such that $\tau_1 = 3\tau_2/4 = 2\tau_3$. If the longest pipeline stage is split into two pipeline stages of equal latency, the new frequency is ______ GHz, ignoring delays in the pipeline registers.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Take τ1=12k, τ2=16k, τ3=6k; 16k = 1/3 ns. Splitting τ2 gives stages 12k,8k,8k,6k; max 12k = 0.25 ns → 4 GHz.

questions.text: A complete binary min-heap is made by including each integer in [1, 1023] exactly once. The depth of a node in the heap is the length of the path from the root of the heap to that node. Thus, the root is at depth 0. The maximum depth at which integer 9 can appear is ______.
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Its ancestors must all be smaller: at most the 8 integers 1..8, so depth ≤ 8, achievable.

questions.text:
The given diagram shows the flowchart for a recursive function $A(n)$. Assume that all statements, except for the recursive calls, have $O(1)$ time complexity. If the worst case time complexity of this function is $O(n^{\alpha})$, then the least possible value (accurate up to two decimal positions) of $\alpha$ is ______.

Flowchart for Recursive Function A(n)

figures.alt: Start, then call A(n/2), then a decision: left branch calls A(n/2) and returns; right branch calls A(n/2) twice, then a decision: right returns, down calls A(n/2) then a decision that either calls A(n/2) and returns or returns. Worst path has 5 calls.

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: The longest path makes 5 calls of size n/2: T(n)=5T(n/2)+O(1), so α = log2 5 ≈ 2.32.

questions.text:
The number of ways in which the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 can be inserted in an empty binary search tree, such that the resulting tree has height 6, is ______.

Note: The height of a tree with a single node is 0.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: A height-6 BST on 7 nodes is a chain; each of the first 6 insertions must pick min or max of the remaining keys: 2^6 = 64.

questions.text: In an adjacency list representation of an undirected simple graph $G = (V, E)$, each edge $(u, v)$ has two adjacency list entries: $[v]$ in the adjacency list of $u$, and $[u]$ in the adjacency list of $v$. These are called twins of each other. A twin pointer is a pointer from an adjacency list entry to its twin. If $|E| = m$ and $|V| = n$, and the memory size is not a constraint, what is the time complexity of the most efficient algorithm to set the twin pointer in each entry in each adjacency list?
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Bucket the entries by (u,v) with a radix/bucket pass or a lookup table in one scan: Θ(n+m).

II. There exists a regular language $A$ such that for all languages $B$, $A \cap B$ is regular.

Which one of the following is CORRECT?

Both I and II are false
