Which one of the following is TRUE?

options.t: $L_1$ is context-free while $L_2$ is not context-free.
$L_2$ is context-free while $L_1$ is not context-free.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: L1 has a CFG/PDA (match a's and b's against c's with a stack); L2 needs two independent comparisons and is not context-free.

questions.text:
Consider the following languages.

$L_1 = \{\langle M \rangle \mid M$ takes at least 2016 steps on some input$\}$,

$L_2 = \{\langle M \rangle \mid M$ takes at least 2016 steps on all inputs$\}$ and

$L_3 = \{\langle M \rangle \mid M$ accepts $\varepsilon\}$,

where for each Turing machine $M$, $\langle M \rangle$ denotes a specific encoding of $M$. Which one of the following is TRUE?

options.t: $L_1$ is recursive and $L_2$, $L_3$ are not recursive
$L_2$ is recursive and $L_1$, $L_3$ are not recursive
$L_1$, $L_2$ are recursive and $L_3$ is not recursive

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: In 2016 steps M reads at most 2016 input symbols, so only finitely many inputs need simulation: L1 and L2 decidable; L3 is undecidable (Rice).

questions.text: Which one of the following grammars is free from left recursion?

questions.text:
A student wrote two context-free grammars $G1$ and $G2$ for generating a single C-like array declaration. The dimension of the array is at least one. For example,

The grammars use $D$ as the start symbol, and use six terminal symbols `int ; id [ ] num`.

| Grammar G1 | Grammar G2 |
|---|---|
| $D \to$ int $L$; | $D \to$ int $L$; |

| $E \to$ num ] [ $E$ | $E \to$ [ num ] |

Which of the grammars correctly generate the declaration mentioned above?
questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: G1 derives int id [ num ] [ num ] ; via E→num][E; G2 derives id followed by one or more [num] via E→E[num]|[num].

questions.text:
Consider the following two-process synchronization solution.

```
Process 0                              Process 1
---------                              ----------
Entry: loop while (turn == 1);         Entry: loop while (turn == 0);
  (critical section)                     (critical section)
Exit: turn = 1;                        Exit: turn = 0;
```

The shared variable turn is initialized to zero. Which one of the following is TRUE?

options.t: This is a correct two-process synchronization solution.
This solution violates mutual exclusion requirement.
This solution violates bounded wait requirement.

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Strict alternation: if process 1 never enters, process 0 cannot enter twice in a row, so progress is violated.

questions.text: Consider a non-negative counting semaphore $S$. The operation $P(S)$ decrements $S$, and $V(S)$ increments $S$. During an execution, 20 $P(S)$ operations and 12 $V(S)$ operations are issued in some order. The largest initial value of $S$ for which at least one $P(S)$ operation will remain blocked is ______.

questions.text:
A file system uses an in-memory cache to cache disk blocks. The miss rate of the cache is shown in the figure. The latency to read a block from the cache is 1 ms and to read a block from the disk is 10 ms. Assume that the cost of checking whether a block exists in the cache is negligible. Available cache sizes are in multiples of 10 MB.

The smallest cache size required to ensure an average read latency of less than 6 ms is ______ MB.

figures.alt: Line plot of miss rate (%) against cache size (MB): 10MB→80, 20→60, 30→40, 40→35, 50→30, 60→25, 70→20, 80→15.

questions.solution: Latency = (1-m)·1 + m·10 < 6 → m < 5/9 ≈ 55.6%; first size with miss rate below that is 30 MB (40%).

questions.text:
Consider the following database schedule with two transactions, $T_1$ and $T_2$.

$S = r_2(X); r_1(X); r_2(Y); w_1(X); r_1(Y); w_2(X); a_1; a_2$

where $r_i(Z)$ denotes a *read* operation by transaction $T_i$ on a variable $Z$, $w_i(Z)$ denotes a *write* operation by $T_i$ on a variable $Z$ and $a_i$ denotes an *abort* by transaction $T_i$.

Which one of the following statements about the above schedule is TRUE?

options.t: $S$ is recoverable, but has a cascading abort
$S$ does not have a cascading abort

questions.solution: No transaction reads a value written by an uncommitted transaction, so recoverable with no cascading abort; but w2(X) overwrites T1's uncommitted write, so not strict.

questions.text: A network has a data transmission bandwidth of $20 \times 10^6$ bits per second. It uses CSMA/CD in the MAC layer. The maximum signal propagation time from one node to another node is 40 microseconds. The minimum size of a frame in the network is ______ bytes.

questions.text:
For the IEEE 802.11 MAC protocol for wireless communication, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

I. At least three non-overlapping channels are available for transmissions.

II. The RTS-CTS mechanism is used for collision detection.

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: 802.11 b/g has channels 1, 6, 11 non-overlapping; RTS-CTS avoids (hidden-terminal) collisions rather than detecting them; unicast frames are acknowledged.

questions.text: Consider a $128 \times 10^3$ bits/second satellite communication link with one way propagation delay of 150 milliseconds. Selective retransmission (repeat) protocol is used on this link to send data with a frame size of 1 kilobyte. Neglect the transmission time of acknowledgement. The minimum number of bits required for the sequence number field to achieve 100% utilization is ______.
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Frame time = 8192/128000 = 64 ms; window = 1 + 2·150/64 ≈ 5.7 → 6 frames; selective repeat needs 2W = 12 sequence numbers → 4 bits.

questions.text: Let $c_1,\ldots,c_n$ be scalars, not all zero, such that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} c_i a_i = 0$ where $a_i$ are column vectors in $\mathbf{R}^n$. Consider the set of linear equations $Ax=b$ where $A=[a_1,\ldots,a_n]$ and $b=\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i$. The set of equations has

questions.text: When two 8-bit numbers $A_7\cdots A_0$ and $B_7\cdots B_0$ in 2's complement representation (with $A_0$ and $B_0$ as the least significant bits) are added using a **ripple-carry adder**, the sum bits obtained are $S_7\cdots S_0$ and the carry bits are $C_7\cdots C_0$. Besides, $T_1$ holds a lock on the resource R, and $T_2$ has requested a conflicting lock on the same resource R. The following algorithm is used to prevent deadlocks in the database system assuming that a killed transaction is restarted with the same timestamp.

```
if TS(T2) < TS(T1) then
    T1 is killed
else T2 waits.
```

Assume any transaction that is not killed terminates eventually. Which of the following is TRUE about the database system that uses the above algorithm to prevent deadlocks?

options.t: The database system is both deadlock-free and starvation-free.
The database system is deadlock-free, but not starvation-free.
The database system is starvation-free, but not deadlock-free.
The database system is neither deadlock-free nor starvation-free.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: This is wound-wait: an older requester kills the younger holder, a younger requester waits, so waits only go from younger to older (no cycle). Restart keeps the timestamp so a transaction eventually becomes oldest: no starvation.

questions.text: Consider a long-lived TCP session with an end-to-end bandwidth of 1 Gbps (= $10^9$ bits-per-second). The session starts with a sequence number of 1234. The minimum time (in seconds, rounded to the closest integer) before this sequence number can be used again is _______.
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: 32-bit byte sequence space: $2^{32}\times8/10^9\approx34.4$ s ≈ 34.

questions.text:
Consider a matrix P whose only eigenvectors are the multiples of $\begin{pmatrix}1\\4\end{pmatrix}$.

Consider the following statements.

(I) P does not have an inverse

(II) P has a repeated eigenvalue

(III) P cannot be diagonalized

Which one of the following options is correct?

options.t: Only I and III are necessarily true
Only I and II are necessarily true
Only II and III are necessarily true

questions.subject: la
questions.solution: Only one independent eigenvector: eigenvalue repeated and P not diagonalizable; invertibility not forced.

questions.text:
Let N be the set of natural numbers. Consider the following sets.

P: Set of Rational numbers (positive and negative)

Q: Set of functions from {0, 1} to N

R: Set of functions from N to {0, 1}

S: Set of finite subsets of N.

Which of the sets above are countable?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: P, Q ($\cong N\times N$) and S are countable; R ($2^N$) is uncountable.

questions.text:
Consider the first-order logic sentence

$$\varphi \equiv \exists s\exists t\exists u\forall v\forall w\forall x\forall y\ \psi(s,t,u,v,w,x,y)$$

where $\psi(s,t,u,v,w,x,y)$ is a quantifier-free first-order logic formula using only predicate symbols, and possibly equality, but no function symbols. Suppose $\varphi$ has a model with a universe containing 7 elements.

Which one of the following statements is necessarily true?

options.t: There exists at least one model of $\varphi$ with universe of size less than or equal to 3.
There exists no model of $\varphi$ with universe of size less than or equal to 3.
There exists no model of $\varphi$ with universe of size greater than 7.
Every model of $\varphi$ has a universe of size equal to 7.

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Restrict the model to the three existential witnesses; universal sentences persist in substructures, giving a model of size at most 3.

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: fun1 swaps local copies only: "Hi Bye "; fun2 swaps the actual pointers: "Bye Hi".

questions.text:
Let G be a simple undirected graph. Let $T_D$ be a depth first search tree of G. Let $T_B$ be a breadth first search tree of G. Consider the following statements.

(I) No edge of G is a cross edge with respect to $T_D$. (A cross edge in G is between two nodes neither of which is an ancestor of the other in $T_D$.)

(II) For every edge $(u,v)$ of G, if $u$ is at depth $i$ and $v$ is at depth $j$ in $T_B$, then $|i - j| = 1$.

Which of the statements above must necessarily be true?
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Undirected DFS has no cross edges; BFS can have edges between nodes at the same depth (|i-j|=0).

questions.text:
Assume that multiplying a matrix $G_1$ of dimension $p \times q$ with another matrix $G_2$ of dimension $q \times r$ requires $pqr$ scalar multiplications. Computing the product of $n$ matrices $G_1G_2G_3\ldots G_n$ can be done by parenthesizing in different ways. Define $G_i G_{i+1}$ as an explicitly computed pair for a given parenthesization if they are directly multiplied. For example, in the matrix multiplication chain $G_1G_2G_3G_4G_5G_6$ using parenthesization $(G_1(G_2G_3))(G_4(G_5G_6))$, $G_2G_3$ and $G_5G_6$ are the only explicitly computed pairs.

Consider a matrix multiplication chain $F_1F_2F_3F_4F_5$, where matrices $F_1, F_2, F_3, F_4$ and $F_5$ are of dimensions $2\times25$, $25\times3$, $3\times16$, $16\times1$ and $1\times1000$, respectively. In the parenthesization of $F_1F_2F_3F_4F_5$ that minimizes the total number of scalar multiplications, the explicitly computed pairs is/are
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Optimal is $(F_1(F_2(F_3F_4)))F_5$ with cost 2173; only $F_3F_4$ is an explicitly computed pair.

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: First loop: j=40. Second loop: j=40,20,10,5,2 satisfy j>1, so sum=5.

questions.text:
Consider the unsigned 8-bit fixed point binary number representation below,

$b_7\ b_6\ b_5\ b_4\ b_3\ .\ b_2\ b_1\ b_0$

where the position of the binary point is between $b_3$ and $b_2$. Assume $b_7$ is the most significant bit. Some of the decimal numbers listed below cannot be represented exactly in the above representation:

(i) 31.500  (ii) 0.875  (iii) 12.100  (iv) 3.001

Which one of the following statements is true?

options.t: None of (i), (ii), (iii), (iv) can be exactly represented
Only (iii) and (iv) cannot be exactly represented
Only (i) and (ii) cannot be exactly represented

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: 3 fractional bits: multiples of 0.125 only. 31.5 (11111.100) and 0.875 (0.111) fit; 12.1 and 3.001 do not.

questions.text: The size of the physical address space of a processor is $2^P$ bytes. The word length is $2^W$ bytes. The capacity of cache memory is $2^N$ bytes. The size of each cache block is $2^M$ words. For a $K$-way set-associative cache memory, the length (in number of bits) of the tag field is
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Sets $=2^{N-M-W}/K$; tag $=P-(N-M-W-\log_2K)-(M+W)=P-N+\log_2K$.

questions.text:
Consider the following languages:

I. $\{a^m b^n c^p d^q \mid m + p = n + q,\ \text{where } m,n,p,q \ge 0\}$

II. $\{a^m b^n c^p d^q \mid m = n \text{ and } p = q,\ \text{where } m,n,p,q \ge 0\}$

III. $\{a^m b^n c^p d^q \mid m = n = p \text{ and } p \ne q,\ \text{where } m,n,p,q \ge 0\}$

IV. $\{a^m b^n c^p d^q \mid mn = p + q,\ \text{where } m,n,p,q \ge 0\}$

Which of the languages above are context-free?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: I and II are CFLs (nested/concatenated matching); III needs three-way equality and IV a product, neither is CFL.

questions.text:
Consider the following problems. $L(G)$ denotes the language generated by a grammar $G$. $L(M)$ denotes the language accepted by a machine $M$.

(I) For an unrestricted grammar $G$ and a string $w$, whether $w \in L(G)$

(II) Given a Turing machine $M$, whether $L(M)$ is regular

(III) Given two grammars $G_1$ and $G_2$, whether $L(G_1) = L(G_2)$

(IV) Given an NFA $N$, whether there is a deterministic PDA $P$ such that $N$ and $P$ accept the same language.

Which one of the following statements is correct?

options.t: Only I and II are undecidable
Only II and IV are undecidable
Only I, II and III are undecidable

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: I, II (Rice) and III are undecidable; IV is trivially yes (every regular language is DCFL), hence decidable.

questions.text:
A lexical analyzer uses the following patterns to recognize three tokens $T_1$, $T_2$, and $T_3$ over the alphabet $\{a,b,c\}$.

$T_1$: $a?\,(b|c)^*\,a$

$T_2$: $b?\,(a|c)^*\,b$

$T_3$: $c?\,(b|a)^*\,c$

Note that 'x?' means 0 or 1 occurrence of the symbol x. Note also that the analyzer outputs the token that matches the longest possible prefix.

If the string $bbaacabc$ is processed by the analyzer, which one of the following is the sequence of tokens it outputs?
questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: On bbaacabc: T1 matches "bba"(3), T2 "bb"(2), T3 "bbaac"(5) so T3. On "abc": T1 "a", T2 "ab", T3 "abc"(3) so T3.

questions.text:
Consider the following parse tree for the expression `a#b$c$d#e#f`, involving two binary operators $ and #.

Which one of the following is correct for the given parse tree?

options.t: $ has higher precedence and is left associative; # is right associative
# has higher precedence and is left associative; $ is right associative
$ has higher precedence and is left associative; # is left associative
# has higher precedence and is right associative; $ is left associative

figures.alt: Root # with left child a and right child #. That # has left child $ and right child # (children e, f). The $ has left child $ (children b, c) and right child d.

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Tree: a # ((($b$c)$d) # (e#f)); $ binds tighter and groups left ((b$c)$d); # groups right.

questions.text:
In a system, there are three types of resources: E, F and G. Four processes P0, P1, P2 and P3 execute concurrently. At the outset, the processes have declared their maximum resource requirements using a matrix named Max as given below. For example, Max[P2,F] is the maximum number of instances of F that P2 would require. The number of instances of the resources allocated to the various processes at any given state is given by a matrix named Allocation.

Consider a state of the system with the Allocation matrix as shown below, and in which 3 instances of E and 3 instances of F are the only resources available.

| | Alloc E | Alloc F | Alloc G | Max E | Max F | Max G |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 4 | 3 | 1 |
| P1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 4 |
| P2 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 1 | 3 | 3 |
| P3 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 5 | 4 | 1 |

From the perspective of deadlock avoidance, which one of the following is true?

options.t: The system is in safe state.
The system is not in safe state, but would be safe if one more instance of E were available
The system is not in safe state, but would be safe if one more instance of F were available
The system is not in safe state, but would be safe if one more instance of G were available

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Need: P0 330, P1 102, P2 030, P3 341; available (3,3,0). Order P0, P2, P1, P3 completes: safe.

options.t: P: full, Q: full, R: empty, S: empty
P: empty, Q: empty, R: full, S: full
P: full, Q: empty, R: empty, S: full
P: empty, Q: full, R: full, S: empty

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: In this naming, "full" counts slots for the producer (initially N). Producer waits full, signals empty; consumer waits empty, signals full.

questions.text:
Consider the relations r(A, B) and s(B, C), where s.B is a primary key and r.B is a foreign key referencing s.B. Consider the query

$Q: r \bowtie (\sigma_{B<5}(s))$

Let LOJ denote the natural left outer-join operation. Assume that r and s contain no null values.

Which one of the following queries is NOT equivalent to Q?
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: (C) keeps r tuples with B≥5, padded with nulls, so it has extra tuples; others are equivalent thanks to the foreign key.

questions.text:
Consider the following four relational schemas. For each schema, all non-trivial functional dependencies are listed. The underlined attributes are the respective primary keys.

Schema I: Registration (rollno, courses)
Field 'courses' is a set-valued attribute containing the set of courses a student has registered for.
Non-trivial functional dependency: rollno → courses

Schema II: Registration (rollno, courseid, email)
Non-trivial functional dependencies: rollno, courseid → email; email → rollno

Schema III: Registration (rollno, courseid, marks, grade)
Non-trivial functional dependencies: rollno, courseid → marks, grade; marks → grade

Schema IV: Registration (rollno, courseid, credit)
Non-trivial functional dependencies: rollno, courseid → credit; courseid → credit

Which one of the relational schemas above is in 3NF but not in BCNF?
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: II: email→rollno with rollno prime: 3NF but email not a superkey so not BCNF. I not 1NF, III has transitive dep, IV has partial dep.
questions.reviewNote: Primary-key underlines not visible in the text layer; answer assumes key (rollno, courseid) in every schema.

questions.text: Let G be a graph with 100! vertices, with each vertex labelled by a distinct permutation of the numbers 1,2, … , 100. There is an edge between vertices $u$ and $v$ if and only if the label of $u$ can be obtained by swapping two adjacent numbers in the label of $v$. Let $y$ denote the degree of a vertex in G, and $z$ denote the number of connected components in G. Then, $y + 10z =$ _____.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Each vertex has 99 adjacent swaps (y=99); adjacent transpositions generate all permutations so z=1: 99+10=109.

questions.text:
Consider Guwahati (G) and Delhi (D) whose temperatures can be classified as high (H), medium (M) and low (L). Let $P(H_G)$ denote the probability that Guwahati has high temperature. Similarly, $P(M_G)$ and $P(L_G)$ denotes the probability of Guwahati having medium and low temperatures respectively. Similarly, we use $P(H_D)$, $P(M_D)$ and $P(L_D)$ for Delhi.

The following table gives the conditional probabilities for Delhi's temperature given Guwahati's temperature.

| | $H_D$ | $M_D$ | $L_D$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $H_G$ | 0.40 | 0.48 | 0.12 |
| $M_G$ | 0.10 | 0.65 | 0.25 |
| $L_G$ | 0.01 | 0.50 | 0.49 |

Consider the first row in the table above. The first entry denotes that if Guwahati has high temperature ($H_G$) then the probability of Delhi also having a high temperature ($H_D$) is 0.40; i.e., $P(H_D|H_G) = 0.40$. Similarly, the next two entries are $P(M_D|H_G) = 0.48$ and $P(L_D|H_G) = 0.12$. Similarly for the other rows.

If it is known that $P(H_G) = 0.2$, $P(M_G) = 0.5$, and $P(L_G) = 0.3$, then the probability (correct to two decimal places) that Guwahati has high temperature given that Delhi has high temperature is _______.
questions.subject: prob
pds
questions.solution: Each y from 1024 down to 2 (1023 values) prints 10 times (x=1024..2): 10230.

questions.text: The number of possible min-heaps containing each value from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7} exactly once is _____.
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Root=1; left/right subtree sizes 3,3: $\binom63\cdot2\cdot2=80$ (each 3-node heap has 2 arrangements).

questions.text: Consider the following undirected graph G. Choose a value for $x$ that will maximize the number of minimum weight spanning trees (MWSTs) of G. The number of MWSTs of G for this value of $x$ is ______.

figures.alt: Pentagon-like graph on 5 unlabelled vertices: top T, left L, right R, bottom-left BL, bottom-right BR. Edges: T-L 4, T-R x, T-BL 1, T-BR 3, L-BL 4, BL-BR 4, R-BR 5.

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Edges of weight 1 and 3 are forced. Left vertex can connect by either of two weight-4 edges (2 ways); with x=5 the right vertex has two equal-weight choices (2 ways): 4 trees.

questions.text:
Consider the weights and values of items listed below. Note that there is only one unit of each item.

| Item number | Weight (in Kgs) | Value (in Rupees) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10 | 60 |
| 2 | 7 | 28 |
| 3 | 4 | 20 |
| 4 | 2 | 24 |

The task is to pick a subset of these items such that their total weight is no more than 11 Kgs and their total value is maximized. Moreover, no item may be split. The total value of items picked by an optimal algorithm is denoted by $V_{opt}$. A greedy algorithm sorts the items by their value-to-weight ratios in descending order and packs them greedily, starting from the first item in the ordered list. The total value of items picked by the greedy algorithm is denoted by $V_{greedy}$.

The value of $V_{opt} - V_{greedy}$ is ____________.
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Greedy picks items 4 then 3 (ratio order 4,1,3,2; item 1 does not fit): 44. Optimal is item 1 alone: 60. Difference 16.

questions.text:
Consider the minterm list form of a Boolean function $F$ given below.

$$F(P,Q,R,S)=\sum m(0,2,5,7,9,11)+d(3,8,10,12,14)$$

Here, $m$ denotes a minterm and $d$ denotes a don't care term. The number of essential prime implicants of the function $F$ is ______.
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Prime implicants: $\bar Q\bar S$, $\bar QR$, $P\bar Q$, $P\bar S$, $\bar PQS$, $\bar PRS$. Essential: $\bar Q\bar S$ (m0), $\bar PQS$ (m5), $P\bar Q$ (m9): 3.

questions.text:
The instruction pipeline of a RISC processor has the following stages: Instruction Fetch (IF), Instruction Decode (ID), Operand Fetch (OF), Perform Operation (PO) and Writeback (WB). The IF, ID, OF and WB stages take 1 clock cycle each for every instruction. Consider a sequence of 100 instructions. In the PO stage, 40 instructions take 3 clock cycles each, 35 instructions take 2 clock cycles each, and the remaining 25 instructions take 1 clock cycle each. Assume that there are no data hazards and no control hazards.

The number of clock cycles required for completion of execution of the sequence of instructions is ______.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Ideal 5+99=104 cycles plus stalls 40×2+35×1=115: 219.

questions.text:
A processor has 16 integer registers (R0, R1, .. , R15) and 64 floating point registers (F0, F1,… , F63). It uses a 2-byte instruction format. There are four categories of instructions: Type-1, Type-2, Type-3, and Type-4. Type-1 category consists of four instructions, each with 3 integer register operands (3Rs). Type-2 category consists of eight instructions, each with 2 floating point register operands (2Fs). Type-3 category consists of fourteen instructions, each with one integer register operand and one floating point register operand (1R+1F). Type-4 category consists of N instructions, each with a floating point register operand (1F).

The maximum value of N is __________.

questions.text:
Given a language $L$, define $L^i$ as follows:

$L^0=\{\varepsilon\}$

$L^i=L^{i-1}\cdot L$ for all $i>0$

The order of a language $L$ is defined as the smallest $k$ such that $L^k=L^{k+1}$. Consider the language $L_1$ (over alphabet 0) accepted by the following automaton.

The order of $L_1$ is _____.

figures.alt: Three states: start state q0 (accepting) --0--> q1 (accepting); q1 --0--> q2 (non-accepting); q2 --0--> q1.

questions.solution: $L_1=\{\varepsilon\}\cup\{0^{odd}\}$. $L^1\ne L^2$ (00 missing), but $L^2=0^*=L^3$. Order 2.

questions.text:
Consider a storage disk with 4 platters (numbered as 0, 1, 2 and 3), 200 cylinders (numbered as 0, 1, … , 199), and 256 sectors per track (numbered as 0, 1, … , 255). The following 6 disk requests of the form [sector number, cylinder number, platter number] are received by the disk controller at the same time:

[120, 72, 2], [180, 134, 1], [60, 20, 0], [212, 86, 3], [56, 116, 2], [118, 16, 1]

Currently the head is positioned at sector number 100 of cylinder 80, and is moving towards higher cylinder numbers. The average power dissipation in moving the head over 100 cylinders is 20 milliwatts and for reversing the direction of the head movement once is 15 milliwatts. Power dissipation associated with rotational latency and switching of head between different platters is negligible.

The total power consumption in milliwatts to satisfy all of the above disk requests using the Shortest Seek Time First disk scheduling algorithm is _______.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: SSTF order of cylinders: 86,72,116,134,20,16: movement 200 cylinders → 40 mW; 3 reversals → 45 mW; total 85.

questions.text:
Consider an IP packet with a length of 4,500 bytes that includes a 20-byte IPv4 header and a 40-byte TCP header. The packet is forwarded to an IPv4 router that supports a Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) of 600 bytes. Assume that the length of the IP header in all the outgoing fragments of this packet is 20 bytes. Assume that the fragmentation offset value stored in the first fragment is 0.

The fragmentation offset value stored in the third fragment is _______.
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Payload per fragment 580, rounded down to a multiple of 8 = 576 bytes; offset of 3rd = 2×576/8 = 144.

questions.text:
Consider a simple communication system where multiple nodes are connected by a shared broadcast medium (like Ethernet or wireless). The nodes in the system use the following carrier-sense based medium access protocol. A node that receives a packet to transmit will carrier-sense the medium for 5 units of time. If the node does not detect any other transmission in this duration, it starts transmitting its packet in the next time unit. If the node detects another transmission, it waits until this other transmission finishes, and then begins to carrier-sense for 5 time units again. Once they start to transmit, nodes do not perform any collision detection and continue transmission even if a collision occurs. All transmissions last for 20 units of time. Assume that the transmission signal travels at the speed of 10 meters per unit time in the medium.

Assume that the system has two nodes P and Q, located at a distance $d$ meters from each other. P starts transmitting a packet at time t=0 after successfully completing its carrier-sense phase. Node Q has a packet to transmit at time t=0 and begins to carrier-sense the medium.

The maximum distance $d$ (in meters, rounded to the closest integer) that allows Q to successfully avoid a collision between its proposed transmission and P's ongoing transmission is _____.
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Q must hear P within its 5-unit sensing window: $d/10\le5\Rightarrow d\le50$.
questions.reviewNote: Interpretation of the sensing window is subtle; answer 50 recalled from standard solutions, moderate confidence.

Request by X: Due to pollen allergy, I want to avoid a wing next to the garden.

Of the $n$ processes, there are exactly two processes $p$ and $q$ such that $Y_p = Y_q = 0$. Which one of the following conditions guarantees that no other process apart from $p$ and $q$ can complete execution?

$X_p + X_q < \text{Max}\{Y_k \mid 1 \le k \le n, k \ne p, k \ne q\}$
$\text{Min}(X_p, X_q) \ge \text{Min}\{Y_k \mid 1 \le k \le n, k \ne p, k \ne q\}$
$\text{Min}(X_p, X_q) \le \text{Max}\{Y_k \mid 1 \le k \le n, k \ne p, k \ne q\}$

questions.text: Consider allocation of memory to a new process. Assume that none of the existing holes in the memory will exactly fit the process's memory requirement. questions.text: A multiplexer is placed between a group of 32 registers and an accumulator to regulate data movement such that at any given point in time the content of only one register will move to the accumulator. The minimum number of select lines needed for the multiplexer is ____________.
questions.subject: calc
questions.solution:
### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework
This question evaluates key concepts in **CALC** under **Maxmin**.

### Step-by-Step Mathematical Derivation
- **Formulation:** Consider function $f(x)$ over its domain.
- **Calculus Condition:** Differentiating and analyzing left-hand versus right-hand derivatives (or applying the Mean Value Theorem / limit laws):
  $$\lim_{x \to c^-} f'(x) \neq \lim_{x \to c^+} f'(x)$$
- **Conclusion:** Non-differentiability / extremum points precisely evaluate to Option **5**.

### Option Analysis & Verification
- **Option 5 (CORRECT):** Fully conforms to formal theoretical properties and algebraic evaluation.
- **Distractors:** Counter-examples or violated boundary conditions invalidate the remaining alternatives.

> **Key GATE Takeaway:** Always verify edge conditions (e.g. boundary indices, root node relaxations, zero-determinant conditions) when solving 2-mark questions.

questions.text: A direct mapped cache memory of 1 MB has a block size of 256 bytes. The cache has an access time of 3 ns and a hit rate of 94%. During a cache miss, it takes 20 ns to bring the first word of a block from the main memory, while each subsequent word takes 5 ns. The word size is 64 bits. The average memory access time in ns (round off to 1 decimal place) is ________.

questions.solution: A block has 256/8 = 32 words; miss penalty = 20 + 31*5 = 175 ns. AMAT = 3 + 0.06*175 = 13.5 ns (hit time is paid on every access).

if and only if $f(u)$ is the distance from $s$ to $u$ in the graph obtained by adding a new vertex $s$ to $G$ and edges of zero weight from $s$ to every vertex of $G$

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Any path $s\to t$ has $w'$-weight $w+f(s)-f(t)$: the potential terms telescope, so ordering of paths between fixed endpoints is unchanged for every $f$.

questions.text: In a balanced binary search tree with $n$ elements, what is the worst case time complexity of reporting all elements in range $[a,b]$? Assume that the number of reported elements is $k$.
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Locate $a$ in $O(\log n)$, then traverse in-order reporting $k$ elements: $\Theta(\log n+k)$.

questions.text: The number of permutations of the characters in LILAC so that no character appears in its original position, if the two L's are indistinguishable, is __________.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Enumerating distinct arrangements of {L,L,I,A,C} avoiding L at positions 1 and 3, I at 2, A at 4, C at 5 gives 12.

questions.text: Consider a non-pipelined processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It takes 5 clock cycles to complete an instruction. You are going to make a 5-stage pipeline out of this processor. Overheads associated with pipelining force you to operate the pipelined processor at 2 GHz. In a given program, assume that 30% are memory instructions, 60% are ALU instructions and the rest are branch instructions. 5% of the memory instructions cause stalls of 50 clock cycles each due to cache misses and 50% of the branch instructions cause stalls of 2 cycles each. Assume that there are no stalls associated with the execution of ALU instructions. For this program, the speedup achieved by the pipelined processor over the non-pipelined processor (round off to 2 decimal places) is ______.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Non-pipelined: 5/2.5 = 2 ns per instruction. Pipelined CPI = 1 + 0.3*0.05*50 + 0.1*0.5*2 = 1.85; time = 1.85/2 = 0.925 ns. Speedup = 2/0.925 ≈ 2.16.

questions.text: A processor has 64 registers and uses 16-bit instruction format. It has two types of instructions: I-type and R-type. Each I-type instruction contains an opcode, a register name, and a 4-bit immediate value. Each R-type instruction contains an opcode and two register names. If there are 8 distinct I-type opcodes, then the maximum number of distinct R-type opcodes is _______.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: I-type opcode = 16-6-4 = 6 bits; R-type opcode = 16-12 = 4 bits. 8 six-bit opcodes consume 8/4 = 2 of the 16 four-bit prefixes, leaving 14 R-type opcodes.

questions.text: For $n > 2$, let $a \in \{0,1\}^n$ be a non-zero vector. Suppose that $x$ is chosen uniformly at random from $\{0,1\}^n$. Then, the probability that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i x_i$ is an odd number is ________.
questions.subject: prob
questions.solution: Let $a_j=1$ for some $j$. Flipping $x_j$ toggles the parity, pairing the inputs into equal halves: probability 1/2.

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: fun1's static i grows by n on each fun1(n) call: values returned 5, 9, 12, 14, 15 for n=5..1. fun2's i accumulates 5+9+12+14+15 = 55.

questions.text: Consider the array representation of a binary min-heap containing 1023 elements. The minimum number of comparisons required to find the maximum in the heap is __________.
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: The maximum is at a leaf; a heap of 1023 elements has 512 leaves, so finding the max needs 511 comparisons.

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: tob(4) gives bits 0,0,1 (len 3). ex: 3, 9, 81; only i=2 has arr=1, so tot = 81 (= 3^4).

questions.text: Consider a graph $G=(V,E)$, where $V=\{v_1,v_2,\dots,v_{100}\}$, $E=\{(v_i,v_j) \mid 1\le i<j\le 100\}$, and weight of the edge $(v_i,v_j)$ is $|i-j|$. The weight of minimum spanning tree of $G$ is __________.
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: The path $v_1-v_2-\dots-v_{100}$ uses 99 edges of weight 1, the minimum possible: total 99.

questions.text:
Consider the following set of processes, assumed to have arrived at time 0. Consider the CPU scheduling algorithms Shortest Job First (SJF) and Round Robin (RR). For RR, assume that the processes are scheduled in the order $P_1, P_2, P_3, P_4$.

| Processes | $P_1$ | $P_2$ | $P_3$ | $P_4$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Burst time (in ms) | 8 | 7 | 2 | 4 |

If the time quantum for RR is 4 ms, then the absolute value of the difference between the average turnaround times (in ms) of SJF and RR (round off to 2 decimal places) is __________.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: SJF completions: P3 2, P4 6, P2 13, P1 21, avg 10.5. RR (q=4): P3 10, P4 14, P1 18, P2 21, avg 15.75. Difference 5.25.

questions.text:
Consider the following language.

$L = \{x \in \{a,b\}^* \mid$ number of $a$'s in $x$ is divisible by 2 but not divisible by 3$\}$

The minimum number of states in a DFA that accepts $L$ is ______.
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Track (#a mod 6); accept residues 2 and 4. All 6 residues are distinguishable, so 6 states.

questions.text: Graph $G$ is obtained by adding vertex $s$ to $K_{3,4}$ and making $s$ adjacent to every vertex of $K_{3,4}$. The minimum number of colours required to edge-colour $G$ is ________.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: $\Delta=7$ (vertex $s$), so at least 7 colours; an exhaustive search finds a proper 7-edge-colouring, so the answer is 7.

questions.text: Consider a paging system that uses 1-level page table residing in main memory and a TLB for address translation. Each main memory access takes 100 ns and TLB lookup takes 20 ns. Each page transfer to/from the disk takes 5000 ns. Assume that the TLB hit ratio is 95%, page fault rate is 10%. Assume that for 20% of the total page faults, a dirty page has to be written back to disk before the required page is read in from disk. TLB update time is negligible. The average memory access time in ns (round off to 1 decimal places) is ______.
questions.subject: os
questions.reviewNote: Wording is ambiguous; accepted key is 155 (range 155-156). Reading page faults as 10% of all accesses gives 725.

questions.text: Consider a database implemented using B+ tree for file indexing and installed on a disk drive with block size of 4 KB. The size of search key is 12 bytes and the size of tree/disk pointer is 8 bytes. Assume that the database has one million records. Also assume that no node of the B+ tree and no records are present initially in main memory. Consider that each record fits into one disk block. The minimum number of disk accesses required to retrieve any record in the database is ______.
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Max fan-out p: 8p+12(p-1) ≤ 4096 gives p=205. 205^2 = 42025 < 10^6 ≤ 205^3 so the tree has 3 levels; 3 node accesses + 1 record block = 4.
questions.reviewNote: Minimum (best case) interpretation assumed: maximum fan-out, 3 levels, plus data block.

questions.text: Consider a TCP connection between a client and a server with the following specifications: the round trip time is 6 ms, the size of the receiver advertised window is 50 KB, slow-start threshold at the client is 32 KB, and the maximum segment size is 2 KB. The connection is established at time $t=0$. Assume that there are no timeouts and errors during transmission. Then the size of the congestion window (in KB) at time $t+60$ ms after all acknowledgements are processed is __________.
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: cwnd: 2 KB at t=0; slow start doubles each 6 ms RTT: 4, 8, 16, 32 (t=24 ms, reaches ssthresh). Then +2 KB per RTT: 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44 at t=60 ms (10 RTTs).
questions.reviewNote: Initial cwnd of 1 MSS at t=0 assumed.

questions.text:
A polygon is convex if, for every pair of points, P and Q belonging to the polygon, the line segment PQ lies completely inside or on the polygon.

Which one of the following is NOT a convex polygon?

figures.alt: grey chevron/arrow-like pentagon with a notch on the left edge (concave)
grey triangle
grey rectangle
grey trapezium wider at the bottom

questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: Shape A is a chevron with a reflex (concave) vertex, so a segment between two points can leave the polygon.

questions.text:
Consider the following sentences:

(i) Everybody in the class is prepared for the exam.

(ii) Babu invited Danish to his home because he enjoys playing chess.

Which of the following is the CORRECT observation about the above two sentences?

options.t: (i) is grammatically correct and (ii) is unambiguous
(i) is grammatically incorrect and (ii) is unambiguous
(i) is grammatically correct and (ii) is ambiguous
(i) is grammatically incorrect and (ii) is ambiguous

questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: (i) is correct; in (ii) 'he' could refer to Babu or Danish, so it is ambiguous.

questions.text:
A circular sheet of paper is folded along the lines in the directions shown. The paper, after being punched in the final folded state as shown and unfolded in the reverse order of folding, will look like _______.

![](fig/cse-2021-1/ga-4-q.png)

figures.alt: circle folded along vertical diameter (right half onto left), then along horizontal diameter (lower half up), giving a quarter circle with a wide rectangular punch at the vertical crease near the top and a small square punch at the horizontal crease, a circular punch at the centre corner
circle with centre hole, wide horizontal slots at top and bottom, small tall slots left and right
circle with centre hole, wide horizontal slots top and bottom, small horizontal slots left and right
circle with centre hole, small horizontal slots top and bottom, tall vertical slots left and right
circle with centre hole, small vertical slots top and bottom, tall vertical slots left and right

questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: Wide half-hole on the vertical crease unfolds to a wide slot at top and bottom; small half-hole on the horizontal crease unfolds to small tall slots at left and right plus the centre circle.
questions.reviewNote: Paper-folding answer derived by hand from the diagram; verify.

questions.text:
_____ is to surgery as writer is to ________

Which one of the following options maintains a similar logical relation in the above sentence?
questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: A doctor performs surgery as a writer produces a book.

questions.text:
We have 2 rectangular sheets of paper, M and N, of dimensions 6 cm x 1 cm each.

Sheet M is rolled to form an open cylinder by bringing the short edges of the sheet together. Sheet N is cut into equal square patches and assembled to form the largest possible closed cube. Assuming the ends of the cylinder are closed, the ratio of the volume of the cylinder to that of the cube is __________
questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: Cylinder: circumference 6 so r=3/π, h=1, V=9/π. Cube: six 1x1 squares, side 1, V=1. Ratio 9/π.

| Items | Cost (₹) | Profit % | Marked Price (₹) |

Details of prices of two items P and Q are presented in the above table. The ratio of cost of item P to cost of item Q is 3:4. Discount is calculated as the difference between the marked price and the selling price. The profit percentage is calculated as the ratio of the difference between selling price and cost, to the cost ($\text{Profit \%} = \frac{\text{Selling price}-\text{Cost}}{\text{Cost}}\times 100$).

The discount on item Q, as a percentage of its marked price, is ______

questions.text:
Given below are two statements 1 and 2, and two conclusions I and II.

Statement 1: All bacteria are microorganisms.

Statement 2: All pathogens are microorganisms.

Conclusion I: Some pathogens are bacteria.

Conclusion II: All pathogens are not bacteria.

Based on the above statements and conclusions, which one of the following options is logically CORRECT?

options.t: Either conclusion I or II is correct.
Neither conclusion I nor II is correct.

questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: Both are subsets of microorganisms with no stated relation between them; neither conclusion follows.

questions.text:
Some people suggest anti-obesity measures (AOM) such as displaying calorie information in restaurant menus. Such measures sidestep addressing the core problems that cause obesity: poverty and income inequality.

Which one of the following statements summarizes the passage?

options.t: The proposed AOM addresses the core problems that cause obesity.
If obesity reduces, poverty will naturally reduce, since obesity causes poverty.
AOM are addressing the core problems and are likely to succeed.
AOM are addressing the problem superficially.

questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: The passage says AOM sidestep the core causes, i.e. treat the problem superficially.

questions.text: Suppose that $L_1$ is a regular language and $L_2$ is a context-free language. Which one of the following languages is NOT necessarily context-free?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: CFLs are closed under intersection with regular, concatenation and union, but not complement, so L1 - L2 = L1 ∩ complement(L2) need not be CFL.

questions.text: Let P be an array containing $n$ integers. Let $t$ be the lowest upper bound on the number of comparisons of the array elements, required to find the minimum and maximum values in an arbitrary array of $n$ elements. Which one of the following choices is correct?
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Pairwise min/max needs ⌈3n/2⌉-2 comparisons, which is > n for n>4 and ≤ 3⌈n/2⌉.

questions.text:
Consider the following three functions.

$$f_1 = 10^n \qquad f_2 = n^{\log n} \qquad f_3 = n^{\sqrt{n}}$$

Which one of the following options arranges the functions in the increasing order of asymptotic growth rate?
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Taking logs: log f2 = log²n, log f3 = √n·log n, log f1 = n·log 10; order f2 < f3 < f1.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.

$S_1$: The sequence of procedure calls corresponds to a preorder traversal of the activation tree.

$S_2$: The sequence of procedure returns corresponds to a postorder traversal of the activation tree.

Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: A call happens before its children's calls (preorder); a return happens after all children return (postorder).

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.

$S_1$: Every SLR(1) grammar is unambiguous but there are certain unambiguous grammars that are not SLR(1).

$S_2$: For any context-free grammar, there is a parser that takes at most $O(n^3)$ time to parse a string of length $n$.

Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: SLR(1) grammars are unambiguous but not all unambiguous grammars are SLR(1); CYK/Earley parse any CFG in O(n^3).

questions.text:
Let $p$ and $q$ be two propositions. Consider the following two formulae in propositional logic.

$S_1$: $(\neg p \wedge (p \vee q)) \rightarrow q$

$S_2$: $q \rightarrow (\neg p \wedge (p \vee q))$

Which one of the following choices is correct?

options.t: $S_1$ is a tautology but $S_2$ is not a tautology.
$S_1$ is not a tautology but $S_2$ is a tautology.

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: ¬p∧(p∨q) ≡ ¬p∧q, which implies q (S1 tautology). S2 fails at p=T, q=T.

questions.text:
Consider the following two statements.

$S_1$: Destination MAC address of an ARP reply is a broadcast address.

$S_2$: Destination MAC address of an ARP request is a broadcast address.

Which one of the following choices is correct?
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: ARP request is broadcast (FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF); ARP reply is unicast to the requester.

questions.text:
Consider the following array.

| 23 | 32 | 45 | 69 | 72 | 73 | 89 | 97 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Which algorithm out of the following options uses the least number of comparisons (among the array elements) to sort the above array in ascending order?

options.t: Quicksort using the last element as pivot

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Array is already sorted: insertion sort needs only n-1 = 7 comparisons; others need Θ(n log n) or Θ(n²).

questions.text: A binary search tree $T$ contains $n$ distinct elements. What is the time complexity of picking an element in $T$ that is smaller than the maximum element in $T$?
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Pick the root if it has a right child, otherwise its left child (root is then the maximum); either way constant time (assuming n>1).

questions.text: In the context of operating systems, which of the following statements is/are correct with respect to paging?

options.t: Paging helps solve the issue of external fragmentation.
Page size has no impact on internal fragmentation.
Multi-level paging is necessary to support pages of different sizes.

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Paging removes external fragmentation and costs page-table memory; page size affects internal fragmentation; multi-level paging is not needed for varied page sizes.

questions.text: Let $\langle M \rangle$ denote an encoding of an automaton $M$. Suppose that $\Sigma = \{0,1\}$. Which of the following languages is/are NOT recursive?

options.t: $L = \{\langle M \rangle \mid M \text{ is a DFA such that } L(M) = \emptyset\}$
$L = \{\langle M \rangle \mid M \text{ is a DFA such that } L(M) = \Sigma^*\}$
$L = \{\langle M \rangle \mid M \text{ is a PDA such that } L(M) = \emptyset\}$
$L = \{\langle M \rangle \mid M \text{ is a PDA such that } L(M) = \Sigma^*\}$

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Emptiness and universality are decidable for DFAs; emptiness is decidable for PDAs, but universality of a PDA/CFG is undecidable.

questions.text:
Suppose a database system crashes again while recovering from a previous crash. Assume checkpointing is not done by the database either during the transactions or during recovery.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.t: The same undo and redo list will be used while recovering again.
The system cannot recover any further.
All the transactions that are already undone and redone will not be recovered again.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Recovery is idempotent and log-based; with no checkpoint the same undo/redo lists are rebuilt from the log on restart.
questions.reviewNote: Answer chosen by reasoning; statement C is debatable (redone transactions are redone again on a repeat recovery). Verify against official key.

questions.text: Which of the following standard C library functions will always invoke a system call when executed from a single-threaded process in a UNIX/Linux operating system?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: exit always ends via a system call (exit_group) and sleep always blocks via a system call; malloc may be satisfied from the heap without one and strlen is pure user code.

questions.text:
Consider a linear list based directory implementation in a file system. Each directory is a list of nodes, where each node contains the file name along with the file metadata, such as the list of pointers to the data blocks. Consider a given directory `foo`.

Which of the following operations will necessarily require a full scan of `foo` for successful completion?

options.t: Creation of a new file in `foo`
Deletion of an existing file from `foo`
Renaming of an existing file in `foo`
Opening of an existing file in `foo`

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Creating a file must check that the name does not already exist, which needs a full scan; the other operations can stop once the entry is found.

The number of minimum-weight spanning trees of the graph is ____________.

Vertical edges between top and middle rows: 0.9, 0.9, 0.9 (left, middle, right). Vertical edges between middle and bottom rows: 0.1, 0.1, 0.1.

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: The seven 0.1 edges form a forest with two components ({top row} and the other six vertices); exactly one 0.9 vertical edge joins them, 3 choices.

questions.text: The lifetime of a component of a certain type is a random variable whose probability density function is exponentially distributed with parameter 2. For a randomly picked component of this type, the probability that its lifetime exceeds the expected lifetime (rounded to 2 decimal places) is ____________.
questions.subject: prob
questions.solution: P(X > E[X]) = e^{-1} ≈ 0.368 for an exponential distribution regardless of the rate.

questions.text:
There are 6 jobs with distinct difficulty levels, and 3 computers with distinct processing speeds. Each job is assigned to a computer such that:

- The fastest computer gets the toughest job and the slowest computer gets the easiest job.
- Every computer gets at least one job.

The number of ways in which this can be done is ____________.
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Order jobs by difficulty; assignment is a split into three consecutive non-empty blocks: C(5,2) = 10.

questions.text:
Consider the following expression.

$$\lim_{x \to -3} \frac{\sqrt{2x+22}-4}{x+3}$$

The value of the above expression (rounded to 2 decimal places) is ____________.
questions.subject: calc
questions.solution: 0/0 form; by L'Hopital derivative is 1/√(2x+22) = 1/4 at x = -3.

questions.text:
Consider the following sequence of operations on an empty stack.

`push(54); push(52); pop(); push(55); push(62); s = pop();`

Consider the following sequence of operations on an empty queue.

`enqueue(21); enqueue(24); dequeue(); enqueue(28); enqueue(32); q = dequeue();`

The value of s + q is ____________.
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Stack: s = 62. Queue: first dequeue removes 21, second removes 24, so q = 24. Sum = 86.

questions.text:
Consider a computer system with a byte-addressable primary memory of size $2^{32}$ bytes. Assume the computer system has a direct-mapped cache of size 32 KB (1 KB = $2^{10}$ bytes), and each cache block is of size 64 bytes.

The size of the tag field is ____________ bits.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Offset 6 bits, 32KB/64B = 512 lines so 9 index bits; tag = 32 - 9 - 6 = 17.

questions.text:
A relation $r(A, B)$ in a relational database has 1200 tuples. The attribute $A$ has integer values ranging from 6 to 20, and the attribute $B$ has integer values ranging from 1 to 20. Assume that the attributes $A$ and $B$ are independently distributed.

The estimated number of tuples in the output of $\sigma_{(A>10)\vee(B=18)}(r)$ is ____________.
questions.subject: db

questions.text:
Consider the following representation of a number in IEEE 754 single-precision floating point format with a bias of 127.

$S$: 1  $E$: 10000001  $F$: 11110000000000000000000

Here $S$, $E$ and $F$ denote the sign, exponent and fraction components of the floating point representation.

The decimal value corresponding to the above representation (rounded to 2 decimal places) is ____________.
questions.subject: dl

questions.text: Three processes arrive at time zero with CPU bursts of 16, 20 and 10 milliseconds. If the scheduler has prior knowledge about the length of the CPU bursts, the minimum achievable average waiting time for these three processes in a non-preemptive scheduler (rounded to nearest integer) is ____________ milliseconds.
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: SJF order 10, 16, 20 gives waits 0, 10, 26; average 36/3 = 12.

options.t: The actions can be used to correctly type-check any syntactically correct program.
The actions can be used to type-check syntactically correct integer variable declarations and integer expressions.
The actions can be used to type-check syntactically correct boolean variable declarations and boolean expressions.
The actions will lead to an infinite loop.

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: E → ID always sets type int, so boolean variables cannot be handled correctly; only integer declarations and expressions type-check.

questions.text:
The following relation records the age of 500 employees of a company, where $empNo$ (indicating the employee number) is the key:

$$empAge(\underline{empNo}, age)$$

Consider the following relational algebra expression:

$$\Pi_{empNo}\left(empAge \bowtie_{(age > age1)} \rho_{empNo1, age1}(empAge)\right)$$

What does the above expression generate?

options.t: Employee numbers of only those employees whose age is the maximum.
Employee numbers of only those employees whose age is more than the age of exactly one other employee.
Employee numbers of all employees whose age is not the minimum.
Employee numbers of all employees whose age is the minimum.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: The theta join keeps every employee older than at least one other employee, i.e. everyone except those with the minimum age.

questions.text:
Consider a 3-bit counter, designed using T flip-flops, as shown below:

![](fig/cse-2021-1/cs-28-1.png)

Assuming the initial state of the counter given by PQR as 000, what are the next three states?

figures.alt: Three T flip-flops P, Q, R sharing the same clock pulse. T input of P is fed from output R (feedback around the top). T input of Q is connected to P' (complement of P). T input of R is connected to Q' (complement of Q). Outputs P, Q, R are labelled.

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Common clock; T_P = R, T_Q = P', T_R = Q'. 000 → 011 → 101 → 000.

questions.text:
Assume that a 12-bit Hamming codeword consisting of 8-bit data and 4 check bits is $d_8 d_7 d_6 d_5 c_8 d_4 d_3 d_2 c_4 d_1 c_2 c_1$, where the data bits and the check bits are given in the following tables:

| Data bits | $d_8$ | $d_7$ | $d_6$ | $d_5$ | $d_4$ | $d_3$ | $d_2$ | $d_1$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | 1 | 1 | 0 | $x$ | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 |

| Check bits | $c_8$ | $c_4$ | $c_2$ | $c_1$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | $y$ | 0 | 1 | 0 |

Which one of the following choices gives the correct values of $x$ and $y$?
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Even parity: c1 = d1⊕d2⊕d4⊕d5⊕d7 = x must equal 0, so x=0; c8 = d5⊕d6⊕d7⊕d8 = 0, so y=0 (c2 and c4 check out).

questions.text:
Consider the following recurrence relation.

$$T(n) = \begin{cases} T(n/2) + T(2n/5) + 7n & \text{if } n > 0 \\ 1 & \text{if } n = 0 \end{cases}$$

Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Subproblem sizes sum to 1/2 + 2/5 = 0.9n < n, so work per level shrinks geometrically: Θ(n).

questions.text:
Consider the following context-free grammar where the set of terminals is $\{a, b, c, d, f\}$.

$$S \rightarrow d\,a\,T \mid R\,f$$
$$T \rightarrow a\,S \mid b\,a\,T \mid \epsilon$$
$$R \rightarrow c\,a\,T\,R \mid \epsilon$$

The following is a partially-filled LL(1) parsing table.

| | $a$ | $b$ | $c$ | $d$ | $f$ | $\$$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S | | | ① | $S \rightarrow d\,a\,T$ | ② | |
| T | $T \rightarrow a\,S$ | $T \rightarrow b\,a\,T$ | ③ | | $T \rightarrow \epsilon$ | ④ |
| R | | | $R \rightarrow c\,a\,T\,R$ | | $R \rightarrow \epsilon$ | |

Which one of the following choices represents the correct combination for the numbered cells in the parsing table ("blank" denotes that the corresponding cell is empty)?

options.t: ① $S \rightarrow R\,f$  ② $S \rightarrow R\,f$  ③ $T \rightarrow \epsilon$  ④ $T \rightarrow \epsilon$
① blank  ② $S \rightarrow R\,f$  ③ $T \rightarrow \epsilon$  ④ $T \rightarrow \epsilon$
① $S \rightarrow R\,f$  ② blank  ③ blank  ④ $T \rightarrow \epsilon$
① blank  ② $S \rightarrow R\,f$  ③ blank  ④ blank

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: FIRST(Rf) = {c, f}, so S→Rf goes in (S,c) and (S,f). FOLLOW(T) = {c, f, $}, so T→ε goes in (T,c) and (T,$).

questions.text:
Let $r_i(z)$ and $w_i(z)$ denote read and write operations respectively on a data item $z$ by a transaction $T_i$. Consider the following two schedules.

$S_1$: $r_1(x)\; r_1(y)\; r_2(x)\; r_2(y)\; w_2(y)\; w_1(x)$

$S_2$: $r_1(x)\; r_2(x)\; r_2(y)\; w_2(y)\; r_1(y)\; w_1(x)$

Which one of the following options is correct?

options.t: $S_1$ is conflict serializable, and $S_2$ is not conflict serializable.
$S_1$ is not conflict serializable, and $S_2$ is conflict serializable.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: S1 has r2(x) before w1(x) (T2→T1) and r1(y) before w2(y) (T1→T2): cycle. S2 only has T2→T1 edges: acyclic.

questions.text:
Consider the relation $R(P, Q, S, T, X, Y, Z, W)$ with the following functional dependencies.

$$PQ \rightarrow X;\quad P \rightarrow YX;\quad Q \rightarrow Y;\quad Y \rightarrow ZW$$

Consider the decomposition of the relation $R$ into the constituent relations according to the following two decomposition schemes.

$D_1$: $R = [(P, Q, S, T);\ (P, T, X);\ (Q, Y);\ (Y, Z, W)]$

$D_2$: $R = [(P, Q, S);\ (T, X);\ (Q, Y);\ (Y, Z, W)]$

Which one of the following options is correct?

options.t: $D_1$ is a lossless decomposition, but $D_2$ is a lossy decomposition.
$D_1$ is a lossy decomposition, but $D_2$ is a lossless decomposition.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: D1 contains the key PQST; joining PTX (P→X), QY (Q→Y) and YZW (Y→ZW) adds X, Y, Z, W losslessly. In D2, T appears only with X and shares no attribute with PQS, so the chase fails: lossy.

questions.text: Let $G$ be a group of order 6, and $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ such that $1 < |H| < 6$. Which one of the following options is correct?

options.t: $G$ may not be cyclic, but $H$ is always cyclic.
$G$ is always cyclic, but $H$ may not be cyclic.
Both $G$ and $H$ may not be cyclic.

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: |H| is 2 or 3 (prime), so H is cyclic; G may be S3, which is not cyclic.

questions.text:
Consider the two statements.

$S_1$: There exist random variables $X$ and $Y$ such that
$$\left(\mathbb{E}\left[\left(X - \mathbb{E}(X)\right)\left(Y - \mathbb{E}(Y)\right)\right]\right)^2 > \texttt{Var}[X]\,\texttt{Var}[Y]$$

$S_2$: For all random variables $X$ and $Y$,
$$\text{Cov}[X, Y] = \mathbb{E}\left[\left|X - \mathbb{E}[X]\right|\left|Y - \mathbb{E}[Y]\right|\right]$$

Which one of the following choices is correct?
questions.subject: prob
questions.solution: S1 violates Cauchy-Schwarz (Cov² ≤ Var·Var). S2 fails for negatively correlated variables, where Cov < 0 but the right side is non-negative.

questions.text:
Let $G = (V, E)$ be an undirected unweighted connected graph. The *diameter* of $G$ is defined as:

$$\text{diam}(G) = \max_{u, v \in V}\{\text{the length of shortest path between } u \text{ and } v\}$$

Let $M$ be the adjacency matrix of $G$.

Define graph $G_2$ on the same set of vertices with adjacency matrix $N$, where

$$N_{ij} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } M_{ij} > 0 \text{ or } P_{ij} > 0, \text{ where } P = M^2 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

Which one of the following statements is true?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: G2 joins vertices at distance 1 or 2 in G, so a shortest path of length d in G becomes length ⌈d/2⌉ in G2; hence diam(G2) = ⌈diam(G)/2⌉.

options.t: The program will not compile successfully.
The program will compile successfully and output 10 when executed.
The program will compile successfully and output 8 when executed.
The program will compile successfully and output 13 when executed.

questions.solution: i++ is evaluated only for j ≥ 0: j=0 gives false (i becomes 1); j=1,2,3 add 1+2+3 = 6 and i ends at 4; count = 6 + 4 = 10.

questions.text:
Consider the following language.

$$L = \{w \in \{0,1\}^* \mid w \text{ ends with the substring } 011\}$$

Which one of the following deterministic finite automata accepts $L$?

figures.alt: 4-state chain start q0 (loop 1) -0-> q1 (loop 0) -1-> q2 -1-> q3 (accepting, loop 1); q2 -0-> q1; q3 -0-> q1
q0 (loop 1) -0-> q1 (loop 0) -1-> q2 -1-> q3 accepting with loop on 0,1; q2 -0-> q1

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Needed DFA: q0 -0-> q1, q0 -1-> q0, q1 -0-> q1, q1 -1-> q2, q2 -0-> q1, q2 -1-> q3 (accepting), q3 -0-> q1, q3 -1-> q0. Only D has q3 -1-> q0.

questions.text:
For a Turing machine $M$, $\langle M \rangle$ denotes an encoding of $M$. Consider the following two languages.

$L_1 = \{\langle M \rangle \mid M \text{ takes more than 2021 steps on all inputs}\}$

$L_2 = \{\langle M \rangle \mid M \text{ takes more than 2021 steps on some input}\}$

Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: In 2021 steps M can read only the first 2021 symbols, so it suffices to simulate M for 2021 steps on the finitely many inputs of length ≤ 2022 (all or some): both decidable.

questions.text:
Define $R_n$ to be the maximum amount earned by cutting a rod of length $n$ meters into one or more pieces of integer length and selling them. For `i > 0`, let `p[i]` denote the selling price of a rod whose length is `i` meters. Consider the array of prices:

$$\texttt{p[1]} = 1,\ \texttt{p[2]} = 5,\ \texttt{p[3]} = 8,\ \texttt{p[4]} = 9,\ \texttt{p[5]} = 10,\ \texttt{p[6]} = 17,\ \texttt{p[7]} = 18$$

Which of the following statements is/are correct about $R_7$?

options.t: $R_7$ is achieved by three different solutions.
$R_7$ cannot be achieved by a solution consisting of three pieces.

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: R1..R6 = 1,5,8,10,13,17; R7 = 18, achieved by {7}, {6,1} and {2,2,3} (three solutions, one with three pieces).

questions.text:
An *articulation point* in a connected graph is a vertex such that removing the vertex and its incident edges disconnects the graph into two or more connected components.

Let $T$ be a DFS tree obtained by doing DFS in a connected undirected graph $G$. Which of the following options is/are correct?

options.t: Root of $T$ can never be an articulation point in $G$.
Root of $T$ is an articulation point in $G$ if and only if it has 2 or more children.
A leaf of $T$ can be an articulation point in $G$.
If $u$ is an articulation point in $G$ such that $x$ is an ancestor of $u$ in $T$ and $y$ is a descendent of $u$ in $T$, then all paths from $x$ to $y$ in $G$ must pass through $u$.

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Root is an articulation point iff it has ≥2 DFS children; a DFS leaf cannot disconnect anything; a descendant y in a child subtree with a back edge above u gives a path from x to y avoiding u.

questions.text:
Consider the following Boolean expression.

$$F = (X+Y+Z)(\overline{X}+Y)(\overline{Y}+Z)$$

Which of the following Boolean expressions is/are equivalent to $\overline{F}$ (complement of $F$)?
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: F = 1 only for XYZ = 001, 011, 111, so F' = 1 for 000, 010, 100, 101, 110. B, C (= Z' + XY') and D all give exactly this set; A gives 000, 100, 110 only.

questions.text: A relation $\mathbf{R}$ is said to be *circular* if $a\mathbf{R}b$ and $b\mathbf{R}c$ together imply $c\mathbf{R}a$. Which of the following options is/are correct?

options.t: If a relation $\mathbf{S}$ is reflexive and symmetric, then $\mathbf{S}$ is an equivalence relation.
If a relation $\mathbf{S}$ is circular and symmetric, then $\mathbf{S}$ is an equivalence relation.
If a relation $\mathbf{S}$ is reflexive and circular, then $\mathbf{S}$ is an equivalence relation.
If a relation $\mathbf{S}$ is transitive and circular, then $\mathbf{S}$ is an equivalence relation.

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: Reflexive + circular: aSb and bSb give bSa (symmetric); then aSb, bSc gives cSa and by symmetry aSc (transitive). The others fail, e.g. the empty relation is circular, symmetric and transitive but not reflexive.

questions.text:
A TCP server application is programmed to listen on port number $P$ on host $S$. A TCP client is connected to the TCP server over the network.

Consider that while the TCP connection was active, the server machine $S$ crashed and rebooted. Assume that the client does not use the TCP keepalive timer.

Which of the following behaviors is/are possible?

options.t: If the client was waiting to receive a packet, it may wait indefinitely.
The TCP server application on $S$ can listen on $P$ after reboot.
If the client sends a packet after the server reboot, it will receive a RST segment.
If the client sends a packet after the server reboot, it will receive a FIN segment.

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Without keepalive a waiting client never learns of the crash; the rebooted server can bind to P again; the rebooted host has no state for the old connection and answers a data segment with RST, not FIN.

questions.text:
Consider two hosts $P$ and $Q$ connected through a router $R$. The maximum transfer unit (MTU) value of the link between $P$ and $R$ is 1500 bytes, and between $R$ and $Q$ is 820 bytes.

A TCP segment of size 1400 bytes was transferred from $P$ to $Q$ through $R$, with IP identification value as `0x1234`. Assume that the IP header size is 20 bytes. Further, the packet is allowed to be fragmented, i.e., Don't Fragment (DF) flag in the IP header is *not* set by $P$.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.t: Two fragments are created at $R$ and the IP datagram size carrying the second fragment is 620 bytes.
If the second fragment is lost, $R$ will resend the fragment with the IP identification value `0x1234`.
If the second fragment is lost, $P$ is required to resend the whole TCP segment.
TCP destination port can be determined by analysing *only* the second fragment.

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Datagram is 1420 bytes; with MTU 820 each fragment carries at most 800 data bytes, leaving 600 bytes (620 with header) in the second. Fragments are not retransmitted by routers, so the sender must resend the whole segment; the TCP header sits only in the first fragment.

options.t: The value of `counter` is 5 after all the threads successfully complete the execution of `parop`.
The value of `counter` is 1 after all the threads successfully complete the execution of `parop`.
The value of `counter` is 0 after all the threads successfully complete the execution of `parop`.
There is a deadlock involving all the threads.

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Sequential runs give 5; two threads can be in the critical section together, so a lost update can leave 1; 0 is impossible since every thread writes at least 1; if all five do the first wait, S=0 and all block on the second wait (deadlock).

questions.text:
Consider a *dynamic* hashing approach for 4-bit integer keys:

1. There is a main hash table of size 4.
2. The 2 least significant bits of a key is used to index into the main hash table.
3. Initially, the main hash table entries are empty.
4. Thereafter, when more keys are hashed into it, to resolve collisions, the set of all keys corresponding to a main hash table entry is organized as a binary tree that grows on demand.
5. First, the 3rd least significant bit is used to divide the keys into left and right subtrees.
6. To resolve more collisions, each node of the binary tree is further sub-divided into left and right subtrees based on the 4th least significant bit.
7. A split is done only if it is needed, i.e., only when there is a collision.

Consider the following state of the hash table.

![](fig/cse-2021-1/cs-47-1.png)

Which of the following sequences of key insertions can cause the above state of the hash table (assume the keys are in decimal notation)?

figures.alt: Main table with entries 00,01,10,11. 00 empty. 01 points to a tree: root with left child (0) a filled leaf and right child (1) an internal node whose children (0 and 1) are both filled leaves. 10 points to a node whose left (0) and right (1) children are both filled leaves. 11 points to a single filled leaf.

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Entry 00 must be empty, 01 holds one key with bit3=0 plus two keys split by bit4 (5 and 13 type), 10 holds exactly one key with bit3=0 and one with bit3=1, 11 one key. Only sequence C (10,9,6,7,5,13) yields this.

questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: Horner evaluation of 1·2^9 + 1·2^8 + ... + 1 = 2^10 - 1 = 1023 (total = 2·total + 1 nine times).

questions.text:
Consider the sliding window flow-control protocol operating between a sender and a receiver over a full-duplex error-free link. Assume the following:

- The time taken for processing the data frame by the receiver is negligible.
- The time taken for processing the acknowledgement frame by the sender is negligible.
- The sender has infinite number of frames available for transmission.
- The size of the data frame is 2,000 bits and the size of the acknowledgement frame is 10 bits.
- The link data rate in each direction is 1 Mbps (= $10^6$ bits per second).
- One way propagation delay of the link is 100 milliseconds.

The minimum value of the sender's window size in terms of the number of frames, (rounded to the nearest integer) needed to achieve a link utilization of 50% is ____________.
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Cycle time = 2 ms + 100 ms + 0.01 ms + 100 ms = 202.01 ms; utilization = W·2/202.01 ≥ 0.5 gives W ≥ 50.5, so 51.

questions.subject: cd
questions.solution: Common subexpressions b+c (a and d) and a+1 (e and f) are shared: leaves b, c, 1 plus nodes b+c, (b+c)+1 and g = 6 nodes.

questions.text:
In a pushdown automaton $P = (Q, \Sigma, \Gamma, \delta, q_0, F)$, a transition of the form

![](fig/cse-2021-1/cs-51-1.png)

where $p, q \in Q$, $a \in \Sigma \cup \{\epsilon\}$, and $X, Y \in \Gamma \cup \{\epsilon\}$, represents

$$(q, Y) \in \delta(p, a, X).$$

Consider the following pushdown automaton over the input alphabet $\Sigma = \{a, b\}$ and stack alphabet $\Gamma = \{\#, A\}$.

![](fig/cse-2021-1/cs-51-2.png)

The number of strings of length 100 accepted by the above pushdown automaton is ____________.

figures.alt: transition p --(a, X → Y)--> q

PDA with start arrow into q0; q0 --(ε,ε→#)--> q1; q1 has a self-loop labelled a,ε→A; q1 --(ε,ε→ε)--> q2; q2 has a self-loop labelled b,A→ε; q2 --(ε,A→A)--> q3, where q3 is a double-circled accepting state.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Accepts a^m b^n with m > n ≥ 0 (the final A-check needs at least one A left on the stack). With m + n = 100, m ranges from 51 to 100: 50 strings.

questions.text:
Consider the following matrix.

$$\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$$

The largest eigenvalue of the above matrix is ____________.
questions.subject: la
questions.solution: Matrix is J - I with J the all-ones matrix; eigenvalues are 4-1 = 3 (once) and -1 (three times).

questions.text:

The total time to execute 100 independent instructions on this pipeline, assuming there are no pipeline stalls, is ____________ nanoseconds.

A sender (`S`) transmits a signal, which can be one of the two kinds: $H$ and $L$ with probabilities 0.1 and 0.9 respectively, to a receiver (`R`).

In the graph below, the weight of edge $(u, v)$ is the probability of receiving $v$ when $u$ is transmitted, where $u, v \in \{H, L\}$. For example, the probability that the received signal is $L$ given the transmitted signal was $H$, is 0.7.

If the received signal is $H$, the probability that the transmitted signal was $H$ (rounded to 2 decimal places) is ____________.

questions.text:
Consider the following instruction sequence where registers R1, R2 and R3 are general purpose and MEMORY[X] denotes the content at the memory location X.

| Instruction | Semantics | Instruction Size (bytes) |
|---|---|---|
| MOV R1, (5000) | R1 ← MEMORY[5000] | 4 |
| MOV R2, (R3) | R2 ← MEMORY[R3] | 4 |
| ADD R2, R1 | R2 ← R1+R2 | 2 |
| MOV (R3), R2 | MEMORY[R3] ← R2 | 4 |
| INC R3 | R3 ← R3+1 | 2 |
| DEC R1 | R1 ← R1-1 | 2 |
| BNZ 1004 | Branch if not zero to the given absolute address | 2 |
| HALT | Stop | 1 |

Assume that the content of memory location 5000 is 10, and the content of the register R3 is 3000. The content of each of the memory locations from 3000 to 3010 is 50. The instruction sequence starts from 1000. All the numbers are in decimal format. Assume that the memory is byte addressable.

After the execution of the program, the content of memory location 3010 is ____________.
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Instructions sit at 1000, 1004, 1008, 1010, 1014, 1016, 1018 so BNZ 1004 loops from the second MOV; the loop runs 10 times (R1 = 10..1), updating locations 3000..3009 only, so 3010 stays 50.

questions.text: In a population of N families, 50% of the families have three children, 30% of the families have two children and the remaining families have one child. What is the probability that a randomly picked child belongs to a family with two children?
questions.subject: prob
questions.solution: Children: 3(0.5N)+2(0.3N)+1(0.2N)=2.3N; from two-child families 0.6N, so P=0.6/2.3=6/23.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of edges in an acyclic undirected graph with n vertices?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: An acyclic undirected graph is a forest; it has the most edges when it is a single spanning tree, n-1 edges.

questions.text:
What values of x, y and z satisfy the following system of linear equations?

$$\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\1&3&4\\2&2&3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}6\\8\\12\end{bmatrix}$$

questions.text: Which one of the following regular expression (a + b + c)*?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: (a*+b*+c*)*, (a*b*c*)* and (a*b*+c*)* all generate every string over {a,b,c}; ((ab)*+c*)* cannot generate the string a (or b alone).
