questions.text: What is the minimum number of NAD gates required to implement a 2-input EXCLUSIVE-OR function without using any other logic gate?
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: "NAD" is a misprint for NAND. XOR = NAND(NAND(A,N), NAND(B,N)) with N = NAND(A,B): 4 NAND gates.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?

options.t: There exist context-free languages such that all the context-free grammars generating them are ambiguous
An unambiguous context-free grammar always has a unique parse tree for each string of the language generated by it
Both deterministic and non-deterministic pushdown automata always accept the same set of languages
A finite set of strings from some alphabet is always a regular language

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: DPDAs accept only the deterministic CFLs, a proper subset of the languages accepted by NPDAs (e.g. even-length palindromes).

questions.text: What is the minimum size of ROM required to store the complete truth table of an 8-bit $\times$ 8-bit multiplier?
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: 16 input bits give 2^16 = 64K addresses; the product of two 8-bit numbers needs 16 bits, so 64K x 16.

questions.text: What is the hit rate of a video terminal unit with 50 characters/line, 8 bits/character and horizontal sweep time of 100 $\mu$v (including 20 $\mu$s of retrace time)?
questions.subject: la
questions.solution: With the original paper's 80 characters/line: 80 x 8 = 640 bits sent in the 80 us of active sweep (100-20) = 8 Mbps. With the printed 50 characters/line, 400 bits/80 us = 5 Mbps, which matches no option.
questions.reviewNote: Reprint typos: 'hit rate' = bit rate, '100 µv' = 100 µs, and '50 characters/line' appears to be 80 in the original paper; with 50 no option is correct. Answer A assumes 80 chars/line.

questions.text: Consider a system with 2 level cache. Access times of Level 1 cache, Level 2 cache and main memory are 1 ns, 10 ns and 500 ns, respectively. The hit rates of Level 1and Level 2 caches are 0.5 and 0.9, respectively. What is the average access time of the system ignoring the search time within the cache?
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: With the original paper's L1 hit rate 0.8: 0.8(1) + 0.2(0.9)(10) + 0.2(0.1)(500) = 0.8 + 1.8 + 10 = 12.6 ns. With the printed 0.5 the result is 30 ns, matching no option.
questions.reviewNote: Reprint prints L1 hit rate 0.5, which gives 30 ns (no option); the original GATE IT 2004 paper has 0.8, giving 12.6 ns (C).

questions.text: Let P be a singly linked list. Let Q be the pointer to an intermediate node x in the list. What is the worst-case time complexity of the best-known algorithm to delete the node x from the list?
questions.subject: pds
questions.solution: To unlink x its predecessor must be found by traversing from the head, O(n) in the worst case. (Copying the successor's data into x and deleting the successor would be O(1), which is why the key is disputed.)
questions.reviewNote: Answer disputed: O(n) (find predecessor) vs O(1) (copy-next-node trick, valid since x is intermediate).

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT shared by the threads of the same process?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Each thread has its own stack (and registers); address space, open files and IPC objects are shared.

questions.text:
Let x be an integer which can take a value of 0 or 1. The statement

```c
if (x == 0) x = 1; else x = 0;
```

is equivalent to which one of the following?
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution:
### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework
This question evaluates key concepts in **COA** under **Isa**.

### Step-by-Step Mathematical Derivation
- **Analytical Logic:** Evaluating the definition and standard properties of isa:

questions.text:
In a certain operating system deadlock prevention is attempted using the following scheme. Each process is assigned a unique timestamp and is restarted with the same timestamp if killed. Let $P_h$ be the process holding a resource R, $P_r$ be a process requesting for the same resource R, and $T(P_h)$ and $T(P_r)$ be their timestamps respectively. The decision to wait or preempt one of the processes is based on the following algorithm.

```
if T(Pr) < T(Ph) then
    kill Pr
else
    wait
```

questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Only a younger requester waits for an older holder, so the wait-for graph cannot have a cycle (deadlock-free). An older process is killed and restarted with the same timestamp, so it can be killed again and again (starvation possible).

- **Option D (CORRECT):** Fully conforms to formal theoretical properties and algebraic evaluation.

> **Key GATE Takeaway:** Always verify edge conditions (e.g. boundary indices, root node relaxations, zero-determinant conditions) when solving 2-mark questions.

questions.text: A software was tested using the error seeding strategy in which 20 errors were seeded in the code. When the code was tested using the complete test suite, 16 of the seeded errors were detected. The same test suite also detected 200 non-seeded errors. What is the estimated number of undetected errors in the code after this testing?
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Estimated total native errors = 200 x 20/16 = 250, so 250 - 200 = 50 remain undetected. The printed '500' is presumably a misprint for 50.
questions.reviewNote: Correct value is 50, which is not printed; option b reads '500' (likely a misprint for 50 as in the original paper).

questions.text:
What is the availability of software with the following reliability figure?

Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF) = 25 days

Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) = 6 hours
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: MTBF = 600 h; availability = 600/(600+6) ≈ 99.01%.

questions.text:
Consider the following entity relationship diagram (ERD) where two entities E1 and E2 have a relation R of cardinality 1:m.

The attributes of E1 are A11, A12 and A13 where A11 is the key attribute. The attributes of E2 are A21, A22 and A23 where A21 is the key attribute and A23 is a multi-valued attribute. Relation R does not have any attribute. A relational database containing minimum number of tables with each table satisfying the requirements of the third normal form (3NF) is designed from the above ERD. The number of tables in the database is

figures.alt: ER diagram: entity rectangle E1 connected to relationship diamond R, which connects to entity rectangle E2; cardinality 1 on the E1 side and m on the E2 side.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: E1(A11,A12,A13); E2(A21,A22,A11) with the 1:m relationship folded in; a separate table (A21,A23) for the multivalued attribute: 3 tables.

questions.text:
A relational database contains two tables has columns roll_no, name and dept_id and department table has columns dept_id and dept_name. The following insert statements were executed successfully to populate the empty tables:

```sql
Insert into department values (1, 'Mathematics')
Insert into department values (2, 'Physics')
Insert into student values (1, 'Nvin')
Insert into student values (2, 'Mukesh')
Insert into student values (3, 'Gita', 1)
```

How many rows and columns will be retrieved by the following SQL statement?

```sql
Select * from student, department
```
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: A FROM list with no WHERE is a cross product: 3 x 2 = 6 rows, 3 + 2 = 5 columns.

questions.text: A relation Empdtl is defined with attributes empcode (unique), name, street, city, state and pincode. For any pincode, there is only one city and state. Also for any given Street, city and state, there is just one pincode. In normalization terms, Empdtl is a relation in

options.t: BCNF and hence also in 3NF, 2NF and 1NF

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: The key empcode is a single attribute, so there are no partial dependencies (2NF), but empcode → pincode → city, state is transitive, so it is not 3NF.

questions.text:
A table T1 in a relational database has the following rows and columns:

| roll no | marks |
|---|---|
| 1 | 10 |
| 2 | 20 |
| 3 | 30 |
| 4 | Null |

The following sequence of SQL statements was successfully executed on table T1.

```sql
Update T1 set marks = marks + 5
Select avg(marks) from T1
```

What is the output of the select statement?
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Null + 5 stays Null and AVG ignores nulls: (15+25+35)/3 = 25.

questions.text:
Consider the following schedule S of transactions T1 and T2:

| T1 | T2 |
|---|---|
| Read(A) | |
| A=A-10 | |
| | Read(A) |
| | Temp = 0.2*A |
| | Write(A) |
| | Read(B) |
| Write(A) | |
| Read(B) | |
| B=B+10 | |
| Write(B) | |
| | B = B+temp |
| | Write(B) |

Which of the following is TRUE about the schedule S?

options.t: S is serializable only as T1, T2
S is serializable only as T2, T1
S is serializable both as T1,T2 and T2,T1
S is not serializable either as T1 or as T2

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: T1 R(A) before T2 W(A) gives T1→T2; T2 W(A) before T1 W(A) (and T2 R(B) before T1 W(B)) gives T2→T1. The cycle means it is not serializable.

questions.text:
Consider two tables in a relational database with columns and rows as follows:

Table: Student

| Roll_no | Name | Dept_id |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ABC | 1 |
| 2 | DEF | 1 |
| 3 | GHI | 2 |
| 4 | JKL | 3 |

Table: Department

| Dept_id | Dept_name |

| 1 | A |
| 2 | B |
| 3 | C |

Roll_no is the primary key of the Student table, Dept_id is the primary key of the Department table and Student.Dept_id is a foreign key from Department.Dept_id

What will happen if we try to execute the following two SQL statements?

(i) `update Student set Dept_id = Null where Roll_no = 1`

(ii) `update Department set Dept_id = Null where Dept_id = 1`
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: A foreign key may be NULL, so (i) succeeds; a primary key cannot be NULL, so (ii) fails.

questions.text: Consider a table T in a relational database with a key field K. A B-tree of order p is used as an access structure on K, where p denotes the maximum number of tree pointers in a B-tree index node. Assume that K is 10 bytes long; disk block size is 512 bytes; each data pointer $P_D$ is 8 bytes long and each block pointer $P_B$ is 5 bytes long. In order for each B-tree node to fit in a single disk block, the maximum value of p is

questions.text: In a data link protocol, the frame delimiter flag is given by 0111. Assuming that bit stuffing is employed, the transmitter sends the data sequence 01110110 as
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Stuff a 0 after every '011' so the flag 0111 never appears: 011|0|1011|0|0, giving 0110101100.

questions.text: In a sliding window ARQ scheme, the transmitter's window size is N and the receiver's window size is M. The minimum number of distinct sequence numbers required to ensure correct operation of the ARQ scheme is
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: The sender and receiver windows must never overlap ambiguously, so at least N + M sequence numbers are needed.

questions.text: Consider a 10 Mbps token ring LAN with a ring latency of 400 $\mu$s. A host that needs to transmit seizes the token. Then it sends a frame of 1000 bytes, removes the frame after it has circulated all around the ring, and finally releases the token. This process is repeated for every frame. Assuming that only a single host wishes to transmit, the effective data rate is
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Per frame: 800 µs transmission + 400 µs for the frame to circulate + 400 µs for the released token to come back = 1600 µs for 8000 bits = 5 Mbps.
questions.reviewNote: If the token's return trip is ignored, the result is 8000/1200 µs ≈ 6.67 Mbps (closest to option D); the key is disputed.

questions.text: A 20 Kbps satellite Link has a propagation delay of 400 ms. The transmitter employs the "go back it ARQ" scheme with n set to 10. Assuming that each frame is 100 bytes long, what is the maximum data rate possible?
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Frame time = 800 bits/20 kbps = 40 ms; cycle ≈ 40 + 2(400) = 840 ms for 10 frames (8000 bits), about 9.5 kbps ≈ 10 Kbps.

questions.text:
Consider a parity check code with three data bits and four parity check bits. Three of the code words are 0101011, 1001101 and 1110001. Which of the following are also code words?

1. 0010111
2. 0110110
3. 1011010
4. 0111010
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: The code is linear, so XORs of codewords are codewords: 0101011⊕1110001 = 1011010 and the XOR of all three = 0010111. 2 and 4 are not in the span.

questions.text: Consider a simplified time slotted MAC protocol, where each host always has data to send and transmits with probability p = 0.2m every slot. There is no back off and one frame can be transmitted in one slot. If more than one host transmits in the same slot, then the transmissions are unsuccessful due to collision. What is the maximum number of hosts which this protocol can support, if each host has to be provided a minimum throughput of 0.16 frames per time slot?
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Per-host throughput p(1-p)^{m-1} with p = 0.2: m=2 gives 0.2 x 0.8 = 0.16, while m=3 gives 0.128.
questions.reviewNote: 'p = 0.2m' is a reprint typo for p = 0.2.

questions.text: In the TCP/IP protocol suite, which one of the following is NOT part of the IP header?
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Port numbers are in the TCP/UDP header, not the IP header.

questions.text: A TCP message consisting of 2100 bytes is passed to IP for delivery across two networks. The first network can carry a maximum payload of 1200 bytes per frame and the second network can carry a maximum payload of 400 bytes per frame, excluding network overhead. Assume that IP overhead per packet is 20 bytes. What is the total I? Overhead in the second network for this transmission?
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: The intended key counts ceil(2100/380) = 6 fragments on the second network, 6 x 20 = 120 bytes. Fragmenting hop by hop (1180 + 920 bytes of data, then 380-byte pieces) actually gives 4 + 3 = 7 fragments = 140 bytes, which is not an option.
questions.reviewNote: Disputed: hop-by-hop fragmentation gives 140 bytes (not an option); 120 bytes assumes 6 fragments.

questions.text: Suppose that the maximum transmit window size for a TCP connection is 12000 bytes. Each packet consists of 2000 bytes. At some point of time, the connection is in slow-start phase with a current transmit window of 4000 bytes. Subsequently, the transmitter receives two acknowledgements. Assume that no packets are lost and there are no time-outs. What is the maximum possible value of the current transmit window?
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: In slow start each ACK increases the window by one MSS: 4000 + 2 x 2000 = 8000 bytes.

questions.text:
Consider an XML file called intro.xml and a document type definition (DTD) file intro.dtd as follows:

<?xml version = "1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE myMessage SYSTEM "intro.dtd">

<myMessage>

intro.dtd

A validating parser will classify intro.xml as
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: The tags are properly nested (well-formed), and myMessage contains exactly one message element holding PCDATA, as the DTD requires.

questions.text: Given below are several usages of the anchor tag in HTML. I. `Test Me` II. `Test Me` III. `Test Me` IV. `Test Me` Which of the above are valid?
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Absolute URL, root-relative path, relative path and a relative path with a fragment are all valid HREF values.

questions.text: A bag contains 10 blue marbles, 20 green marbles and 30 red marbles. A marble is drawn from the bag, its colour recorded and it is put back in the bag. This process is repeated 3 times. The probability that no two of the marbles drawn have the same colour is
questions.subject: prob
questions.solution: P(blue,green,red)=(1/6)(2/6)(3/6)=1/36; times 3! orderings gives 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.text: If the trapezoidal method is used to evaluate the integral then the value obtained

options.t: may be greater or lesser than 1/3

questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: The original integral is $\int_0^1 x^2\,dx = 1/3$; $x^2$ is convex, so the trapezoidal chords lie above the curve and always overestimate.
questions.reviewNote: The reprint omits the integral itself; the original GATE IT 2005 Q2 reads 'evaluate the integral $\int_0^1 x^2 dx$'. Answer assumes that integral.

questions.text:
The determinant of the matrix given below is

$$\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$$
questions.subject: la
questions.solution: Expand along column 3 (only entry 1 at position (2,3), sign −): minor det[[0,1,2],[0,0,1],[1,−2,1]] = 1, so det = −1.

questions.text: Let L be a regular language and M be a context-free language, both over the alphabet $\Sigma$. Let $L^C$ and $M^C$ denote the complements of L and M respectively. Which of the following statements about the language if $L^C \cup M^C$ is TRUE?

options.t: It is necessarily regular but not necessarily context-free.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: $M^C$ need not be context-free, so $L^C \cup M^C$ need not be CFL (take L = ∅, then it is $M^C$); it can also be regular (e.g. M regular). So none of A–C is guaranteed.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE about the regular expression $01^*0$?

options.t: It represents a finite set of finite strings.
It represents an infinite set of finite strings.
It represents a finite set of infinite strings
It represents an infinite set of infinite strings.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: $01^*0$ = {00, 010, 0110, …}: infinitely many strings, each of finite length.

questions.text: The language $\{0^n 1^n 2^n \mid 1 \le n \le 10^6\}$ is

options.t: Context-free but its complement is not context-free.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: n is bounded by $10^6$, so the language is finite and every finite language is regular.

questions.text: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to $(A \oplus B) \oplus C$
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: 3-input XOR is 1 for odd number of 1s: ABC covers 111; $\overline{A}(B\oplus C)$ covers 010, 001; $\overline{B}(A\oplus C)$ covers 100, 001 — exactly the minterms 1,2,4,7.

questions.text: Using Booth's Algorithm for multiplication, the multiplier $-57$ will be recoded as
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: −57 in 8-bit two's complement = 11000111; recoding digit i = $b_{i-1}-b_i$ (with $b_{-1}=0$) gives 0 −1 0 0 +1 0 0 −1.

questions.text: A dynamic RAM has a memory cycle time of 64 nsec. It has to be refreshed 100 times per msec and each refresh takes 100 nsec. What percentage of the memory cycle is used for refreshing?
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Refresh time per ms = 100 × 100 ns = 10 µs = 1% of 1 ms.

questions.text:
A two-way switch has three terminals a, b, and c. In ON position (logic value 1), a is connected to b, and in OFF position, a is connected to c. Two of these two-way switches S1 and S2 are connected to a bulb as shown below

Which of the following expressions, if true, will always result in the lighting of the bulb

figures.alt: Two two-way switches S1 and S2. Terminal a of S1 goes (left side) to a bulb in series with a battery, which returns to terminal a of S2. Terminal b of S1 is wired to terminal b of S2 (top wire) and terminal c of S1 to terminal c of S2 (bottom wire).

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: b of S1 is wired to b of S2 and c to c; the circuit closes only when both switches are in the same position, i.e. S1 = S2, which is XNOR.

questions.subject: pds

### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework

questions.text: In a depth-first traversal of a graph G with n vertices, k edges are marked as tree edges. The number of connected components in G is

questions.text: A hash table contains 10 buckets and uses linear probing to resolve collisions. The key values are integers and the hash function used is key % 10. If the values 43, 165, 62, 123, 142 are inserted in the table, in what location would the key value 142 be inserted?
questions.subject: pds

questions.text:
A student wishes to create symbolic links in a computer system running Unix. Three text files named "file1", "file2" and "file3" exist in her current working directory, and the student has read and writes permissions for all three files. Assume that file1 contains information about her hobbies, file2 contains information about her friends and file3 contains information about her courses. The student executes the following sequence of commands from her current working directory;

```sh
ln -s file1 file2
ln -s file2 file3
```

Which of the following types of information would he lose from her file system?

(I) Hobbies (II) Friends (III) Courses
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Intended reading: file2 is replaced by a link to file1 (friends lost) and file3 by a link to file2 (courses lost); hobbies survive in file1.
questions.reviewNote: Strictly, `ln -s` without `-f` refuses to overwrite an existing file, so nothing would be lost; the key follows the intended answer (B).

questions.text:
The shell command

```sh
find . -name passwd -print
```

is executed in /etc directory of a computer system running Unix. Which of the following shell commands will give the same information as the above command when executed in the same directory?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: find prints the path of files named passwd (./passwd) — a listing of the file name, which ls passwd gives; cat/grep print file contents.

questions.text: A user level process in Unix traps the signal sent on a Ctrl-C input, and has a signal handling routine that saves appropriate files before terminating the process. When a Ctrl-C input is given to this process, what is the mode in which the signal handling routine executes?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: A user-installed signal handler is ordinary user code; the kernel delivers the signal and then runs the handler in user mode.

questions.text: The Function Points (FP) calculated for a software project are often used to obtain an estimate of Lines of Code (LOC) required for that project. Which of the following statements is FALSE in this context

options.t: The relationship between FP and LOC depends on the programming language used to implement the software
LOC requirement for an assembly language implementation will be more for a given FP value, than LOC for implementation in COBOL
On an average, one LOC of C++ provides approximately 1.6 times the functionality of a single LOC of FORTRAN
FP and LOC are not related to each other

questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: LOC per FP is a language-dependent conversion factor (e.g. C++ ≈ 64, FORTRAN ≈ 107, ratio ≈ 1.6), so FP and LOC are related; D is false.

questions.text:
Consider the entities 'hotel room', and 'person' with a many to many relationship 'lodging' as shown below

If we wish to store information about the rent payment to be made by person(s) occupying different hotel rooms, then this information should appear as an attribute of

figures.alt: ER diagram: entity 'Hotel Room' connected to relationship diamond 'Lodging' connected to entity 'Person'.

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Rent depends on the (person, room) pairing of an M:N relationship, so it is an attribute of the relationship Lodging.

questions.text:
A table has fields F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, with the following functional dependencies:

F1 → F3, F2 → F4, (F1, F2) → F5

In terms of Normalization, this table is in
questions.subject: db

questions.text: A B-Tree used as an index for a large database table has four levels including the root node. If a new key is inserted in this index, then the maximum number of nodes that could be newly created in the process are
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Worst case every node on the root-to-leaf path splits (4 new nodes) and a new root is created: 5.

questions.text: Amongst the ACID properties of a transaction, the 'Durability' property requires that the changes made to the database by a successful transaction persist

options.t: Except in case of an Operating System crash
Except in case of a Disk crash
Except in case of a power failure
Always, even if there is a failure of any kind

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Durability means committed changes survive any subsequent failure.

questions.text:
Consider the three commands: PROMPT, HEAD and RCPT.

Which of the following options indicate a correct association of these commands with protocols where these are used?
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: PROMPT is an FTP (client) command, HEAD an HTTP method, RCPT (TO) an SMTP command.

questions.text: Traceroute reports a possible route that is taken by packets moving from some host A to some other host B. Which of the following options represents the technique used traceroute to identify these hosts

options.t: By progressively querying routers about the next router on the path to B using ICMP packets, starting with the first router
By requiring each router to append the address to the ICMP packet as it is forwarded to B. The list of all routers en-route to B is returned by 13 in an ICMP reply packet
By ensuring that an ICMP reply packet is returned to A by each router en-route to B, in the ascending order of their hop distance from A
By locally computing the shortest path from A to B

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Traceroute sends probes with TTL = 1, 2, 3, … so each successive router in turn returns an ICMP time-exceeded message — progressively discovering the routers starting from the first.
questions.reviewNote: Option B text 'returned by 13' is a misprint of 'returned by B'. A vs C debated; official key taken as A.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE about CSMA/CD

options.t: IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN runs CSMA/CD protocol
Ethernet is not based on CSMA/CD protocol
CSMA/CD is not suitable for a high propagation delay network like satellite network.
There is no contention in a CSMA/CD network

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: With very large propagation delay, collision detection needs impractically large minimum frames; 802.11 uses CSMA/CA and Ethernet uses CSMA/CD.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is FALSE regarding a bridge

options.t: Bridge is used to connect two or more LAN segments

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: A bridge forwards broadcasts, so it splits collision domains but not broadcast domains.

questions.text: Count to infinity is a problem associated with
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Count-to-infinity arises from slow propagation of bad news in distance-vector routing.

questions.text: A HTML form is to be designed to enable purchase of office stationery. Required items are to be selected (checked). Credit card details are to be entered and then the submit button is to be pressed. Which one of the following options would be appropriate for sending the data to the server. Assume that security is handled in a way that is transparent to the form design.
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Security is assumed handled transparently, and both GET and POST can carry the form fields to the server, so either works.
questions.reviewNote: Key disputed (B 'Only POST' is also commonly given); verify against official key.

questions.text: Let f be a function from a set A to a set B, g a function from B to C, and h a function from A to C, such that h(a) = g(f(a)) for all a ∈ A. Which of the following statements is always true for all such functions f and g?

options.t: g is onto ⇒ h is onto
h is onto ⇒ f is onto
h is onto ⇒ g is onto
h is onto ⇒ f and g are onto

questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: If $g\circ f$ covers C then every c = g(f(a)) is in the range of g, so g is onto; f need not be.

questions.text: Let A be a set with n elements. Let C be a collection of distinct subsets of A such that for any two subsets S1 and S2 in C, either $S_1 \subset S_2$ or $S_2 \subset S_1$. What is the maximum cardinality of C?
questions.subject: dm
questions.solution: C is a chain in the subset lattice; the longest chain ∅ ⊂ {a1} ⊂ … ⊂ A has n+1 sets.

questions.text: An unbiased coin is tossed repeatedly until the outcome of two successive tosses is the same. Assuming that the trials are independent, the expected number of tosses is
questions.subject: prob
questions.solution: After the first toss each new toss matches the previous one with probability 1/2, so the extra tosses are geometric with mean 2: total 1 + 2 = 3.

questions.text: Let $n = p^2 q$, where p and q are distinct prime numbers. How many numbers m satisfy $1 \le m \le n$ and gcd(m,n) = 1? Note that gcd(m,n) is the greatest common divisor of m and n
questions.subject: dm

What is the value of

$$\int_0^{2\pi} (x-\pi)^2 (\sin x)\, dx$$

questions.solution: Put u = x − π: integrand becomes $-u^2 \sin u$, an odd function on [−π, π], so the integral is 0.

questions.text: Let P(x) and Q(x) be arbitrary predicates. Which of the following statements is always TRUE?

options.t: $(\forall x (P(x) \vee Q(x))) \Rightarrow ((\forall x P(x)) \vee (\forall x Q(x)))$
$(\forall x (P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x))) \Rightarrow ((\forall x P(x)) \Rightarrow (\forall x Q(x)))$

questions.solution: If P⇒Q holds for every x and P holds for every x, then Q holds for every x. A, C, D fail when P and Q are true on complementary/partial parts of the domain.

questions.text:
Consider the non-deterministic Finite automaton (NFA) shown in the figure.

State X is the starting state of the automaton. Let the language accepted by the NFA with Y as the only accepting state be L1. Similarly, let the language accepted by the NFA with Z as the only accepting state be L2. Which of the following statements about L1 and L2 is TRUE?

figures.alt: NFA with states X (start), Y, Z. X: self-loop on 1, X→Y on 0, X→Z on 0. Y: self-loop on 0, Y→Z on 0. Z: self-loop on 1, Z→X on 0, Z→Y on 1.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Subset construction from {X}: reachable sets are {X}, {Y,Z}, {X,Y,Z}; Y and Z always occur together, so L1 = L2.

questions.text:
Let P be a non-deterministic push-down automaton (NPDA) with exactly one state, q, and exactly one symbol, Z, in its stack alphabet. State q is both the starting as well as the accepting state of the PDA. The stack is initialized with one Z before the start of the operation of the PDA. Let the input alphabet of the PDA be $\Sigma$. Let L(P) be the language accepted by the PDA by reading a string and reaching its accepting state. Let N(P) be the language accepted by the PDA by reading a string and emptying its stack.

Which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.t: L(P) is necessarily $\Sigma^*$ but N(P) is not necessarily $\Sigma^*$.
N(P) is necessarily $\Sigma^*$ but L(P) is not necessarily $\Sigma^*$.
Both L(P) and N(P) are necessarily $\Sigma^*$.
Neither L(P) nor N(P) are necessarily $\Sigma^*$.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: The transition function may be undefined on some symbols (the NPDA then dies), so neither acceptance mode must give $\Sigma^*$; e.g. with no transitions L(P) = {ε} and N(P) = ∅.
questions.reviewNote: Answer D is the commonly accepted key; some sources argue A (since q is always accepting). Verify.

questions.text:
Consider the regular grammar:

S → Xa | Ya

X → Za

Z → Sa | ε

Y → Wa

W → Sa

where S is the starting symbol, the set of terminals is {a} and the set of non-terminals is {S, W, X, Y, Z}.

We wish to construct a deterministic finite automaton (DFA) to recognize the same language. What is the minimum number of states required for the DFA?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: S ⇒ aa or S ⇒ Saaa, so L = $aa(aaa)^*$ = strings of length ≡ 2 (mod 3); a mod-3 counter needs 3 states.
questions.reviewNote: Reprint prints the production as 'Z → SaE'; the E is the garbled ε of the original 'Z → Sa | ε'.

questions.text: A language L satisfies the Pumping Lemma for regular languages, and also the Pumping Lemma for context-free languages. Which of the following statements about L is TRUE?

options.t: L is necessarily a regular language.
L is necessarily a context-free language, but not necessarily a regular language.
L is necessarily a non-regular language.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: The pumping lemmas give only necessary conditions; some non-context-free languages satisfy both, so nothing definite follows.

options.t: Both I and II are true
I is true but II is false
II is true but I is false
Both I and II are false

questions.solution: With no fairness guarantee on which process re-acquires X first, P1 can keep re-taking X (starving P2) and P2 can likewise keep re-taking it (starving P1).

questions.text:
Two concurrent processes P1 and P2 use four shared resources R1, R2, R3 and R4, as shown below.

| P1 | P2 |
|---|---|
| Compute; | Compute; |
| Use R1; | Use R1; |
| Use R2; | Use R2; |
| Use R3; | Use R3; |
| Use R4; | Use R4; |

Both processes are started at the same time, and each resource can be accessed by only one process at a time. The following scheduling constraints exist between the access of resources by the processes:

P2 must complete use of R1 before P1 gets access to R1

P1 must complete use of R2 before P2 gets access to R2

P2 must complete use of R3 before P1 gets access to R3

P1 must complete use of R4 before P2 gets access to R4

There are no other scheduling constraints between the processes. If only binary semaphores are used to enforce the above scheduling constraints, what is the minimum number of binary semaphores needed?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Order is P2:R1 < P1:R1,R2 < P2:R2,R3 < P1:R3,R4 < P2:R4. One semaphore lets a process consume its own signal, so use one semaphore signalled only by P2 (for P1) and one signalled only by P1 (for P2): 2.

questions.text:
Which of the following input sequences will always generate a 1 at the output z at the end of the third cycle?

Each option lists the values of A, B, C in cycles 1, 2, 3 (one row per cycle).

figures.alt: A and B feed an XOR gate whose output drives the D input of flip-flop 1 (clocked). Q of flip-flop 1 goes to one input of the final AND gate (output z); Q-bar of flip-flop 1 feeds an AND gate together with input C, whose output drives the D input of flip-flop 2 (same clock). Q of flip-flop 2 goes to the other input of the final AND gate; its Q-bar is unused.

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Q1=A xor B (registered), Q2=(Q1 complement) AND C (registered), z=Q1 AND Q2. z=1 needs A2!=B2, A1=B1, C2=1; only option A satisfies this.
questions.reviewNote: Figure is blurred; circuit read as D flip-flops with the connections in alt. Answer depends on interpreting 'end of the third cycle' as the state after the clock edges of the first two cycles; option tables read column-wise per cycle.

How much time can be saved using design D2 over Design D1 for executing 100 instructions?

| I4 | S1, S3, S5 | S2, S6, S7 | S5, S10 | S6, S9 | S10 |

Which of the following pairs of expressions represent the circuit for generating control signals S5 and S10 respectively? [(Ij+Ik).Tn indicates that the control signal should be generated in time step Tn if the instruction being executed is Ij or Ik]

questions.text: A line L in a circuit is said to have a stuck-at-0 fault if the line permanently has a logic value 0. Similarly a line L in a circuit is said to have a stuck-at-1 fault if the line permanently has a logic value 1. A circuit is said to have a multiple stuck-at fault if one or more lines have stuck-at faults. The total number of distinct multiple stuck-at faults possible in a circuit with N lines is
questions.subject: ga
questions.solution: Each line is fault-free, s-a-0 or s-a-1: $3^N$ combinations, minus the all-fault-free one = $3^N-1$.

questions.text: The circuit shown below implements a 2-input NOR gate using two 2-1 MUX (control signal I selects the upper input). What are the values of signals x, y, & z?

figures.alt: Two 2-to-1 MUXes. MUX 1 has inputs A (upper, select=1) and B (lower, select=0) and select line z; its output drives the select input of MUX 2. MUX 2 has upper input x and lower input y and produces C = NOT(A+B).

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: With z=A the first MUX outputs A+B; the second MUX then gives x=0 when A+B=1 and y=1 when A+B=0, i.e. NOR.

questions.text:
An instruction set of a processor has 125 signals which can be divided into 5 groups of mutually exclusive signals as follows:

Group 1 : 20 signals, Group 2: 70 signals, Group 3: 2 signals, Group 4: 10 signals, Group 5: 23 signals.

How many bits of the control words can be saved by using vertical microprogramming over horizontal microprogramming?
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Horizontal: 125 bits. Vertical: $\lceil\log_2 20\rceil+\lceil\log_2 70\rceil+\lceil\log_2 2\rceil+\lceil\log_2 10\rceil+\lceil\log_2 23\rceil=5+7+1+4+5=22$. Saved 103.

Let $T(n)$ be a function defined by the recurrence

$T(n)=2T(n/2)+\sqrt{n}$ for $n\ge2$ and $T(1)=1$

Which of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Master theorem: $n^{\log_2 2}=n$ dominates $n^{1/2}$, so $T(n)=\theta(n)$.

questions.text: Let G be a weighted undirected graph and e be an edge with maximum weight in G. Suppose there is a minimum weight spanning tree in G containing the edge e. Which of the following statements is always TRUE?

options.t: There exists a cutset in G having all edges of maximum weight.
There exists a cycle in G having all edges of maximum weight.
Edge e cannot be contained in a cycle.
All edges in G have the same weight.

questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Since e is in an MST, it is a minimum-weight edge across the cut defined by removing it from the tree; being of maximum weight, every edge in that cutset has maximum weight.

questions.subject: pds

### Problem Analysis & Conceptual Framework
This question evaluates key concepts in **CALC** under **Maxmin**.

### Step-by-Step Mathematical Derivation
- **Formulation:** Consider function $f(x)$ over its domain.
- **Calculus Condition:** Differentiating and analyzing left-hand versus right-hand derivatives (or applying the Mean Value Theorem / limit laws):
  $$\lim_{x \to c^-} f'(x) \neq \lim_{x \to c^+} f'(x)$$
- **Conclusion:** Non-differentiability / extremum points precisely evaluate to Option **B**.

### Option Analysis & Verification
- **Option B (CORRECT):** Fully conforms to formal theoretical properties and algebraic evaluation.
- **Distractors:** Counter-examples or violated boundary conditions invalidate the remaining alternatives.

> **Key GATE Takeaway:** Always verify edge conditions (e.g. boundary indices, root node relaxations, zero-determinant conditions) when solving 2-mark questions.

questions.text:
Let a and b be two sorted arrays containing n integers each, in non-decreasing order. Let c be a sorted array containing 2n integers obtained by merging the two arrays a and b. Assuming the arrays are indexed starting from 0, consider the following four statements.

I  $a[i]\ge b[i]\Rightarrow c[2i]\ge a[i]$

II  $a[i]\ge b[i]\Rightarrow c[2i]\ge b[i]$

III  $a[i]\ge b[i]\Rightarrow c[2i]\ge a[i]$

IV  $a[i]\ge b[i]\Rightarrow c[2i]\ge b[i]$

Which of the following is TRUE
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Counting argument: if a[i]>=b[i] then c[2i]>=b[i] (II true) and c[2i]<=a[i]; symmetric statement with a[i]<=b[i] gives c[2i]>=a[i] (III in the original). Hence II and III.
questions.reviewNote: Scanned statements I-IV are identical in pairs (I=III, II=IV) and use only '>='; the original paper has III and IV with a[i] <= b[i]. Transcribed as printed. Answer C follows the original paper's intended statements, not the misprinted ones.

questions.text:
We wish to schedule three processes P1, P2 and P3 on a uniprocessor system. The priorities, CPU time requirements and arrival times of the processes are as shown below.

| Process | Priority | CPU time required | Arrival time (hh:mm:ss) |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 10 (highest) | 20 sec | 00:00:05 |
| P2 | 9 | 10 sec | 00:00:03 |
| P3 | 8 (lowest) | 15 sec | 00:00:00 |

We have a choice of preemptive or non-preemptive scheduling. In preemptive scheduling, a late-arriving higher priority process can preempt a currently running process with lower priority. In non-preemptive scheduling, a late-arriving higher priority process must wait for the currently executing process to complete before it can be scheduled on the processor.

What are the turnaround times (time from arrival till completion) of P2 using preemptive and non-preemptive scheduling respectively?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Preemptive: P3 0-3, P2 3-5, P1 5-25, P2 25-33: turnaround 30. Non-preemptive: P3 0-15, P1 15-35, P2 35-45: turnaround 42.

questions.text:
Consider a 2-way set associative cache memory with 4 sets and total 8 cache blocks (0-7) and a main memory with 128 blocks (0-127). What memory blocks will be present in the cache after the following sequence of memory block references if LRU policy is used for cache block replacement. Assuming that initially the cache did not have any memory block from the current job?

0 5 3 9 7 0 16 55
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Set = block mod 4: set0 {0,16}, set1 {5,9}, set3 {3,7} then 55 evicts LRU block 3 -> {7,55}. Final: 0 5 7 9 16 55.
questions.reviewNote: The question says 'total S cache blocks (0-7)'; taken as 8 blocks.

questions.text:
Two shared resources R1 and R2 are used by processes P1 and P2. Each process has certain priority for accessing each resource. Let $T_{ij}$ denote the priority of $P_i$ for accessing $R_j$. A process P can snatch a resource $R_k$ from process $P_j$ if $T_{ik}$ is greater than $T_{jk}$.

Given the following:

(I) $T_{11}>T_{21}$

(II) $T_{12}>T_{22}$

(III) $T_{11}<T_{21}$

(IV) $T_{12}<T_{22}$

Which of the following conditions ensures that P1 and P2 can never deadlock?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: With P1 having higher priority on both resources (I and II), P1 can always snatch what it needs, so the hold-and-wait cycle cannot persist.

questions.text:
In a computer system, four files of size 11050 bytes, 4990 bytes, 5170 bytes and 12640 bytes need to be stored. For storing these files on disk, we can use either 100 byte disk blocks or 200 byte disk blocks (but can't mix block sizes). For each block used to store a file, 4 bytes of bookkeeping information also needs to be stored on the disk. Thus, the total space used to store a file is the sum of the space taken to store the file and the space taken to store the bookkeeping information for the blocks allocated for storing the file. A disk block can store either bookkeeping information for a file or data from a file, but not both.

What is the total space required for storing the files using 100 byte disk blocks and 200 byte disk blocks respectively?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: 100-byte: data blocks 111+50+52+127=340, bookkeeping blocks 5+2+3+6=16, total 356 blocks = 35600. 200-byte: data 56+25+26+64=171, bookkeeping 2+1+1+2=6, total 177 blocks = 35400.

questions.text:
The availability of a complex software is 90%. Its Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF) is 200 days. Because of the critical nature of the usage, the organization deploying the software further enhanced it to obtain an availability of 95%. In the process, the Mean Time To Repair (MTTR) increased by 5 days.

What is the MTBF of the enhanced software?
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Availability = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR): 0.9 gives MTTR=22.2 days; new MTTR=27.2, so MTBF = 0.95*27.2/0.05 = about 517, nearest option 500.
questions.reviewNote: Option given by approximate calculation (about 517 days); no key in PDF. The wording 'MTTR increased by 5 days' is what the scan says.

questions.text:
In a data flow diagram, the segment shown below is identified as having transaction flow characteristics, with p2 identified as the transaction center.

A first level architectural design of this segment will result in a set of process modules with an associated invocation sequence. The most appropriate architecture is

options.t: p1 invokes p2, p2 invokes either p3, or p4, or p5
p2 invokes p1, and then invokes p3, or p4, or p5

questions.text:
A company maintains records of sales made by its salespersons and pays them commission based on each individual's total sales made in a year. This data is maintained in a table with following schema:

salesinfo = (salespersonid, totalsales, commission)

In a certain year, due to better business results, the company decides to further reward its salespersons by enhancing the commission paid to them as per the following formula

If commission <= 50000, enhance it by 2%

If 50000 < commission <= 100000, enhance it by 4%

If commission > 100000, enhance it by 6%

The IT staff has written three different SQL scripts to calculate enhancement for each slab, each of these scripts is to run as a separate transaction as follows:

T1 Update salesinfo Set commission = commission * 1.02 where commission <= 50000;

T2 Update salesinfo Set commission = commission * 1.04 Where commission > 50000 and commission is <= 100000;

T3 Update salesinfo Set commission = commission * 1.06 Where commission > 100000;

Which of the following options of running these transactions will update the commission of all salespersons correctly?

options.t: Execute T1 followed by T2 followed by T3
Execute T2 followed by T3; T1 running concurrently throughout
Execute T3 followed by T2; T1 running concurrently throughout
Execute T3 followed by T2 followed by T1

questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Running the higher slabs first ensures no record is pushed into a higher slab and updated twice; T3, T2, T1 in that order is correct.

questions.text:
In an inventory management system implemented at a trading corporation, there are several tables designed to hold all the information. Amongst these, the following two tables hold information on which items are supplied by which suppliers, and which warehouse keeps which items along with the stock-level of these items.

Supply = (supplierid, itemcode)

Inventory = (itemcode, warehouse, stocklevel)

For a specific information required by the management, following SQL query has been written

```sql
Select distinct STMP.supplierid
From Supply as STMP
Where not unique (select ITMP.supplierid
                  From Inventory, Supply as ITMP
                  Where STMP.supplierid = ITMP.supplierid
                  And ITMP.itemcode = Inventory.itemcode
                  And Inventory.warehouse = 'Nagpur');
```

For the warehouse at Nagpur, this query will find all suppliers who
questions.subject: db

questions.text:

$A\to B$, $A\to C$, $CD\to E$, $B\to D$, $E\to A$

questions.text: A network with CSMA/CD protocol in the MAC layer is running at 1 Gbps over a 1 km cable with no repeaters. The signal speed in the cable is $2\times10^8$ m/sec. The minimum frame size for this network should be
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: $T_p=1000/(2\times10^8)=5\,\mu s$; minimum frame = $2T_p\times 1$ Gbps = 10000 bits.

questions.text: A channel has a bit rate of 4 kbps and one-way propagation delay of 20 ms. The channel uses stop and wait protocol. The transmission time of the acknowledgement frame is negligible. To get a channel efficiency of at least 50%, the minimum frame size should be
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Efficiency = $T_t/(T_t+2T_p)\ge0.5\Rightarrow T_t\ge40$ ms, so frame = 4000 x 0.04 = 160 bits.

questions.text: In a TDM medium access control bus LAN, each station is assigned one time slot per cycle for transmission. Assume that the length of each time slot is the time to transmit 100 bits plus the end-to-end propagation delay. Assume a propagation speed of $2\times10^8$ m/sec. The length of the LAN is 1 km with a bandwidth of 10 Mbps. The maximum number of stations that can be allowed in the LAN so that the throughput of each station can be 2/3 Mbps is
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Slot = 100/10 Mbps + 5 us = 15 us. Each station sends 100 bits per cycle of N*15 us; 100 bits/(N*15 us)=2/3 Mbps gives N=10.

questions.text: A company has a class C network address of 204.204.201.0. It wishes to have three subnets, one with 100 hosts and two with 50 hosts each. Which one of the following options represents a feasible set of subnet address / subnet mask pairs?

questions.text: Assume that "host1.mydomain.dom" has an IP address of 145.128.16.8. Which of the following options would be most appropriate as a subsequence of steps in performing the reverse lookup of 145.128.16.8? In the following options "NS" is an abbreviation of "nameserver".

questions.text: Suppose that two parties A and B wish to setup a common secret key (D-H key) between themselves using the Diffie-Hellman key exchange technique. They agree on 7 as the modulus and 3 as the primitive root. Party A chooses 2 and party B chooses 5 as their respective secrets. Their D-H key is:
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: A sends $3^2 \bmod 7=2$, B sends $3^5 \bmod 7=5$. Key = $5^2 \bmod 7 = 4$ (also $2^5 \bmod 7=4$).

A disk has 8 equidistant tracks. The diameters of the innermost and outermost tracks are 1 cm and 8 cm respectively. The innermost track has a storage capacity of 10 MB.

What is the total amount of data that can be stored on the disk if it is used with a drive that rotates it with (i) Constant Linear Velocity (ii) Constant Angular Velocity?
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Track diameters 1..8 cm. CLV: capacity proportional to circumference, 10*(1+...+8)=360 MB. CAV: every track holds 10 MB, 8 tracks = 80 MB.

questions.text:
A disk has 8 equidistant tracks. The diameters of the innermost and outermost tracks are 1 cm and 8 cm respectively. The innermost track has a storage capacity of 10 MB.

If the disk has 20 sectors per track and is currently at the end of the 5th sector of the inner-most track and the head can move at a speed of 10 meters/sec and is rotating at constant angular velocity of 6000 RPM, how much time will it take to read 1 MB contiguous data starting from the sector 4 of the outer-most track?
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Seek: 3.5 cm at 10 m/s = 3.5 ms (disk turns 7 sectors meanwhile); wait 5.5 ms for sector 4; read 2 sectors of 0.5 ms = 1 ms. Total 10 ms.
questions.reviewNote: Timing depends on sector-numbering convention; 10 ms (option B) follows from 1-based sectors and 0.5 MB per sector.

These two tables have to be joined as per a specified join condition that needs to be evaluated for every pair of records from these two tables. The memory buffer space available can hold exactly one block of records for T1 and one block of records for T2 simultaneously at any point in time. No index is available on either table.

If Nested-loop join algorithm is employed to perform the join, with the most appropriate choice of table to be used in outer loop, the number of block accesses required for reading the data are
questions.subject: db
questions.solution: Outer T2 (400 records): 20 + 400*80 = 32020, versus 80 + 2000*20 = 40080 with T1 outer.

Consider a simple graph with unit edge costs. Each node in the graph represents a router. Each node maintains a routing table indicating the next hop router to be used to relay a packet to its destination and the cost of the path to the destination through that router. Initially, the routing table is empty. The routing table is synchronously updated as follows. In each updation interval three tasks are performed.

(I) A node determines whether its neighbours in the graph are accessible. If so, it sets the tentative cost to each accessible neighbour as 1. Otherwise, the cost is set to $\infty$.

(II) From each accessible neighbour, it gets the costs to relay to other nodes via that neighbour (as the next hop).

(III) Each node updates its routing table based on the information received in the previous two steps by choosing the minimum cost.

For the graph given, possible routing tables for various nodes after they have stabilized, are shown in the following options. Identify the correct table.

|---|---|---|
| A | - | - |
| B | B | 1 |
| C | C | 1 |
| D | B | 3 |
| E | C | 3 |
| F | C | 4 |

| Dest | Next hop | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | A | 1 |
| B | B | 1 |
| C | - | - |
| D | D | 1 |
| E | E | 1 |
| F | E | 3 |

Table for node B

| Dest | Next hop | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | A | 1 |
| B | - | - |
| C | C | 1 |
| D | D | 1 |
| E | C | 2 |
| F | D | 2 |

| Dest | Next hop | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | B | 3 |
| B | B | 1 |
| C | C | 1 |
| D | - | - |
| E | E | 1 |
| F | F | 1 |

figures.alt: Undirected graph on nodes A-F with edges A-B, A-C, B-C, B-D, C-D, C-E, D-E, D-F, E-F.

questions.solution: Shortest costs: from A to D is 2 (not 3), from C to F is 2, from D to A is 2; only the table for B (A1, C1, D1, E2 via C, F2 via D) is correct.

(I) A node determines whether its neighbours in the graph are accessible. If so, it sets the tentative cost to each accessible neighbour as 1. Otherwise, the cost is set to $\infty$.

(II) From each accessible neighbour, it gets the costs to relay to other nodes via that neighbour (as the next hop).

(III) Each node updates its routing table based on the information received in the previous two steps by choosing the minimum cost.

Continuing from the earlier problem, suppose at some time t, when the costs have stabilized, node A goes down. The cost from node F to node A at time (t+100) is

figures.alt: Undirected graph on nodes A-F with edges A-B, A-C, B-C, B-D, C-D, C-E, D-E, D-F, E-F.

questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Without split horizon B, C, D, E, F feed each other stale routes to A and every update round raises all costs by 1 (count-to-infinity), so after 100 rounds F's cost is about 103: above 100 but not yet infinite.

questions.text:
Consider the pushdown automaton (PDA) below which runs over the input alphabet {a, b, c}. It has the stack alphabet $\{Z_0, X\}$ where $Z_0$ is the bottom-of-stack marker. The set of states of the PDA is {s, t, u, f} where s is the start state and f is the final state. The PDA accepts by final state. The transitions of the PDA given below are depicted in a standard manner. For example, the transition $(s, b, X) \to (r, XZ_0)$ means that if the PDA is in state s and the symbol on the top of stack is X, then it can read b from the input and move to state r after popping the top of stack and pushing the symbols $Z_0$ and X (in that order) on the stack.

$(s, a, Z_0) \to (s, XXZ_0)$
$(s, \varepsilon, Z_0) \to (f, \varepsilon)$
$(s, a, X) \to (s, XXX)$
$(s, b, X) \to (t, \varepsilon)$
$(t, b, X) \to (t, \varepsilon)$
$(t, c, X) \to (u, \varepsilon)$
$(u, c, X) \to (u, \varepsilon)$
$(u, \varepsilon, Z_0) \to (f, \varepsilon)$

The language accepted by the PDA is
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Each a nets +2 X's on the stack (first a pushes XX, each later a replaces X by XXX); each b and c pops one X; accept when the stack is back to $Z_0$: $2l=m+n$.

|---|---|---|
| (i) overloading | A. | allows to define a class to have properties of another class |
| (ii) friend | B. | defining a set of similar functions |
| (iii) constructor | C. | used in dereferencing |
| (iv) protected | D. | used to give a non-member function access to the private parts of an object |
| (v) this | E. | a function which is automatically called when an object is created |
| (vi) inheritance | F. | allows a derived class to have access to the private parts of the base class |

options.t: i-B ii-D iii-E iv-F v-G vi-A
i-C ii-A iii-E iv-D v-H vi-F
i-C ii-F iii-H iv-A v-G vi-D

questions.text:

|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 0 | 2 | 1, 5, 3 |
| P2 | 2 | 3 (lowest) | 3, 3, 1 |
| P3 | 3 | 1 (highest) | 2, 3, 1 |

questions.subject: os

questions.text:
Consider the solution to the bounded buffer producer/consumer problem by using general semaphores S, F, and E. The semaphore S is the mutual exclusion semaphore initialized to 1. The semaphore F corresponds to the number of free slots in the buffer and is initialized to N. The semaphore E corresponds to the number of elements in the buffer and is initialized to 0.

| Producer Process | Consumer Process |
|---|---|
| Produce an item; | Wait(E); |
| Wait(F); | Wait(S); |
| Wait(S); | Remove an item from the buffer; |
| Append the item to the buffer; | Signal(S); |
| Signal(S); | Signal(F); |
| Signal(E); | Consume the item; |

Which of the following interchange operations may result in a deadlock?

1. Interchanging Wait(F) and Wait(S) in the Producer process
2. Interchanging Signal(S) and Signal(F) in the Consumer process
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: (1) Producer may hold S while blocked on Wait(F) with a full buffer, and the consumer then blocks on Wait(S): deadlock. (2) Swapping the two Signals only changes release order, no circular wait.
questions.reviewNote: Problem statement prints 'S, F, and F' and the empty-buffer semaphore as 'E' (blurred); read as S, F, E.

The paging method for memory management uses two-level paging, and its storage overhead is P. The storage overhead for the segmentation method is S. The storage overhead for the segmentation and paging method is T. What is the relation among the overheads for the different methods of memory management in the concurrent execution of the above four processes?
questions.subject: os
questions.solution: Segmentation only needs 20 segment-table entries (smallest overhead); paging needs page tables for ~858 pages plus outer tables; segmentation with paging needs segment tables and per-segment page tables (largest).
questions.reviewNote: The symbol S is used for both the entry size and the segmentation overhead in the paper; question is a qualitative comparison. Answer agrees with published key.

questions.text: A software program consists of two modules M1 and M2 that can fail independently, but never simultaneously. The program is considered to have failed if any of these modules fails. Both the modules are 'repairable' and so the program starts working again as soon as the repair is done. Assume that the mean time to failure (MTTF) of M1 is T1 with a mean time to repair (MTTR) of R1. The MTTF of M2 is T2 with an MTTR of R2. What is the availability of the overall program given that the failure and repair times are all exponentially distributed random variables?
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: 3-state chain (up, M1 down, M2 down): P(down1)=P(up)R1/T1, P(down2)=P(up)R2/T2, so availability = 1/(1+R1/T1+R2/T2) = T1T2/(T1T2+T2R1+T1R2).
questions.reviewNote: Option denominators are blurred in the scan; reading of options C and D as above (D matches derived formula).

questions.text: Suppose that it takes 1 unit of time to transmit a packet (of fixed size) on a communication link. The link layer uses a window flow control protocol with a window size of N packets. Each packet causes an ack or a nak to be generated by the receiver, and ack/nak transmission times are negligible. Further, the round trip time on the link is equal to N units. Consider time $i > N$. If only acks have been received till time i (no naks), then the goodput evaluated at the transmitter at time i (in packets per unit time) is
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: By time i the sender has sent i packets but only i-N acks can have returned: goodput = (i-N)/i = 1 - N/i.
questions.reviewNote: Option D exponent sign is unreadable in the scan; assumed 1 - e^{-(i/N)}.

The values of $S_1$ and $S_2$ are, respectively,
questions.subject: cn

A pipelined processor uses a 4-stage instruction pipeline with the following stages: Instruction fetch (IF), Instruction decode (ID), Execute (EX) and Write back (WB). The arithmetic operations as well as the load and store operations are carried out in the EX stage. The sequence of instructions corresponding to the statement X = (S - R * (P + Q))/T is given below. The values of variables P, Q, R, S and T are available in the registers R0, R1, R2, R3 and R4 respectively, before the execution of the instruction sequence.

```
ADD   R5, R0, R1   ; R5 <- R0 + R1
MUL   R6, R2, R5   ; R6 <- R2 * R5
SUB   R5, R3, R6   ; R5 <- R3 - R6
DIV   R6, R5, R4   ; R6 <- R5 / R4
STORE R6, X        ; X <- R6
```

The IF, ID and WB stages take 1 clock cycle each. The EX stage takes 1 clock cycle each for the ADD, SUB and STORE operations, and 3 clock cycles each for MUL and DIV operations. Operand forwarding from the EX stage to the ID stage is used. The number of clock cycles required to complete the sequence of instructions is
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: With EX->ID forwarding a dependent instruction can decode in the last EX cycle of its producer: ADD ID2 EX3; MUL ID3 EX4-6; SUB ID6 EX7; DIV ID7 EX8-10; STORE ID10 EX11 WB12 = 12 cycles.
questions.reviewNote: Depends on the timing convention for EX->ID forwarding; 12 agrees with the published key (gateoverflow 3623).

questions.text:
Let L be a regular language. Consider the constructions on L below:

(I) $repeat(L) = \{ww \mid w \in L\}$

(II) $prefix(L) = \{u \mid \exists v : uv \in L\}$

(III) $suffix(L) = \{v \mid \exists u : uv \in L\}$

(IV) $half(L) = \{u \mid \exists v : |v| = |u| \text{ and } uv \in L\}$

Which of the constructions could lead to a non-regular language?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: prefix and suffix preserve regularity; repeat and half can produce non-regular languages (e.g. repeat((a+b)*) = {ww}).

questions.text:
Let L be a regular language. Consider the constructions on L below:

(I) $repeat(L) = \{ww \mid w \in L\}$

(II) $prefix(L) = \{u \mid \exists v : uv \in L\}$

(III) $suffix(L) = \{v \mid \exists u : uv \in L\}$

(IV) $half(L) = \{u \mid \exists v : |v| = |u| \text{ and } uv \in L\}$

Which choice of L is best suited to support your answer above?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: For L=(a+b)*, repeat(L)={ww | w in {a,b}*} is not regular; L must be regular, which rules out {a^n b^n}, and finite L or (ab)* give regular results.

Phase P4 cannot commence until both P2 and P3 are completed. The optimistic, most likely, and pessimistic estimates of the phase completion times in days, for P1, P2, P3 and P4 are, respectively, (11, 15, 25), (7, 8, 15), (8, 9, 22), and (3, 8, 19).

The critical path for the above project and the slack of P2 are, respectively,
questions.subject: legacy

questions.text: Let A be the matrix $\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix}$. What is the maximum value of $x^TAx$ where the maximum is taken over all $x$ that are the unit eigenvectors of A?

questions.solution: For a unit eigenvector, $x^TAx=\lambda$. Characteristic equation $\lambda^2-5\lambda+5=0$ gives $\lambda=(5\pm\sqrt5)/2$; max is $(5+\sqrt5)/2$.

questions.text: Consider a weighted undirected graph with positive edge weights and let uv be an edge in the graph. It is known that the shortest path from the source vertex s to u has weight 53 and the shortest path from s to v has weight 65. Which one of the following statements is always true?

questions.solution: Triangle inequality on shortest distances: d(s,v) ≤ d(s,u) + w(u,v), so w(u,v) ≥ 65 − 53 = 12.

questions.subject: cn

A partial order P is defined on the set of natural numbers as follows. Here x/y denotes integer division.

questions.text: A depth-first search is performed on a directed acyclic graph. Which of the following statements is always true for all edges (u, v) in the graph?
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: In a DAG there are no back edges, so for every edge (u,v) the call on v finishes before the call on u: f[u] > f[v].

questions.text: What is the largest integer m such that every simple connected graph with n vertices and n edges contains at least m different spanning trees?

questions.text: Consider n jobs $J_1, J_2, \ldots, J_n$ such that job $J_i$ has execution time $t_i$ and a non-negative integer weight $w_i$. The weighted mean completion time of the jobs is defined to be $\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_iT_i}{\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i}$, where $T_i$ is the completion time of job $J_i$. Assuming that there is only one processor available, in what order must the jobs be executed in order to minimize the weighted mean completion time of the jobs?
questions.subject: algo
questions.solution: Exchange argument (Smith's rule): swapping adjacent jobs i,j lowers cost iff $w_i/t_i > w_j/t_j$, so schedule by non-increasing $w_i/t_i$.

which of the following memory blocks will not be in the cache at the end of the sequence?

questions.solution: Final cache (block mod 8): slot0=24, slot1=17, slot2=82, slot3=3, slot4=20, slot5=5, slot6=30, slot7=63. Block 18 was evicted from slot 2 by 2 and then 82.

questions.text:
The following expression was to be realized using 2-input AND and OR gates. However, during the fabrication all 2-input AND gates were mistakenly substituted by 2-input NAND gates.

$(a\cdot b)\cdot c + (\bar a\cdot c)\cdot d + (b\cdot c)\cdot d + a\cdot d$

What is the function finally realized?
questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Each product becomes: NAND(NAND(a,b),c) = ab + c̄; NAND(NAND(ā,c),d) = āc + d̄; NAND(NAND(b,c),d) = bc + d̄; NAND(a,d) = ā + d̄. ORing all: ā + b + c̄ + d̄.

questions.text:
Data forwarding techniques can be used to speed up the operation in presence of data dependencies. Consider the following replacements of LHS with RHS.
(i) R1 → Loc, Loc → R2 ≡ R1 → R2, R1 → Loc
(ii) R1 → Loc, Loc → R2 ≡ R1 → R2
(iii) R1 → Loc, R2 → Loc ≡ R1 → Loc
(iv) R1 → Loc, R2 → Loc ≡ R2 → Loc

In which of the following options, will the result of executing the RHS be the same as executing the LHS irrespective of the instructions that follow?
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: (i) keeps the store to Loc so memory state is identical. (ii) drops the store to Loc and later reads of Loc differ. (iii) leaves Loc = R1 instead of R2. (iv) the first store is overwritten anyway.

questions.text: What is the final value stored in the linear feedback shift register if the input is 101101?

figures.alt: Four-cell shift register initially 0 1 1 0; the last (rightmost) cell output is fed back to one input of an XOR gate whose other input is the serial input 101101; the XOR output feeds the first cell.

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: Register starts 0110; each clock new first bit = input XOR last bit, then shift right. States after 6 inputs: 1011, 1101, 0110, 1011, 1101, 0110, so the final value is 0110.
questions.reviewNote: Initial register contents (0110) are blurry in the scan; the input 101101 is a palindrome so bit order does not matter.

questions.text:
Following table indicates the latencies of operations between the instruction producing the result and instruction using the result.

| Instruction producing the result | Instruction using the result | Latency |
|---|---|---|
| ALU Operation | ALU Operation | 2 |
| ALU Operation | Store | 2 |
| Load | ALU Operation | 1 |
| Load | Store | 0 |

Consider the following code segment.

```
Load R1, Loc1        ; Load R1 from memory location Loc1
Load R2, Loc2        ; Load R2 from memory location Loc2
Add  R1, R2, R1      ; Add R1 and R2 and save result in R1
Dec  R2              ; Decrement R2
Dec  R1              ; Decrement R1
Mpy  R1, R2, R3      ; Multiply R1 and R2 and save result in R3
Store R3, Loc3       ; Store R3 in memory location Loc3
```

What is the number of cycles needed to execute the above code segment assuming each instruction takes one cycle to execute?

figures.alt: Latency table: ALU->ALU 2, ALU->Store 2, Load->ALU 1, Load->Store 0.

questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: 7 instructions plus stall cycles: Add after Load R2 needs 1; Dec R1 after Add needs 2-1 (one instruction in between) = 1; Mpy after Dec R1 needs 2; Store after Mpy needs 2. Total 7+1+1+2+2 = 13.
questions.reviewNote: Stall counting convention (latency = idle cycles, in-order issue) assumed; matches the standard key 13.

questions.subject: dl
questions.reviewNote: Subscript bases are blurry in the scan (H, B, and octal answer base read from context).

questions.text: An error correcting code has the following code words: 00000000, 00001111, 01010101, 10101010, 11110000. What is the maximum number of bit errors that can be corrected?
questions.subject: cn
questions.solution: Minimum Hamming distance between code words is 4, so up to floor((4-1)/2) = 1 bit error can be corrected.

questions.text:
A hard disk system has the following parameters:
Number of tracks = 500
Number of sectors/track = 100
Number of bytes/sector = 500
Time taken by the head to move from one track to adjacent track = 1 ms
Rotation speed = 600 rpm.

What is the average time taken for transferring 250 bytes from the disk?
questions.subject: coa
questions.solution: Average seek = 250 tracks x 1 ms = 250 ms; average rotational latency = half of 100 ms = 50 ms; transfer of 250 bytes = half a sector = 0.5 ms (a sector passes in 1 ms). Total 300.5 ms.

questions.text:
The line T in the following figure is permanently connected to the ground.

Which of the following inputs (X1 X2 X3 X4) will detect the fault?

figures.alt: A 3-input NAND gate (inputs X1, X2, X3) output goes to a 2-input OR gate together with X4; the OR output feeds a 2-input NOR gate whose other input is line T, the output of a 2-input AND gate with inputs X3 and X4; the NOR output is the circuit output.

questions.subject: dl
questions.solution: T (output of AND(X3,X4)) stuck at 0. To expose it T must be 1 (X3=X4=1), but then X4=1 already forces the OR output to 1, so the NOR output is 0 with or without the fault. The fault is undetectable.
questions.reviewNote: Wiring read from a blurry scan (NAND inputs X1,X2,X3; AND inputs X3,X4).

questions.text:
The two grammars given below generate a language over the alphabet {x, y, z}.

G1: S → x | z | xS | zS | yB
    B → y | z | yB | zB

G2: S → y | z | yS | zS | xB
    B → y | yS

Which one of the following choices describes the properties satisfied by the strings in these languages?

options.t:
G1: No y appears before any x
G2: Every x is followed by at least one y

G1: No y appears before any x
G2: No x appears before any y

G1: No y appears after any x
G2: Every x is followed by at least one y

G1: No y appears after any x
G2: Every y is followed by at least one x

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: G1: only x/z can be generated before the first y, after that only y/z, so no x after any y. G2: every x is introduced by S→xB and B always begins with y.

questions.text:
Consider the following DFA in which s0 is the start state and s1, s3 are the final states.

What language does this DFA recognize?

options.t: All strings of x and y
All strings of x and y which have either even number of x and even number of y or odd number of x and odd number of y
All strings of x and y which have equal number of x and y
All strings of x and y with either even number of x and odd number of y or odd number of x and even number of y

figures.alt: Four states s0 (start), s1 (final), s2, s3 (final) placed in a diamond. Transitions: s0<->s1 on x; s1<->s2 on y; s2<->s3 on x; s3<->s0 on y (each edge drawn in both directions).

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: x toggles s0<->s1 and s2<->s3, y toggles s0<->s3 and s1<->s2, so the state records parities: s0 (even,even), s1 (odd x, even y), s2 (odd,odd), s3 (even x, odd y). Final states s1,s3 = exactly one parity odd.

questions.text:
Consider the grammar given below.

S → xB | yA
A → x | xS | yAA
B → y | yS | yBB

Consider the following strings.
(i) xxyyx
(ii) xxyyxy
(iii) xyxy
(iv) yxxy
(v) yxx
(vi) xyx

Which of the above strings are generated by the grammar?
questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: A generates strings with one more x than y, B one more y than x, so S generates non-empty strings with equal numbers of x and y (and every such string derivable): (ii), (iii), (iv) qualify; (i), (v), (vi) are unbalanced.
questions.reviewNote: The scan prints the last rule as B → y | yS | yBB (the original GATE paper has xBB). Taken literally only (iii) and (iv) are generated and no option matches; with the intended xBB rule the grammar generates the non-empty strings with equal x and y, giving (ii),(iii),(iv): option C.

questions.text:
Consider the following grammars. Names representing terminals have been specified in capital letters.

G1: stmnt → WHILE (expr) stmnt
    stmnt → OTHER
    expr → ID

G2: stmnt → WHILE (expr) stmnt
    stmnt → OTHER
    expr → expr + expr
    expr → expr * expr
    expr → ID

Which one of the following statements is true?

options.t: G1 is context-free but not regular and G2 is regular
G2 is context-free but not regular and G1 is regular
Both G1 and G2 are regular
Both G1 and G2 are context-free but neither of them is regular

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: G1 generates (WHILE ( ID ))* OTHER. In G2 expr only generates ID((+|*)ID)*, a regular set, so the language is (WHILE ( expr ))* OTHER: regular too.
questions.reviewNote: Parentheses in 'WHILE (expr)' treated as literal terminal symbols; answer C per standard key.

questions.text:
Consider the following finite automata P and Q over the alphabet {a, b, c}. The start states are indicated by a double arrow and final states are indicated by a double circle. Let the languages recognized by them be denoted by L(P) and L(Q) respectively.

The automaton which recognizes the language L(P) ∩ L(Q) is

figures.alt: Two 4-state automata P (states p0..p3) and Q (q0..q3) over {a,b,c}, all states drawn as double circles; edges are too blurry to read reliably in the scan.
Four states r0..r3 (all double circles): r0-a->r1, r1-b->r2, r2-a->r1, r2-c->r3, r0-b->r2 (long arc), r0 to r3 via a top arc a; bottom arc labelled b.
Four states r0..r3, r0-a->r1, r1-b->r2, r2-a->r1, r2-c->r3, arcs labelled b over the top r0->r2 and b along the bottom r1->r3.
Four states r0..r3 with a-edge r0->r1, b/a between r1 and r2, b/c between r2 and r3, arcs on top labelled a and bottom labelled a.
Four states r0..r3 with a r0->r1, b/a between r1 and r2, b/c between r2 and r3, top arc c from r2 to r0 and bottom arc b.

questions.subject: toc
questions.solution: Product-automaton construction: strings must satisfy both automata's constraints on reaching 'c'; only option A accepts all strings accepted by both P and Q (e.g. 'aa') while B, C and D reject them.
questions.reviewNote: The automata are illegible in the low-resolution scan (edge labels unreadable). Answer A taken from the gateoverflow accepted answer.

questions.text:
Given the following algorithm for sorting an array X of N numbers:

```
SUBROUTINE SORT(X, N)
    IF (N < 2)
        RETURN
    FOR (i = 2 TO N INCREMENT BY 1)
        FOR (j = 1 TO i INCREMENT BY 1)
            IF (X[i] > X[j])
                CONTINUE
            TEMP = X[i]
            X[i] = X[j]
            X[j] = TEMP
        END FOR
    END FOR
END SUBROUTINE
```

A good approximation of Halstead's estimated program length is
questions.subject: legacy
questions.solution: Halstead length N^ = n1 log2 n1 + n2 log2 n2 with about 7 distinct operands (X, N, i, j, TEMP, 1, 2) and about 15 distinct operators: 15*3.9 + 7*2.8 ≈ 78, i.e. ~80.
questions.reviewNote: Operator/operand count is judgement-based; the code is also slightly garbled in the scan (e.g. 'TEMP = X[i]'). 80 is the nearest option.

questions.text:
In the simplified flowchart given below, the shaded boxes represent code that is executed during a test case.

The branch coverage is

figures.alt: Flowchart: entry box, then a decision with left branch (executed) and right branch (not executed); left branch leads to a decision whose left box is not executed and right box is executed; right branch leads to a decision whose two boxes are both not executed; both sides join, then a decision at the bottom with left box not executed and right box executed, then exit.

questions.solution: The flowchart has 4 decisions = 8 branches. Executed branches: top decision left branch (1), second-level left decision right branch (1), the right-hand decision none, final decision right branch (1): 3 of 8.
